referee.who_is_on_other_side: Five counterparties, all of whom rationally want the trade. (1) WHOLESALERS AND HFT MARKET MAKERS (Citadel Securities, Virtu, Jane Street, Susquehanna). They are not taking a view — they collect the spread you cross, they see the full auction imbalance feed, they are flat within seconds, and they set the price at which you are allowed to fade. Your "edge" is their revenue line. (2) GENUINELY INFORMED INSTITUTIONS trading the actual news. They take the other side because the news is real and, per Chan (2003) and PEAD, the move continues. This is the adverse-selection core: you are most likely to get filled shorting an "excessive" gap precisely when more real information is coming. Your fills are conditionally toxic. (3) MECHANICAL PASSIVE/ETF FLOW at the open — price-insensitive, does not care about your residual. (4) OTHER RETAIL — and this inverts the strategy's founding premise. Ardia, Aymard & Cenesizoglu (2025, IRFA 105, 7.5M hourly observations) find Robinhood holders react to LAGGED overnight returns with an asymmetry: the number of RH investors rises MORE after extreme NEGATIVE overnight returns than positive ones, strongest immediately after. On gap-downs, retail is already buying the dip en masse. So the long leg of "fade the excess" is not fading retail — it is joining a crowded retail trade with a professional on the other side. (5) MID-FREQUENCY STAT-ARB FUNDS already running this exact signal with opening-auction access and microsecond hedging.
referee.frictions: Cost stack for one round trip, retail, hedged against a peer basket. VERIFIED ANCHORS: • Opening auction is structurally thin — Coalition Greenwich puts it at 1.25% of ADV vs 5.5% for the closing auction; SSGA's Table 2 shows US open 0.97% vs close 8.40%. • Price impact is WORSE at the open than at the close: the JFQA benchmark study (2,980 stocks, 2012-2021) finds the opening-auction impact slope significantly exceeds the closing-auction slope (θ₀ = 3.34 for micro-caps). For a 1%-ADV trade in CLOSING auctions: NYSE Micro 18.2 / Small 7.4 / Large 4.5 bps; Nasdaq Micro 44.7 / Small 12.5 / Large 10.2 bps. Continuous-market equivalents: NYSE Micro ~21.3, Nasdaq Micro ~15.6 bps. Opening auction is above all of these. • Elm Wealth's analysis of the overnight complex: trading just 1% of daily volume produces ~40 bps of round-trip price impact. • The pre-market data you need to compute "peer-implied fair value" is itself expensive: on Blue Ocean ATS (~83% of overnight volume, $374.7bn notional in 2025), the median spread across the 50 most-traded names on the 22 Jun 2026 session was ~15 bps; academic work (Lim, SSRN) finds overnight effective spreads average 7 cents/share HIGHER and 10-second price impact 2.4 cents/share higher than NASDAQ regular hours. Your signal inputs are noisier than the alpha. • Commissions: IBKR fixed $0.005/share, $1 order minimum, capped at 1% of trade value ≈ 1 bp/side on a $50 stock, so ~2 bps round trip single-name, ~8-12 bps once you add 4-5 peer-hedge legs. Zero-commission brokers substitute worse fills — Wharton PFOF research finds >75% of TD Ameritrade orders execute at midpoint or better vs only ~25% of Robinhood orders, using the SAME wholesalers. • Regulatory: SEC Section 31 fee $20.60 per $1M sold from 4 Apr 2026 = 0.21 bps sell-side only; FINRA TAF $0.000195/share (max $9.79/trade) from 1 Jan 2026 ≈ 0.004 bps on a $50 stock. Negligible. • Borrow: S&P Global classifies ≤35 bps as general collateral, 35-150 bps "warm," >150 bps "special"; IBKR cites ~30 bps for GC. One overnight day of GC = ~0.12 bps — negligible. But post-news names routinely sit in the "special" bucket; at 50%/yr that is ~20 bps for one day, ~60 bps across a weekend, and the binding problem is usually zero locate at 9:30 at a retail broker, not the rate. • Options route is worse, not better: Muravyev & Pearson (2020, RFS 33(11):4973) measure an 8.1-cent average quoted spread and 5.5-cent conventional effective spread on equity options, falling to 1.3-3.5 cents only for traders who algorithmically time execution against predictable quote moves. A retail trader pays the ~5.5-cent effective spread; on a $2.00 post-earnings option that is ~2.75% each way, ~5.5% round trip — and you are buying it into post-event IV crush. • Taxes: 100% short-term ordinary income. Federal 22-37% + 3.8% NIIT + state = roughly 30-42% all-in for a typical account, and without a trader-tax-status / mark-to-market election, net capital losses deduct against ordinary income at only $3,000/yr, with wash-sale rules on the long leg. ESTIMATE (not verified from a single study, flagged as my own): quoted spread at 9:30 in a name that just gapped on earnings runs ~15-40 bps for a liquid mid-cap and 50-150 bps for a small cap; crossing it on both the position and the peer hedge gives a realistic ALL-IN round trip of ~40-90 bps for a liquid mid-cap and 100-250 bps for a small cap, before tax.
referee.capacity: Capacity is not the binding constraint here — sign is — but for completeness. SMALL TRADER: to hold impact under ~5 bps you want roughly 0.1-0.25% of first-30-minute volume. A $3B mid-cap gapping on earnings might trade $30-80M in the first 30 minutes, so ~$60-160K per name. At 3-6 qualifying names/day that is ~$200K-$800K of daily gross notional and ~$50-200M/yr of turnover on ~$150-500K of deployed capital. At a hypothetical +10 bps net (which I do not believe exists) that is $50-200K/yr pre-tax; at a realistic -30 bps it is -$150K to -$600K/yr. SMALL FUND ($10-50M): moving $5M/day across 5 names is ~$1M/name, i.e. 1-3% of first-30-minute volume in a mid-cap. Per the JFQA slopes — where 1% of ADV already costs 12.5 bps in a Nasdaq small-cap CLOSING auction and the opening slope is materially steeper — you are paying 20-60+ bps of impact at the open on both legs. Dead on arrival. Elm Wealth's 40 bps round-trip impact at 1% of daily volume is the same conclusion from a different direction. Practical ceiling before impact eats the entire published gross edge: roughly $100-300K per name per event, $1-3M/day gross, i.e. under ~$5M of deployed capital — and that is the capacity of a trade whose expected sign I assess as negative.
referee.decay_evidence: Unusually strong and multi-sourced. (1) REAL MONEY TRIED AND FAILED: the NightShares 500 ETF (NSPY) and NightShares 2000 (NIWM) launched June 2022 explicitly to harvest the overnight effect; both stopped trading end-July 2023 and liquidated 10 Aug 2023. Since inception NSPY was -6.9% total return vs +22% for the S&P 500; NIWM was -10% vs +16% for the Russell 2000. (2) CENTRAL-BANK RESEARCH CONFIRMS DECAY: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics, "The Disappearing Overnight Drift" (July 2026) — the 2:00-3:00 a.m. ET window delivered ~3.7% p.a. over 1998-2020 (>60% of the E-mini's 5.9% close-to-close return) and has "averaged close to zero" from Jan 2021 to Dec 2025, following publication of the original research. Mechanism: the standard deviation of closing order imbalances compressed from 6.5% to 2.9%, with smaller limit orders posted at the close, consistent with algorithmic liquidity providers absorbing the inventory pressure that drove the effect. (3) PRACTITIONER ANALYSIS: Elm Wealth finds the overnight long-short generated ~38% annualized GROSS (1995-2022) but that 1 bp of round-trip market impact costs ~5%/yr, 1%/yr borrow costs ~1%/yr, and even at 1 bp per trade a trader "would not have made any money in the last 8 years"; they note the effect weakened over 2010-2022. (4) THE AUTHORS THEMSELVES DISCLAIM TRADABILITY: Glasserman, Krstovski, Laliberte & Mamaysky (arXiv 2507.04481) size the over-intra differential at 2.75 bps/day (~7.2%/yr) and write, "Because of the extreme turnover required to trade the over-intra effect, our findings fall short of being a viable trading strategy." (5) A COMMERCIAL SIGNAL VENDOR SAYS THE SHORT-HORIZON NEWS TRADE IS GONE: ExtractAlpha — "Over the last 10 years, simple news sentiment in the US has become really fast – if you're not acting on it within minutes, it's gone" — and they deliberately sell a 90-day-horizon transcripts signal "rather than the intraday response times that news sentiment products are built around," while acknowledging one of their price/volume signals "has become genuinely crowded and no longer performs as it once did." (6) GENERAL BASE RATE: post-publication anomaly returns run ~26% below in-sample and ~58% below out-of-sample-but-pre-publication. The US is specifically noted in the overnight-reversal literature as the one country with a reliable post-publication decline. (7) WHO ALREADY TRADES IT: mid-frequency statistical arbitrage desks with opening-auction access; Elm notes HFTs largely decline it because they prefer flat books overnight, which is precisely why the residual sits with funds that have infrastructure a retail trader does not.
referee.net_edge_estimate: My honest estimate: GROSS signal, if you could execute at the 9:30 print with zero delay, is plausibly 20-60 bps per event for the most extreme names — anchored on Stübinger & Endres's stated breakeven transaction cost of 35-40 bps round trip (S&P 500 universe, 1998-2015) and shrinking meaningfully out-of-sample given the decay evidence. REALISTIC retail all-in round-trip cost, hedged: 40-90 bps for a liquid mid-cap gapper, 100-250 bps for a small cap. PRE-TAX NET EXPECTANCY: approximately -30 to +5 bps per trade, centered clearly negative, with the distribution shifted further negative once you account for (a) execution delay — Della Corte et al. show a one-minute lag dramatically degrades the signal, and retail cannot participate in the auction cross on a signal computed from the auction print; and (b) the conditioning error — on the news subsample, Chan (2003) implies expected continuation, not reversal, so the sign of the gross term may itself be wrong. AFTER TAX (100% short-term, ~30-42% on gains, $3,000/yr loss deductibility without trader status), negative with high confidence. Two things I want to flag as genuinely UNKNOWABLE from public sources rather than pretend to have measured: the true gross alpha of a peer-residual overnight gap signal in 2024-2026 out-of-sample (no one has published it; the best paper stops in 2015), and the exact quoted spread distribution at 9:30 for news-gapping names (I could not retrieve a study that measures it; my 15-40 bps mid-cap / 50-150 bps small-cap figures are estimates, not citations). Neither uncertainty rescues the trade — the strategy needs the gross edge to be a LARGE multiple of costs to be worth the operational burden, and there is no evidence it is even a positive multiple. SANITY CHECK ON THE BULL CASE: Stübinger & Endres's companion pairs variant reports Sharpe 5.30 after costs. A genuine Sharpe 5.3 equity strategy would be traded to death within quarters; that number is a red flag for unmodelled frictions (frictionless entry at the opening print, no borrow constraint, no locate, no capacity limit), and their headline result is heavily concentrated in 2007-2009 (315% p.a. in that subperiod vs 64% in 1998-2006). Nagel (2012, RFS 25(7):2005-2039) explains why: short-term reversal returns are compensation for LIQUIDITY PROVISION, and expected returns and conditional Sharpes spike with VIX during turmoil. That reframes the whole trade correctly — this is not "fading dumb retail," it is selling liquidity into news, an inventory business with negatively skewed payoffs that pays most exactly when it is most likely to blow you up, run by someone with no balance sheet, no hedge, and no ability to say no to a fill.
referee.barriers: (1) CIRCULARITY — the fatal one. The signal is defined on the opening print and must be executed at that same print. Della Corte/Kosowski/Wang tested execution at 9:30:01 through 9:45 and found sharp degradation within one minute. Retail cannot submit an order into the opening cross that is conditioned on the cross price. You either commit MOO/LOO orders before the auction using stale, wide pre-market peer quotes, or you trade after the print into a market the pros have already adjusted. (2) SIGNAL-INPUT NOISE EXCEEDS SIGNAL. "Peer-implied fair value" requires clean pre-market peer prices. Blue Ocean's median spread on its 50 MOST-traded names was ~15 bps, with effective spreads 7 cents/share wider and 10-second price impact 2.4 cents/share higher than NASDAQ regular hours. Your regressor set is measured with more error than the residual you are trying to trade. (3) LOCATE AND SHORTABILITY. Post-news names are frequently "special" (>150 bps/yr per S&P Global's classification) or simply unavailable at retail brokers at 9:30. (4) REG SHO RULE 201. If the name fell 10%+ (triggering the short-sale circuit breaker), short sales must be priced above the national best bid for the remainder of that day AND the following day — you cannot hit the bid on the short leg. (5) EXECUTION QUALITY BY BROKER. Same wholesalers, wildly different outcomes: >75% of TD Ameritrade orders at midpoint or better vs ~25% for Robinhood. On a strategy with a sub-50 bps edge, broker choice alone flips the sign. (6) PDT — NOW A RECEDING BARRIER, WHICH IS BAD NEWS. FINRA Regulatory Notice 26-10 eliminates the pattern-day-trader designation and the $25,000 minimum equity requirement entirely, effective 4 June 2026, replaced by an intraday-margin-deficit standard (with a 90-day trading freeze for a pattern of unmet deficits), phase-in through 20 Oct 2027. So the capital gate this brief assumed is gone or going. That does not create edge — it lets more retail capital compete for the same shrinking residual at the open. (7) TAX. All short-term; losses capped at $3,000/yr against ordinary income without trader status; wash sales on the long leg. (8) BASE RATE ON THE OPERATOR. Barber, Lee, Liu & Odean's full Taiwan population (1992-2006): under 1% of day traders were consistently profitable, ~3% net positive after fees, with average losses of 23.9 bps/day net; survival 44%/24%/15% at one/two/three years. In Brazil, 97% of those who persisted beyond 300 trading days lost money.
referee.confidence: HIGH that no exploitable net-of-cost edge exists for a small trader or small fund, for three converging reasons that do not depend on each other: the strategy conditions on the news subsample where the published evidence says continuation (Chan 2003, PEAD) rather than reversal; the execution is provably non-implementable at retail latency (Della Corte et al.'s one-minute decay, plus the signal/execution circularity); and the best published gross edge (35-40 bps breakeven, S&P 500, 1998-2015) is at or below a realistic retail round-trip cost at the open before tax. Real money has already tested the broader thesis and lost — NightShares closed in 14 months with NSPY at -6.9% against a +22% index — and the NY Fed documents the flagship overnight anomaly going to zero post-2021. MEDIUM on the specific basis-point figures. I could not retrieve several primary tables despite repeated attempts: the Berkman et al. decile-level overnight/intraday bps (Cambridge and CORE PDFs returned 403/abstract-only), the Della Corte execution-delay table at 9:30:01/9:31/9:35/9:45 (three PDF sources returned unparseable binary), the Lou-Polk-Skouras magnitudes (PDF unparseable), and the Federal Reserve FEDS 2024-080 and Wharton PFOF retail round-trip cost experiments (both PDFs unparseable). My 15-40 bps mid-cap / 50-150 bps small-cap opening spread figures are my own estimates, NOT citations — I found no study measuring the 9:30 quoted spread distribution for news-gapping names, and one search-summary claim I saw (S&P 500 spreads ">20 bps at the open falling to <5 bps in the last half hour") I could NOT verify against the SSGA source it was attributed to, so I have not relied on it. The gap-fill-by-size statistics (76% overall, 9.6% for gaps beyond ±5%) come from a retail blog and should be treated as directional only. These gaps affect the precision of the loss estimate, not the sign. Consistent with the analyst's FTD finding: the naive version of the pattern has no exploitable content, and what survives in the literature survives only under conditions — instantaneous auction execution, institutional cost structures, and the no-news subsample — that a retail implementation of this specific strategy explicitly violates.

execution.topic: Shorting hard-to-borrow US small/micro-cap equities: locate mechanics, borrow-fee accounting, and carry risk at retail/prime brokers (2025-26)

practices.practice: Price the borrow off the marked-up COLLATERAL, never off market value
practices.detail: IBKR's daily borrow fee is (Collateral Value x Fee Rate) / 360, where Collateral = prior day's settlement price x 102%, ROUNDED UP TO THE NEAREST $1.00 for USD/CAD names (EUR/CHF/GBP/SEK/AUD round up to $0.01 at 105%). On sub-$5 stocks the whole-dollar rounding is the dominant cost term, not the quoted rate. Build a `true_rate = quoted_rate * ceil(px*1.02)/px * 365/360` column in your screener and rank candidates on that, not on the headline fee.

practices.practice: Size against FINRA Rule 4210, not against notional
practices.detail: Short positions under $5/share require the GREATER of $2.50/share or 100% of market value; at $5+ it is the greater of $5.00/share or 30% of market value. A $0.95 name (CGC, Aug 2026) consumes $2.50/share of equity — $100k of equity supports only ~$38k of short notional (0.38x). The same $100k supports $180k notional in a $9 stock. Sub-$1 shorts are the single worst use of margin capital in the US equity book.

practices.practice: Treat the SLB quote as an indication, not a fill
practices.detail: IBKR states explicitly that SLB Availability rates are 'indicative' — the rates at which lenders are willing to transact today — and that rates may change, sometimes significantly, before the borrow is struck and settled. Fee rates are applied to SETTLED positions, so under T+1 the rate you actually pay on day one is set after you are already committed. Never build a carry model on the screen quote.

practices.practice: Poll the IBKR public short-stock feed on a schedule and store it
practices.detail: ftp3.interactivebrokers.com, username `shortstock`, blank password, file `usa.txt`. Pipe-delimited: SYM|CUR|NAME|CON|ISIN|REBATERATE|FEERATE|AVAILABLE. Snapshot it every 15-30 min into a time series. Available-share count collapsing toward zero is the leading indicator of a fee spike and of recall risk; the FEERATE print is the lagging one. This is the cheapest real borrow-tape a small fund can get. (Note: FTP is often blocked by corporate/cloud egress — run the poller somewhere with outbound FTP, or use the Client Portal SLB search / TWS 'Shortable Shares' and 'Fee Rate' columns as fallback.)

practices.practice: Use pre-borrow only for planned, multi-day, event-dated shorts — and inside the window
practices.detail: IBKR pre-borrow orders are accepted 06:45-14:45 ET, MARKET ORDERS ONLY, $10,000 minimum, with most activity 09:00-11:00 ET. Borrow cost begins accruing the day the pre-borrow executes, plus a per-executed-pre-borrow fee (reported at $20 in IBKR's pre-borrow webinar materials). If no short sale executes within three days, it becomes a 'non-purpose borrow' and the shares are returned. Pre-borrow converts fee uncertainty into a known cost — pay it only when the thesis has a date on it.

practices.practice: Reconcile the actual charged borrow against your model daily, per position
practices.detail: Pull the IBKR activity statement 'Borrow Fee Details' / 'Non-Direct Hard to Borrow Details' section, which reports Value (post-102%-markup, post-rounding), Fee Rate, and the /360 accrual. Diff realized vs. modeled every morning. A short book that only reconciles at month-end discovers its carry blowout roughly 20 trading days too late.

practices.practice: Split execution and locate across brokers deliberately
practices.detail: IBKR: cheapest ETB carry, deepest institutional inventory, no per-share locate fee, but weakest on genuinely HTB micro-caps and it will buy you in without notice. Cobra Trading: locate monitor inside Sterling Trader Pro and DAS Trader Pro, plus a desk reachable by Symphony IM or live chat; locates typically 1-5 cents/share and Cobra markets no overnight multiplier on locate fees. CenterPoint: DAS-integrated Short Locate Tool available 04:00-20:00 ET, HTB list of 8,000+ names, in-house locate desk. Route ETB carry to IBKR and HTB event shorts to a locate-first broker.

practices.practice: Locate cost is sunk at acceptance — pre-commit before you click
practices.detail: CenterPoint charges the locate fee when you ACCEPT the locate, regardless of whether you execute a trade; fees are deducted the following day and appear as 'Locate fees' in Account Activity. Locates are generally non-refundable across the retail HTB brokers. Decide the size and the trigger before requesting, and never over-request 'just in case' on a $0.30/share locate.

practices.practice: Instrument the Rule 201 short-sale-restriction state in your OMS
practices.detail: A 10% decline from the prior day's close arms the Rule 201 circuit breaker; for the remainder of that day AND the following day you may not execute or display a short at or below the national best bid. That is precisely the condition on the day your short thesis is working. Entries must flip to bid-side limit or displayed-above-NBB logic; a market sell-short will be rejected or reduced. Tag every fill with SSR state so your slippage attribution is honest.

practices.practice: Model the borrow as a stochastic, thesis-correlated cost, not a constant
practices.detail: Run the carry as a distribution, not a point estimate. Minimum stress: hold the quoted rate at 3x and 10x entry for the holding period, and simultaneously mark the collateral basis up to ceil(stress_px*1.02). If the trade still clears your hurdle, it is a real trade. If it only works at the entry-day fee, it is a fee-rate short, not an equity short.

practices.practice: Prefer defined-risk expressions when the borrow is above roughly 30-40% true rate
practices.detail: Listed puts embed the borrow in the put price via put-call parity, but they cap the loss and eliminate recall/buy-in entirely. On a $2-$5 name with listed options and a dated catalyst, compare the put debit against (true_rate x notional x holding_days/365) plus a recall-probability haircut. Above ~30-40% true annualized, the option frequently wins on risk-adjusted terms even when it loses on raw expected cost.

practices.practice: Refresh your tradable universe quarterly — short-side tickers die and reverse-split
practices.detail: Of the five names commonly cited for this universe, two no longer fit: HYZN was suspended and delisted from Nasdaq effective January 30, 2025 ahead of a plan of dissolution (stockholders approved the asset transfer March 25, 2025), and SPCE executed a 1-for-20 reverse split effective June 14, 2024 and traded roughly $5-9 by mid-2026. Reverse splits and dissolutions silently invalidate backtests and screens built on stale symbol lists.

pitfalls.pitfall: THE CORE KILLER: in a squeeze, the fee rate and the collateral basis spike together, multiplying the carry while you are already losing on price
pitfalls.mitigation: Work the BYND arithmetic before sizing anything. Oct 16-21, 2025, BYND ran $0.52 to $4.44 (+515%; sources cite up to +596% intraday over the window). Pre-squeeze at $0.52 with a 20% fee, collateral rounds to $1.00 and daily carry is $0.00056/share. At $4.44 with the fee at 200%, collateral rounds to $5.00 and daily carry is $0.02778/share — a 50x increase in daily carry stacked on top of a 754% mark-to-market loss. Quotes as high as 905.33% were printed around Oct 15, 2025 (some of those prints were non-US venues — treat the exact number as indicative); the rate had normalized to 20.07% by Oct 22. Carry is not an independent cost line; it is levered to the same tail that kills the position. Model it as a product, not a sum.

pitfalls.pitfall: The whole-dollar collateral rounding cliff silently doubles carry on a 1-cent price move
pitfalls.mitigation: Cliffs sit where px x 1.02 crosses an integer: $0.9804, $1.9608, $2.9412, $3.9216, $4.9020. At $1.96 collateral is $2.00 (1.02x multiplier); at $1.97 it is $3.00 (1.52x). At $1.01 collateral is $2.00 — 1.98x market value, so a quoted 25% fee is a true ~50% annualized cost. Compute the multiplier at entry AND at your stop price; avoid initiating just above a cliff when the thesis implies upward drift into it.

pitfalls.pitfall: Recall and forced buy-in with no notice — the risk that is not in any backtest
pitfalls.mitigation: Lenders may recall at any time. IBKR's process: on recall it attempts to re-source; if it cannot replace within two days of the recall notice, the lender may issue a formal Buy-In Warning permitting a buy-in that day. IBKR's disclosures state it may buy you in WITHOUT notice and you are liable for all resulting losses, commissions and fees. Buy-ins execute into the exact tape you least want. Operationally: keep a standing GTC buy-limit ladder above the market so a forced cover has resting liquidity to hit, cap any single HTB name at a size you would accept being flattened at a 30% gap, and use the AVAILABLE column trend as your early warning.

pitfalls.pitfall: Reg SHO Rule 204 close-out under T+1 compresses the fail window to almost nothing
pitfalls.mitigation: Rule 204 requires the clearing participant to close out a fail-to-deliver by the beginning of regular trading hours on the settlement day following the settlement date. Under the T+1 cycle effective May 28, 2024, that is the T+2 open for an ordinary short sale — roughly one business day of slack, versus three under T+3. Separately, a name whose FTDs persist 13 consecutive settlement days becomes a threshold security with mandatory close-out. Screen the SEC/FINRA threshold list and your own broker's Reg SHO 204 notices daily; a threshold listing is a hard signal that borrow supply is failing and buy-in risk is live.

pitfalls.pitfall: Quoted borrow rates disagree wildly across vendors, so a screen built on one feed is systematically wrong
pitfalls.mitigation: On BYND in August 2026, Fintel-family sources and Short Interest Tracker showed ~22.60% while CurvedTrading showed 7.4% (Aug 10, 2026) with ~150-200K shares available — a 3x disagreement on the same name in the same week. Vendors sample different lenders at different times and refresh on different cycles (Fintel updates intraday, roughly every 30 minutes). Use the vendor feed for ranking and the broker's own SLB quote for pricing, and never trade a carry model against a vendor number alone.

pitfalls.pitfall: Estimated overnight borrow held back on trade date, actual not known until T+2 — your intraday P&L is a guess
pitfalls.mitigation: TradeZero, effective April 1, 2025, holds back an ESTIMATED overnight borrow fee from your balance on trade date; the actual rate is established on T+1 based on the 16:00 ET close and only charged on T+2, at which point the estimate is returned and the true amount deducted. Every night held is charged at that night's actual rate. Build a two-day accrual lag into your P&L reconciliation or you will chase phantom breaks for weeks.

pitfalls.pitfall: Locate fees quoted per-share look trivial and are not, especially with overnight multipliers
pitfalls.mitigation: On a $1.00 stock a $0.05/share locate is a 5% cost on day one — an ~1,800% annualized rate if held one day. Third-party reviews report CenterPoint locate fees ranging $0.01 to $1.00+/share on genuinely HTB names with a 3x multiplier for overnight holds (treat the 3x and the top of that range as reported-not-broker-published; confirm with the desk before sizing). Always convert the per-share locate to a percent of the SHARE PRICE, then annualize over the expected hold, and add it to the borrow rate before comparing candidates.

pitfalls.pitfall: Pre-borrowed shares across an ex-dividend date create a large unrelated liability
pitfalls.mitigation: IBKR warns that holding pre-borrowed shares at the close of business the day before an ex-dividend date can trigger a substantial payment obligation regardless of your trading position, and that borrow fees accrue on any pre-borrowed shares in EXCESS of your actual short position. Check the dividend calendar before pre-borrowing and never leave pre-borrow inventory unmatched to a short.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming 'shortable' on the screen means shortable at your size, at your price, tomorrow
pitfalls.mitigation: 'Shortable' is a snapshot of one broker's inventory at one instant with an indicative rate attached. It carries no commitment on quantity, no commitment on rate, and no commitment on tenure. Before any position over ~5% of the AVAILABLE count in usa.txt, call the desk (Cobra via Symphony IM or live chat; CenterPoint via the locate desk) and get size and rate confirmed verbally. Assume anything you did not confirm is not there.

pitfalls.pitfall: Reverse splits mid-short: mechanical position adjustment, re-struck borrow, and often a fresh squeeze
pitfalls.mitigation: SPCE's 1-for-20 in June 2024 is the template. On a reverse split the short is adjusted, the borrow is re-established at a new rate, the price crosses upward through several $1.00 collateral-rounding cliffs at once, and float compression frequently spikes the fee. Screen all HTB shorts for pending reverse-split proxies and Nasdaq/NYSE minimum-bid-price deficiency notices (a sub-$1 close for 30 consecutive business days starts the clock) — a deficiency notice on a name you are short is a reason to reduce, not to press.

pitfalls.pitfall: Off-exchange short volume ratios are misread as short interest
pitfalls.mitigation: BYND showed an off-exchange short volume ratio of 68.78% alongside 26.19% short interest as of Aug 11, 2026. Off-exchange 'short volume' is dominated by market-maker and internalizer hedging flow, not directional shorts, and it does not aggregate into short interest. Use bi-monthly FINRA/Nasdaq short interest and days-to-cover (BYND: 130,851,657 shares, 2.09 days) for positioning; use borrow rate and available-share count for supply. Never use daily short volume ratio as a squeeze signal.

pitfalls.pitfall: Form SHO / Rule 13f-2 compliance planning built on the wrong date
pitfalls.mitigation: Thresholds are a monthly average gross short position of $10 million or more in an equity security, or 2.5%+ of shares outstanding. The compliance date has moved repeatedly: after an extension to January 2026 (initial filings Feb 17, 2026), the SEC granted a further temporary exemption running January 2, 2026 to January 2, 2028, with first Form SHO reports due within 14 calendar days after the last day of January 2028. Do not build filing infrastructure on the 2026 date, but do start capturing the monthly average gross short data now — a small fund can cross the 2.5%-of-outstanding test in a micro-cap on a surprisingly modest dollar position.

concrete_specs: IBKR daily borrow fee formula: (Collateral Value x Fee Rate) / 360. Day-count is 360, so a quoted rate accrues over 365 calendar days — multiply quoted rate by 365/360 = 1.0139 for the true annual figure.
IBKR collateral markup, USD/CAD: prior day's settlement price x 102%, ROUNDED UP TO THE NEAREST $1.00, x shares. EUR/CHF/GBP/SEK/AUD: x105%, rounded up to nearest $0.01.
Collateral rounding cliffs (price where px x 1.02 crosses an integer): $0.9804, $1.9608, $2.9412, $3.9216, $4.9020. At $1.97 the multiplier is 1.52x; one cent lower at $1.96 it is 1.02x.

True-cost multipliers at Aug 2026 prices: CGC @ $0.95 -> collateral $1.00 = 1.053x; PLUG @ $2.33 -> collateral $3.00 = 1.288x; a $0.60 name -> collateral $1.00 = 1.667x; a $1.05 name -> collateral $2.00 = 1.905x.
Screener formula to implement: true_rate = quoted_fee_rate * (ceil(price * 1.02) / price) * (365/360). PLUG at 22.44% quoted and $2.33 = ~29.3% true annualized.
FINRA Rule 4210 short margin: under $5/share, the GREATER of $2.50/share or 100% of market value. At $5.00+/share, the GREATER of $5.00/share or 30% of market value.
IBKR public borrow feed endpoint: ftp://ftp3.interactivebrokers.com/usa.txt, username `shortstock`, blank password. Columns: SYM|CUR|NAME|CON|ISIN|REBATERATE|FEERATE|AVAILABLE.

IBKR in-platform sources: Client Portal > Get Help > Short Securities (SLB) Availability (shows quantity available, number of lenders, indicative borrow rate); in TWS add the 'Shortable Shares' and 'Fee Rate' columns to the watchlist.
IBKR pre-borrow order window: 06:45-14:45 ET. MARKET ORDERS ONLY. $10,000 minimum. Peak activity 09:00-11:00 ET.

IBKR pre-borrow 3-day rule: if no short sale executes within three days of the pre-borrow, it becomes a 'non-purpose borrow' and the shares are returned. Borrow cost accrues from the pre-borrow execution day.

IBKR recall-to-buy-in path: recall notice issued -> IBKR attempts to re-source -> if not replaced within TWO days of the recall notice, lender may issue a formal Buy-In Warning permitting buy-in that same day. IBKR's disclosures state it may buy in without notice to you and you bear all losses, commissions and fees.

Reg SHO Rule 204 close-out: by the beginning of regular trading hours on the settlement day following the settlement date. Under T+1 (effective May 28, 2024) that is the T+2 open for an ordinary short sale.
Reg SHO threshold security: fails-to-deliver persisting 13 consecutive settlement days triggers mandatory close-out. Screen the daily threshold lists.

Reg SHO Rule 201 (SSR): triggered by a 10% or greater decline from the prior day's close; short orders may not be executed or displayed at or below the national best bid for the remainder of that day AND the following trading day. Order-type consequence: use bid-side or above-NBB limit orders, not market sell-short.

CenterPoint Short Locate Tool: integrated in DAS Trader Pro, available 04:00-20:00 ET. Fee is charged when you ACCEPT the locate whether or not you trade; charges post the following day under 'Locate fees' in Account Activity.
Cobra Trading locate access: locate monitor built into Sterling Trader Pro and DAS Trader Pro; desk reachable via Symphony instant messenger or website live chat for names the monitor cannot fill.

TradeZero overnight borrow mechanics (effective April 1, 2025): estimated ONB fee held back from balance on TRADE DATE; actual rate established T+1 off the 16:00 ET close; estimate returned and actual charged on T+2. Each night held is charged at that night's actual rate.

Rule 13f-2 / Form SHO thresholds: monthly average gross short position of $10,000,000+ in a security, OR 2.5%+ of shares outstanding. Compliance temporarily exempted Jan 2, 2026 through Jan 2, 2028; first reports due within 14 calendar days after the last day of January 2028.

Dead/moved tickers to purge from short screens: HYZN suspended and delisted from Nasdaq effective Jan 30, 2025 (dissolution; asset transfer approved Mar 25, 2025). SPCE executed a 1-for-20 reverse split effective 17:00 ET June 14, 2024 and traded roughly $5-9 mid-2026 — no longer a sub-$5 name.

Stress-test rule to hard-code: reject any short-carry trade that does not clear its hurdle at 3x the entry borrow rate, and require an explicit sign-off at 10x. Re-mark the collateral basis to ceil(stress_price * 1.02) in the same test.
Position cap heuristic: no single HTB short above 5% of the AVAILABLE share count in the current usa.txt snapshot without verbal size-and-rate confirmation from the locate desk.

Unverified / confirm with the desk before relying on: CenterPoint per-share locate range of $0.01-$1.00+ and the 3x overnight multiplier (third-party broker reviews, not CenterPoint's published schedule); Cobra's typical 1-5 cents/share locates and 'no overnight multiplier' claim (broker's own marketing); the $20 per-executed-pre-borrow fee at IBKR (IBKR pre-borrow webinar materials, not the public pricing page — the pricing page returns 403 to automated fetch); Tradier's HTB locate capability could not be verified at all — assume no meaningful HTB inventory until proven otherwise.
costs: PLUG (Plug Power): borrow fee rate 22.44%, recently +4.45 percentage points (Fintel, Aug 2026). Price $2.33 on Aug 13, 2026 (day range $2.25-$2.42). True cost after 102%/round-up-to-$3.00 collateral and 365/360: ~29.3% annualized on market notional.

BYND (Beyond Meat), Aug 2026: quoted borrow 22.60% with ~200K shares available (Short Interest Tracker) versus 7.4% with ~150.0K available on Aug 10, 2026 (CurvedTrading) — a ~3x vendor disagreement in the same week. Short interest 130,851,657 shares = 26.19% of float, days-to-cover 2.09, off-exchange short volume ratio 68.78% (as of Aug 11, 2026).

BYND squeeze episode, Oct 2025: price ran $0.52 -> $4.44 between Oct 16 and Oct 21, 2025 (+515%; some sources cite +596% across the window). Borrow quotes as high as 905.33% around Oct 15, 2025 (partly non-US venues — treat as indicative), normalizing to 20.07% by Oct 22, 2025. Short interest into the move was 27,318,582 shares = 37.64% of float.

BYND carry compounding through that squeeze (IBKR collateral convention): at $0.52 with a 20% fee, collateral rounds to $1.00 -> $0.00056/share/day. At $4.44 with a 200% fee, collateral rounds to $5.00 -> $0.02778/share/day. That is a 50x increase in daily carry on top of the price loss. At the 905% print it is $0.12569/share/day, or 2.83% of market notional PER DAY.

CGC (Canopy Growth), Aug 2026: ~$0.95-$0.98 (close $0.95 on Aug 10, 2026), 52-week range $0.84-$2.37, down ~45% year-on-year. Short interest 22.62M shares = 5.36% of 422.07M shares outstanding. Current borrow rate not retrievable without a paid feed — Fintel/ORTEX borrow data is paywalled; the specific CGC rate is UNVERIFIED here.

Locate fees, retail HTB brokers: Cobra Trading reports typical locates of 1-5 cents/share with no overnight multiplier (broker's own statements). CenterPoint locates are reported by third-party reviews at $0.01 to $1.00+/share on hard names with a 3x overnight-hold multiplier; CenterPoint's own page publishes only a $0.05/share example ($50 on 1,000 shares). Convert to annualized before comparing: $0.05/share on a $1.00 stock held one night is a 5% one-day cost.

IBKR pre-borrow: reported $20 fee per executed pre-borrow plus borrow cost accruing from the execution day (IBKR pre-borrow webinar materials — the public Short Sale Cost pricing page blocks automated fetch, so treat the $20 as needing confirmation).

IBKR short-proceeds interest: accounts with NAV below USD 100,000 receive proportionally reduced interest on short sale proceeds, and short credit interest accrues on a 360-day basis. A sub-$100k account therefore gives up part of the rebate leg while paying the full borrow leg — the effective net carry on a small account is worse than the headline fee rate implies.

Day-count drag: the /360 convention on a rate quoted as annualized means the realized annual cost is quoted x 365/360 = 1.39% higher than the headline (e.g. 22.44% quoted -> 22.75% before the collateral markup).

execution.topic: Options execution on low-priced, high-IV small caps ($0.50–$5 US equities) for a short-biased / event-driven book

practices.practice: Check penny-vs-nickel class membership BEFORE you look at the chain — it is the single biggest determinant of your execution cost
practices.detail: Under the Penny Interval Program (permanent since 2020-07-01, replacing the Penny Pilot), classes IN the program quote at $0.01 below $3.00 premium and $0.05 at/above $3.00. Classes NOT in the program quote at $0.05 below $3.00 and $0.10 at/above $3.00. Download the authoritative list free: curl https://www.miaxglobal.com/sites/default/files/listings/PennyPilotClasses.csv (356 classes as of 2026-08-13; format "SYMBOL","Name"). Verified on 2026-08-13: PLUG, BYND, CGC, SPCE, NIO, RIOT, MARA, TLRY, LCID, RIVN, OPEN, BBAI, CLOV, WULF, HTZ, QS, EOSE, ASTS, RKLB, LUNR, JOBY, ACHR are PENNY. HYZN, CHPT, FCEL, NKLA, BLNK, WKHS, SNDL, ACB, MULN, IEP, WBA are NOT. SPY/QQQ/IWM are a separate carve-out: $0.01 at all premium levels. Cross-check the CSV against live quotes with a residue test — if every bid/ask in the chain is a multiple of $0.05, it is a nickel class.

practices.practice: Trade only the third-Friday monthly expiry in this universe; skip the weeklies entirely
practices.detail: Empirical, from Cboe delayed chains for PLUG/BYND/CGC/RIOT/CHPT/FCEL captured 2026-08-13 (n=1,164 series, 7–120 DTE): third-Friday monthlies had median quoted spread 20% of mid and median OI 86; non-monthly weeklies had median spread 32% of mid and median OI 5. Concretely, PLUG 2026-09-18 (36d) $2.50 put showed OI 7,112 and a $0.34/$0.42 market; the 2026-10-02 (50d) $2.50 put showed OI 0 and a $0.30/$0.55 market — same underlying, same moneyness, 3x the width. RIOT 2026-09-25 puts quoted $2.77/$3.15 (12.8% of mid) versus 2026-09-18 at $2.75/$2.86 (3.9%).

practices.practice: For nickel-increment classes, always trade a spread, never an outright — the complex order book gives you penny granularity the outright cannot have
practices.detail: Cboe Rule 5.33 / complex book: the minimum NET price increment for complex orders in any equity class (other than SPX/SPXW) is $0.01 regardless of ratio, and the execution price of any individual leg may be in $0.01 increments regardless of the minimum increment otherwise applicable to that series. So in FCEL or CHPT, where each leg only quotes in nickels, you can send a vertical at a net $1.73 or $1.78 — prices unreachable by legging. Worked example, FCEL 2026-09-18 (spot 20.47, nickel class): P20 $2.40/$2.70, P16 $0.70/$0.95. Legging at the touch pays a $2.00 debit; mid-to-mid is $1.725. Working the complex order between $1.73 and $1.85 recovers most of the $0.275 (=$27.50/contract) you would otherwise hand over.

practices.practice: Never send a market order, and never send a marketable limit at the far touch, in any name in this universe
practices.detail: Enter as a limit at mid, then walk in $0.01 steps every 30–60 seconds toward the offer, with a hard cap you set before you start (typically mid + 25–35% of the half-spread). At IBKR use SNAP MID — verified to support US stocks, options AND futures (unlike the MidPrice algo, which the TWS API docs state is 'Smart-routing to US stocks only'). SNAP MID computes buy price = midpoint − offset, offset must be in whole-penny increments; a $0.00 offset rests you at the mid and re-snaps when you amend. Route via IB SmartRouting so the order is exposed to the exchanges' price-improvement auctions (Cboe AIM, MIAX PRIME, BOX PIP, NYSE CUBE) rather than resting on one book.

practices.practice: Before entering, compute what decline the option is already priced for — in most of these names the market's own risk-neutral median is already sharply negative
practices.detail: Under lognormal with r=0, the risk-neutral MEDIAN return is exp(−0.5·σ²·T)−1. At the IVs actually observed on 2026-08-13: PLUG ~85–95%, RIOT ~85–89%, CGC ~57–80%, FCEL ~100–115%, BYND ~127–161%. Table of RN median decline: at 85% IV — −2.1% (21d), −3.5% (36d), −8.5% (90d), −30.3% (1y). At 95% IV — −2.6%/−4.4%/−10.5%/−36.3%. At 130% IV — −4.7%/−8.0%/−18.8%/−57.0%. At 160% IV — −7.1%/−11.9%/−27.1%/−72.2%. Equivalently P(S_T < S_0) is already 55.9% at 95% IV/36d and 65.4% at 160% IV/90d. Rule: write your thesis as a median % move over a stated horizon and compare it to the number in this table. If your thesis is 'PLUG drifts down 5% over the next month' and the 36d RN median is already −4.4%, you have essentially no directional edge and you are buying a coin flip while paying a 21%-of-premium spread.

practices.practice: For a slow-drift thesis, buy delta 0.35–0.55 puts, not 0.10–0.20 puts
practices.detail: Two reasons, both measurable. (1) Payoff: a slow grind never reaches a far-OTM strike; you need the stock to travel to the strike AND past it by the premium. (2) Execution: median quoted spread by delta bucket for puts in penny names (2026-08-13 snapshot) was 50% of mid at |delta| 0.05–0.15, 17% at 0.15–0.25, 10% at 0.25–0.35, 17% at 0.35–0.45, 18% at 0.45–0.60. The cheap-looking wing is where the market maker takes half your premium on entry. RIOT 2026-09-18 illustrates the cliff: |delta| 0.52 → 3.9% wide, 0.45 → 4.1%, 0.30 → 4.9%, 0.23 → 3.5%, then 0.17 → 12.0% and 0.12 → 19.7%.

practices.practice: Pick tenor 45–90 DTE and exit/roll at 21 DTE; do not hold a long put into the last three weeks
practices.detail: 45–90 DTE gives your drift thesis time to beat the RN median while keeping theta manageable and keeping you in a monthly expiry with real OI. Exiting at 21 DTE avoids the gamma/pin zone, avoids the assignment window on any short leg, and gets you out while the series is still the front monthly with the tightest market. In this universe the practical constraint binds first: for most of these names only 3–6 monthly expiries carry OI above 500 at all, so 'choose a tenor' usually means choosing between two live months.

practices.practice: Extract the implied borrow from put-call parity at ATM strikes before shorting stock or buying puts — but only at ATM, and only in liquid monthlies
practices.detail: F_implied = K + (C − P)·e^(rT); annualized carry = (F/S − 1)/T; implied borrow ≈ r − carry. Verified on 2026-08-13 data: RIOT 2026-09-18 at strikes 19–23 clustered at implied borrow +0.4% to +3.3% — consistent, so RIOT was general-collateral at that snapshot. But at strikes 15–17 in the same expiry the same calculation returned −7.3% to +1.2%, and BYND's returned −89% to +23% across expiries. The dispersion is quote noise, not carry. Operational rule: use only strikes within 10% of spot, in a monthly with OI > 500 on BOTH the call and the put, and take the median across the 2–3 nearest strikes. If the strikes disagree by more than ~10 annualized points, the chain is too wide to imply anything and you should not trust its greeks either.

practices.practice: Apply a hard liquidity screen and reject, do not 'adjust for', anything that fails it
practices.detail: Reject the series unless ALL hold, measured between 10:00 and 15:30 ET (never at the open or in the last 10 minutes): (a) open interest ≥ 500 contracts on every leg; (b) the expiry is a third-Friday monthly; (c) quoted width ≤ max($0.05, 15% of mid) for penny classes — 10%-of-mid screens reject essentially the entire universe, since the observed median is 16–25% of mid for premium ≥ $0.20; (d) for nickel classes, no outright at all — spread only, and require net-debit width ≤ 20% of the net debit; (e) bid > $0.00 on both legs (a no-bid short leg cannot be closed); (f) underlying consolidated ADV ≥ 1,000,000 shares. Then size: contracts ≤ 5% of the series' open interest AND ≤ 20% of that series' 20-day average daily contract volume.

practices.practice: Send verticals as a single complex/combo order at a net price — never leg in
practices.detail: In a name where each leg is 20–60% of mid wide, legging means you own the first leg naked while you hunt for the second, and the second leg's market will move against you the moment the first prints. Both IBKR (Combo/BAG order via SmartRouting, which represents each leg independently for routing but only executes at your net) and tastytrade (native spread ticket) accept a net debit/credit. Quote the net in $0.01 steps — legal in every equity class per the complex order rules — starting at mid-to-mid and walking toward the sum-of-touch, stopping at a pre-set cap.

practices.practice: Screen your entire universe against OCC corporate-action memos every morning — reverse splits are routine at these prices and they orphan your position
practices.detail: Poll https://infomemo.theocc.com/ for your tickers daily. Live example in your named universe: OCC memo #59550 dated 2026-08-12 covers Beyond Meat's 1-for-30 reverse split, effective 11:59pm ET 2026-08-13, split-adjusted trading from the open 2026-08-14. Existing BYND options become BYND1 with an adjusted deliverable (1-for-30 implies ~3.3333 new shares plus cash-in-lieu of the fraction per contract — [UNVERIFIED: I could not retrieve the memo text directly; OCC returned HTTP 403. Confirm the exact deliverable and CIL from the memo before acting]). Aggregate strike value is preserved, so the adjustment is economically neutral — but a fresh standard BYND series opens alongside, market makers concentrate there, and your BYND1 contract becomes a near-untradeable orphan. Rule: close or roll any position in a name that has announced a reverse split at least two sessions before the effective date.

practices.practice: Use long puts and put debit spreads rather than short stock, and price the squeeze insurance you are buying
practices.detail: Your stated risk signature — small negative median, fat positive tail against the short — is exactly the shape that destroys short stock and is capped for long options. Quantified on PLUG at spot $2.31: short 100 shares into a +80% squeeze loses $184.80 with no cap, plus recall and buy-in risk; the 2026-09-18 $2.50 put caps loss at the $42 premium. That cap is what the 85–160% IV is charging you for. Do not treat the IV as 'expensive' in the abstract — treat it as the quoted price of the tail protection your strategy structurally requires, and then check (via the RN median table) whether your directional thesis still clears the hurdle after paying it.

practices.practice: Measure and log your own slippage versus arrival mid on every fill, and treat it as a strategy P&L line
practices.detail: Record: NBBO bid/ask at order arrival, your fill price, and (fill − arrival_mid)/arrival_mid. In this universe your realistic target is ≤ 30% of the half-spread. If your rolling average slippage exceeds ~40% of the half-spread you are not running a short-bias strategy, you are running a liquidity-provision subsidy. The reason to instrument this is in the numbers below: on the modelled PLUG trade the difference between filling at $0.38 and $0.42 flips expected P&L from +$3.95 to −$0.05 per contract.

practices.practice: Never carry a short put leg into expiration on a sub-$5 stock; flatten short legs by 21 DTE or at the latest the Wednesday of expiration week
practices.detail: OCC exercise-by-exception auto-exercises anything $0.01 or more in the money absent a Contrary Exercise Advice; holders have until 5:30pm ET on expiration day to submit a CEA, and brokers set earlier internal cutoffs (commonly ~4:30pm ET) [UNVERIFIED at the per-broker level: confirm your own broker's exact deadline in writing]. Being assigned on a $1.50-strike put means you own 100 shares of a delisting-risk micro cap per contract, purchased at a price you did not choose, over a weekend, with the Monday open gapping. The cost of closing the short leg early — often $1–$5 of residual premium plus commission — is trivially cheaper than that.

practices.practice: Ladder entries across two or three sessions and across two adjacent strikes rather than filling the whole clip at once
practices.detail: Given that 5%-of-OI and 20%-of-ADV caps typically permit only single-digit to low-double-digit contracts per day in these names (worked from 2026-08-13 data: CGC Sep18 $1.00 put OI 132 / volume 11 → 6 contract position cap, 2 contracts/day; FCEL Sep18 $20 put OI 803 / volume 33 → 40 cap, 6/day), a target position of 50 contracts is a multi-day build by construction. Splitting across adjacent strikes (e.g. PLUG $2.50 and $2.00) also diversifies you across two different market makers' inventories.

practices.practice: Avoid 09:30–09:45 and 15:50–16:00 ET; quote the chain at 10:00+ and re-quote before every entry
practices.detail: Opening rotation quotes in low-priced names are wide and frequently one-sided, and the auto-quote engines re-anchor for several minutes. The closing window in illiquid series is where the widest prints happen. The 'mid' you screened on at 09:31 is not a price you can trade at. Every liquidity screen threshold above should be re-measured immediately before the order goes in.

pitfalls.pitfall: Paying the offer on a wide, high-IV put hands the market maker the entire modelled edge — this is not a rounding error, it is the trade
pitfalls.mitigation: Worked example on real quotes (PLUG 2026-08-13, spot $2.31, 2026-09-18 $2.50 put, bid $0.34 / ask $0.42 / mid $0.38, IV 94.3%, OI 7,112). Modelling a realistic short-bias distribution (90% weight: grind with vol at 60% of listed IV; 10% weight: +80% median squeeze at 110% vol) and a −12% median grind thesis, expected P&L per contract is +$3.95 filling at $0.38 and −$0.05 filling at $0.42 — BEFORE the ~$1.24–$1.35 round-trip commission. The 4 cents of slippage is 10.5% of premium and 100% of the edge. Same for the 2.50/2.00 vertical: +$1.79/contract at a $0.30 debit, −$1.21 at the $0.33 sum-of-touch. Mitigation: hard price cap set before the order is sent, limit-at-mid with a $0.01 walk, and abandon the trade if it does not fill inside your cap — the trade at the wrong price is not the same trade.

pitfalls.pitfall: Trading a nickel-increment class as if it were a penny class — a 3–5x cost multiplier that is invisible unless you check
pitfalls.mitigation: Median quoted spread as % of mid, by premium bucket, penny vs nickel classes (2026-08-13, n=1,164): $0.10–$0.20 premium → 57% (penny) vs 133% (nickel); $0.20–$0.50 → 23% vs 97%; $0.50–$1.00 → 25% vs 67%; $1.00–$3.00 → 21% vs 34%; $3.00+ → 16% vs 21%. Direct like-for-like: FCEL (nickel, spot $20.47) 36d ~0.40-delta put quoted $2.40/$2.70 = $30/contract to cross; RIOT (penny, spot $19.91) 36d ~0.45-delta put quoted $2.15/$2.24 = $9/contract. Mitigation: consult the MIAX CSV every time; if the name is nickel, either express the trade as a complex order (net price in $0.01) or express it in the equity/short instead.

pitfalls.pitfall: Treating the mid as a real price when the market is 50–130% of mid wide
pitfalls.mitigation: When BYND's 2026-09-25 $0.50 put quoted $0.01/$0.17, its 'mid' of $0.09 carries no information and its printed IV (0.650, versus 1.607 one expiry earlier) is an artifact. Same for greeks: any delta or IV derived from a market that wide is unusable for sizing or hedging. Mitigation: refuse to compute anything from a series failing the width screen. Where you need a valuation, take it from the nearest liquid monthly and interpolate; where you need a delta, compute it yourself from a vol surface fitted only to series that pass the screen.

pitfalls.pitfall: High IV means the option already prices a large decline — buying puts is often a bet on the SPEED of a decline you were right about
pitfalls.mitigation: At 130% IV (BYND's observed range) the 90-day risk-neutral median is −18.8%; at 160% IV it is −27.1%. A thesis of 'this goes down 20% over the next quarter' is, at those IVs, roughly a zero-edge or negative-edge statement expressed through options. Mitigation: state your thesis as a median % move over an explicit horizon, compare it directly against the exp(−0.5σ²T)−1 table, and require a stated margin (I would want the thesis median at least 1.5x the RN median before paying the spread). Where your edge is about the shape/timing of the distribution rather than the median, express it in a spread whose strikes bracket your thesis rather than in an outright.

pitfalls.pitfall: The debit vertical caps exactly the left tail where a short-bias edge earns its money
pitfalls.mitigation: Under a plain lognormal (σ=94%, 36d) the PLUG $2.50 put at $0.42 breaks even in EV at a −6.7% thesis median, while the $2.50/$2.00 vertical at $0.33 requires −14.2% — the vertical is strictly worse because it sells away the crash. Under the more realistic thin-left-tail / fat-right-tail distribution the gap collapses to −12.0% vs −13.3%, and at good fills (−9.7% vs −8.1%) the vertical wins. The honest conclusion: verticals are correct when your thesis is a bounded grind to a specific level, and wrong when your thesis is 'this could go to zero.' Mitigation: place the short strike AT your drift target, not below it, and use outrights (or ratio structures) for genuine solvency/fraud theses where the left tail is the whole point.

pitfalls.pitfall: Early assignment on a short put leg, which converts a defined-risk spread into an unwanted long stock position in a micro cap
pitfalls.mitigation: A short American put is assigned early when its remaining extrinsic value falls below the holder's carry benefit — which for a hard-to-borrow name works in the opposite direction to intuition: HTB stock is valuable to hold and lend, so put holders DELAY exercise and deep-ITM puts can trade below parity. That means (a) your long deep-ITM put may be marked below intrinsic and you cannot monetise it at parity, and (b) assignment risk on your short leg spikes precisely when the borrow eases. Mitigation: monitor extrinsic value on the short leg daily and close it whenever extrinsic < $0.05; never let a short leg go deep ITM; and check for dividends/special distributions on the ETF and any surviving-dividend names in the book (the classic early-exercise trigger for short calls).

pitfalls.pitfall: Reverse-split contract adjustment strands you in an orphaned, non-standard series
pitfalls.mitigation: BYND is the live case: 1-for-30 effective 11:59pm ET 2026-08-13, options adjusted to BYND1 (OCC memo #59550, 2026-08-12). Post-adjustment, the strike stays but the deliverable shrinks, a brand-new standard BYND series lists alongside, and quoting concentrates in the new series — the adjusted contract's market widens dramatically and OI freezes. These names reverse-split routinely to hold Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum bid. Mitigation: daily OCC memo poll across the universe; automatic close/roll rule two sessions before any announced effective date; and a standing rule never to open a new position in a name trading under $1.00 that has not yet dealt with a listing-compliance deficiency.

pitfalls.pitfall: Pin and expiration risk — auto-exercise at $0.01 ITM on a stock whose tick is a large fraction of the strike
pitfalls.mitigation: OCC exercise-by-exception auto-exercises at $0.01 or more ITM. On a $1.00-strike option, a single penny of underlying movement in the closing auction is a 1% move that flips you between flat and long/short 100 shares per contract. Worse, micro caps halt: OCC publishes weekly trading-halt notices removing halted classes from ex-by-ex processing, meaning positions you assumed would auto-exercise will not. Mitigation: flatten everything by 21 DTE as the default; where you must hold to expiry, know your broker's CEA cutoff (industry deadline is 5:30pm ET on expiration day; brokers commonly cut off earlier — confirm yours), monitor the underlying's closing print rather than the 16:00 last, and size so that a full assignment is a position you could actually carry.

pitfalls.pitfall: Commission and fee drag that is invisible on large-cap options but material on $10–$40 positions
pitfalls.mitigation: A 2-leg vertical round trip costs ~$2.49 at tastytrade and ~$2.69 at IBKR Pro tiered. On the PLUG 2.50/2.00 vertical at a $0.28 debit ($28 of premium), that is 8.9% of the position. Mitigation: set a minimum position size (I would not open a spread with under ~$300 of premium at risk given these fee levels), exploit IBKR's premium-based tiering for cheap options (contracts with premium under $0.05 cost $0.25 rather than $0.65), and respect the $1.00 per-ORDER minimum at IBKR — a 1-contract order costs $1.00 regardless of the per-contract rate, so single-contract clips are the most fee-inefficient thing you can do.

pitfalls.pitfall: A class dropping out of the Penny Interval Program mid-year, which both widens your market and cancels your resting orders
pitfalls.mitigation: Per Cboe's Penny Interval Program listing requirements: OCC ranks all multiply-listed classes each December on National Cleared Volume (June 1–November 30 window). Classes in the top 300 (underlying under $200) are ADDED on the first trading day of January; classes falling outside the top 425 are REMOVED on the first trading day of April. Critically, 'Cboe Exchanges will cancel resting orders for any class being removed from the Penny Interval Program after the close on the business day prior.' Mitigation: re-download the MIAX CSV in the first week of January and the first week of April, diff it against your prior copy, and never rely on GTC resting orders surviving an April 1 rebalance.

pitfalls.pitfall: A short leg that goes no-bid, making the spread impossible to close as a unit
pitfalls.mitigation: In the 2026-08-13 snapshot, PLUG's 2026-10-02 $2.00 put quoted $0.00/$2.25 and RIOT's 2026-10-02 $18 put quoted $0.00/$3.50 — you cannot buy back a no-bid short leg at any sane price, and you cannot exit the spread as a package. Mitigation: require bid > $0.00 on both legs at entry; prefer short strikes that are round numbers with existing large OI (these keep a market longest); and where the short leg has decayed to near-zero value, simply abandon it and close the long leg alone rather than paying up to buy back a worthless option — but only after confirming you can carry the residual short exposure through expiration.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming the ORF and fee schedule you priced against is still current
pitfalls.mitigation: Cboe's ORF effective 2026-01-02 is $0.0023/contract on Cboe Options, $0.0002 on BZX and EDGX, $0.0003 on C2 — with all of these scheduled to sunset 2026-06-30 alongside a planned new on-exchange-only ORF model from 2026-07-01 [UNVERIFIED whether that model actually took effect; the source is a November 2025 notice describing a plan]. OCC's clearing fee reverted to $0.025/contract on the first trading day of 2026 after a December 2025 fee holiday, and OCC has run such holidays repeatedly. Mitigation: re-pull the broker fee schedule and the exchange ORF notice quarterly, and reconcile against actual trade confirmations rather than the published schedule.

pitfalls.pitfall: Sizing off open interest alone when daily volume is near zero
pitfalls.mitigation: OI tells you a position exists; volume tells you whether you can get out. PLUG's Sep18 $2.50 put had OI 7,112 but only 5 contracts traded that day — a 5%-of-OI cap suggests 355 contracts, while a 20%-of-ADV cap suggests 1. Mitigation: apply BOTH caps and take the minimum. In practice this means your realistic position in most of these series is 5–50 contracts built over days, and it means the strategy's capacity is a fact you must respect rather than a constraint you can trade around.

pitfalls.pitfall: Using the MidPrice algo for options at IBKR because it works for stock
pitfalls.mitigation: The TWS API documentation states MidPrice is 'Smart-routing to US stocks only' — it will not work for options. SNAP MID (Snap to Midpoint) is the correct order type and is documented to support US stocks, options and futures, with the offset in whole-penny increments. [UNVERIFIED: whether the Adaptive algo supports options — IBKR's API algo documentation shows Adaptive with US-stock examples only and does not state option support; Balance Impact Risk and Minimise Impact are the algos explicitly documented with US option contract examples. Confirm with IBKR before relying on Adaptive for an options combo.]

concrete_specs: Penny/nickel class list endpoint (free, no auth): https://www.miaxglobal.com/sites/default/files/listings/PennyPilotClasses.csv — 356 classes on 2026-08-13. Parallel per-exchange files: MIAXPEARLPennyPilotClasses.csv, MIAXEmeraldPennyPilotClasses.csv, MIAXSapphirePennyPilotClasses.csv in the same directory.

Free delayed options chain with bid/ask/IV/OI/volume/greeks, no auth, no rate limit encountered: https://cdn.cboe.com/api/global/delayed_quotes/options/{SYMBOL}.json — e.g. .../PLUG.json returned 248 series with keys bid, bid_size, ask, ask_size, iv, open_interest, volume, delta, gamma, vega, theta, rho, theo, last_trade_price, last_trade_time. Option symbol field parses as ROOT + YYMMDD + C/P + strike*1000 zero-padded to 8.
Minimum quoting increments — PENNY classes: $0.01 below $3.00 premium, $0.05 at/above $3.00. NON-PENNY classes: $0.05 below $3.00, $0.10 at/above $3.00. SPY/QQQ/IWM: $0.01 at all premium levels.

Complex-order net price minimum increment is $0.01 in every equity option class (SPX/SPXW excepted at $0.05, with boxes/rolls at $0.01), and individual legs may execute in $0.01 increments regardless of the series' own minimum increment. This is the mechanism for getting sub-nickel pricing in FCEL/CHPT/HYZN-type names.

Penny Interval Program rebalance calendar: OCC ranks classes each December on National Cleared Volume for June 1–November 30. Top 300 (underlying < $200) ADDED on the first trading day of January. Outside top 425 REMOVED on the first trading day of April. Resting orders in a removed class are CANCELLED after the close on the prior business day.

IBKR Pro US options, Tiered, ≤10,000 contracts/month: premium < $0.05 → $0.25/contract; $0.05 ≤ premium < $0.10 → $0.50/contract; premium ≥ $0.10 → $0.65/contract. 10,001–50,000: $0.25 / $0.50. 50,001–100,000: $0.25 all premiums. ≥100,001: $0.15 all premiums. Minimum per ORDER: $1.00. IBKR Lite: $0.65/contract flat, $1.00 order minimum, US residents only.

tastytrade equity/ETF options: $1.00/contract to open, $0.00 to close, commission capped at $10 per leg to open. Plus tastytrade clearing fee $0.10/contract, ORF $0.02/contract, FINRA TAF $0.00329/contract on sales, option exercise/assignment $5.

Order types that work: IBKR SNAP MID (Snap to Midpoint) — supports US stocks, options AND futures; offset must be whole pennies; buy limit = midpoint − offset. IBKR MidPrice algo is US STOCKS ONLY and will not work for options. Send verticals as a single Combo/BAG order at a net price via SmartRouting, never legged.

Liquidity screen (reject, do not adjust): OI ≥ 500 per leg; third-Friday monthly expiry only; width ≤ max($0.05, 15% of mid) for penny classes; nickel classes spread-only with net-debit width ≤ 20% of debit; bid > $0.00 on both legs; underlying ADV ≥ 1,000,000 shares; measured 10:00–15:30 ET.

Position sizing caps: min(5% of the series' open interest, 20% of that series' 20-day average daily contract volume). Worked from real data: CGC Sep18 $1.00P (OI 132, vol 11) → 6-contract cap, 2/day. FCEL Sep18 $20P (OI 803, vol 33) → 40-contract cap, 6/day. PLUG Sep18 $2.00P (OI 5,566, vol 1,049) → 278-contract cap, 209/day.

Risk-neutral median decline already embedded in the option, exp(−0.5σ²T)−1 — at 85% IV: −2.1% (21d) / −3.5% (36d) / −5.8% (60d) / −8.5% (90d) / −30.3% (1y). At 95% IV: −2.6% / −4.4% / −7.1% / −10.5% / −36.3%. At 130% IV: −4.7% / −8.0% / −13.0% / −18.8% / −57.0%. At 160% IV: −7.1% / −11.9% / −19.0% / −27.1% / −72.2%. Require your thesis median to be at least ~1.5x these before paying the spread.

Implied borrow from parity: F = K + (C − P)·e^(rT); implied borrow ≈ r − (F/S − 1)/T. Use only strikes within 10% of spot in a monthly with OI > 500 on BOTH call and put; take the median of the 2–3 nearest strikes; discard if strikes disagree by >10 annualized points. RIOT 2026-09-18 strikes 19–23 gave a consistent +0.4% to +3.3% (general collateral); strikes 15–17 in the same expiry gave −7.3% to +1.2% (noise).
Third-Friday monthly vs weekly, same names and window: monthlies median spread 20% of mid, median OI 86; weeklies median spread 32% of mid, median OI 5.
Spread % of mid by put |delta| in penny classes: 0.05–0.15 → 50%; 0.15–0.25 → 17%; 0.25–0.35 → 10%; 0.35–0.45 → 17%; 0.45–0.60 → 18%. Target 0.35–0.55 delta for a slow-drift thesis.

OCC exercise-by-exception threshold: $0.01 in the money, auto-exercised absent a Contrary Exercise Advice. Industry CEA deadline 5:30pm ET on expiration day; brokers set earlier internal cutoffs (commonly ~4:30pm ET — confirm yours in writing). OCC removes halted classes from ex-by-ex processing via weekly trading-halt memos.

Corporate action monitoring: https://infomemo.theocc.com/infomemos?number={N} — memo #59550 (2026-08-12) is the Beyond Meat 1-for-30 reverse split, effective 11:59pm ET 2026-08-13, adjusting BYND options to BYND1. Poll this daily against your universe and close/roll two sessions before any effective date.

Slippage budget and instrumentation: log NBBO bid/ask at order arrival and (fill − arrival_mid)/arrival_mid on every fill; target ≤ 30% of the half-spread; investigate the strategy if the rolling average exceeds 40%.
Time-of-day exclusions: no entries 09:30–09:45 ET or 15:50–16:00 ET; re-measure every screen threshold immediately before sending the order.
costs: Crossing cost per contract at real quotes, 2026-08-13, 36 DTE, ~0.4–0.55 delta puts: RIOT (penny, $19.91 stock) $0.09 wide = $9.00/contract = 4% of premium. PLUG (penny, $2.31) $0.08 wide = $8.00/contract = 21% of premium. CGC (penny, $1.03) $0.05 wide = $5.00/contract = 59% of premium. FCEL (NICKEL, $20.47) $0.30 wide = $30.00/contract = 12% of premium. CHPT (NICKEL, $6.28) $0.10 wide = $10.00/contract = 20% of premium at the $6 strike and 50% at the $5 strike.

Sum-of-touch penalty on a 2-leg vertical: PLUG 2026-09-18 2.50/2.00 puts — mid-to-mid $0.28, sum-of-touch $0.33. The $0.05 is 17.9% of the debit and cuts max profit from $0.22 to $0.17 (−23%). FCEL 2026-09-18 20/16 puts — mid-to-mid $1.725, sum-of-touch $2.00; the $0.275 is 15.9% of the debit and cuts R:R from 1.32:1 to 1.00:1.

Slippage as a fraction of total edge (modelled on real PLUG quotes, thin-left-tail/fat-right-tail distribution, −12% median grind thesis): outright $2.50 put expected P&L +$3.95/contract filled at $0.38 mid, −$0.05/contract filled at $0.42 ask. Vertical expected P&L +$1.79/contract at a $0.30 debit, −$1.21 at the $0.33 sum-of-touch. Source: my own Monte-Carlo-free integration over the Cboe 2026-08-13 chain; the distribution assumption is mine, the quotes are real.

IBKR Pro Tiered US options: $0.65/contract (premium ≥ $0.10), $0.50 (premium $0.05–$0.10), $0.25 (premium < $0.05), $1.00 minimum per order, plus pass-through exchange/clearing/regulatory fees. Source: interactivebrokers.com/en/pricing/commissions-options.php, retrieved 2026-08-13.

execution.topic: Position sizing and risk control for fat-tailed short books in US small/micro-cap equities ($0.5–$5), where ~4% of positions return >+25% against the short and p95 is +21.8%

practices.practice: Define the maximum loss per position BEFORE computing any size — Kelly is mathematically zero for an uncapped short
practices.detail: Kelly maximizes E[log(1 + f·(−r))]. For a short, loss is unbounded above, so for any f>0 there exists r ≥ 1/f in the support and E[log] = −∞. Kelly's answer for a naked micro-cap short is literally 0% — not 'small'. This is not a conservatism argument, it is the arithmetic. Only after you impose a hard ceiling L on the adverse move (long call, long put expression, or defined-risk spread) does an optimal f exist, and it equals at most 1/L. Operational rule: no short position gets entered until the ticket includes the capping leg. In IBKR TWS, build it as a native combo (BAG) order so the short stock and the long call fill together or not at all — never leg in with the intention of 'adding the hedge later'.

practices.practice: Derive per-name size from the capped loss and a single-name NAV budget, not from a volatility target
practices.detail: Rule: w_i ≤ (single-name NAV budget) / L_i, where L_i is the defined max adverse move. Worked table from my simulation: with L = 35% (short stock + 35%-OTM call) and a 1.0%-of-NAV single-name budget, max weight = 2.86% of NAV; at a 0.5% budget, 1.43%. With L = 50%, those become 2.00% and 1.00%. For a pure put-spread expression where L = 100% of the debit, a 1.0%-of-NAV budget means 1.0% of NAV in premium per name. Write this as a hard pre-trade check in the order router, not a guideline.

practices.practice: Set gross exposure from your drawdown budget assuming tail correlation goes to 1.0
practices.detail: In a squeeze regime every heavily-shorted name is the same trade. Budget as: Σ(w_i × L_i) ≤ drawdown_budget. Concrete outputs: a 15% drawdown budget with a 35%-OTM call cap on every name permits 43% gross short notional; with a 50%-OTM cap, 30% gross; with put spreads (L=100% of premium), 15% of NAV in total premium. A 10% drawdown budget permits 29% / 20% / 10% respectively. Note how small these are — that is the correct answer for this asset class, and it is the single most important number in this section.

practices.practice: Use equal-weight, not inverse-vol or vol-target weighting
practices.detail: I simulated 25 names with realized vols spread 6%–20% (inverse-vol weights ranged 2.30%–7.67%, a 3.33x spread). Capped at +35%, equal-weight returned mean +1.68% / sd 2.98% / p01 −5.34% vs inverse-vol +1.62% / sd 2.72% / p01 −5.03% — a marginal body-variance improvement. Uncapped, equal-weight worst case was −12,948% vs inverse-vol −26,225%. Inverse-vol makes the tail WORSE here because squeeze probability is driven by float, borrow scarcity and retail flow, not by trailing realized vol; the coiled pre-squeeze name has low realized vol and gets overweighted. Vol-weighting is a body-risk tool being applied to a tail-risk problem.

practices.practice: Stop diversifying at ~40 names; past that you are buying borrow cost, not risk reduction
practices.detail: At fixed 50% gross with a +35% cap: n=5 gives sd 2.82% / p01 −6.48%; n=10, sd 1.99% / p01 −4.19%; n=20, sd 1.41% / p01 −2.68%; n=40, sd 1.00% / p01 −1.64%; n=80, sd 0.70% / p01 −0.92%. The idiosyncratic term keeps shrinking as 1/√n but the correlated floor does not move: if every name squeezes to its cap you lose 0.35 × 0.50 = 17.5% of NAV regardless of n. Beyond ~40 names you pay 40+ borrow fees and 40+ locate/commission tickets to reduce a variance term that is already dominated by the regime term.

practices.practice: Cap by squeeze cohort, not by GICS sector
practices.detail: The correlation cluster that matters is not 'Industrials' — it is 'names on the r/wallstreetbets radar with >20% short interest, <$1bn float and a rising borrow rate'. In Jan 2021 the Goldman Sachs most-shorted basket (50 Russell 3000 names, >$1bn cap, highest short interest as % of float) rallied 98% over three months. Suggested hard caps: ≤25% of gross in any one squeeze cohort, where cohort is defined by a composite of (short interest % float > 20%), (borrow fee > 25%/yr), (name appeared on a Reg SHO threshold list in the last 60 days), and (retail message-board mention z-score > 2). Recompute cohort membership daily, not monthly.

practices.practice: Gate the universe on options availability, then simply do not trade the ungated names
practices.detail: Options initial listing standards require the underlying to have closed above $3.00 for the five preceding business days, ≥7 million share float, ≥2,000 shareholders and ≥200,000 ADV. Sub-$3 names therefore may have no listed options at all, and once they fall below $3 no new series are added unless the option averaged ≥5,000 contracts/day over the preceding three months. Since your only viable expression is a defined-risk one and defined risk requires options, the honest conclusion is that a large slice of the $0.5–$3 universe is untradeable for this book. Build the options-availability check into the screen at the top of the funnel, not at the order stage.

practices.practice: Price the short-borrow collateral rounding into the sizing decision — for sub-$1 names it doubles or triples the quoted fee
practices.detail: Industry convention (and IBKR's) is that stock-borrow collateral equals 102% of the prior settlement price rounded UP to the nearest whole dollar, minimum $1.00, and the borrow fee accrues on that collateral, not on your notional. Effective multipliers on a $0.50 stock: 2.00x; $0.30: 3.33x; $1.01: 1.98x; $1.99: 1.51x; $4.01: 1.25x. There is a punitive discontinuity at each whole dollar — a $0.99 stock carries a 2.02x multiplier while a $0.95 stock carries 1.05x. Add a rule: never initiate a short in a name trading within 8 cents above a whole-dollar level; wait for it to cross back below, or size down by the multiplier.

practices.practice: Size against real FINRA 4210 maintenance margin, which is 100%–500% of notional for this universe
practices.detail: FINRA Rule 4210(c) short maintenance: for stocks under $5.00 it is $2.50/share OR 100% of current market value, whichever is greater; for stocks at $5.00+ it is $5.00/share OR 30% of market value, whichever is greater. Computed: $0.50 stock = 500% of notional; $1.00 = 250%; $2.00 = 125%; $2.49–$5.00 = 100%; $8.00 = 62%; and the 30% rate only begins to bind above $16.67. Your capital constraint will bite long before your risk constraint does, which is a second, independent argument for expressing this book in options rather than stock.

practices.practice: Do not treat stop orders as defined risk — they are not, in this universe
practices.detail: I simulated stop-outs with a 25% probability of gapping through (overnight gap, LULD halt, or halt-resume). At a +25% stop, expected short P&L was +0.34% with zero slippage and −0.14% with 20% slippage, versus +1.90% for a true option-capped position; the worst case with a stop was still −31,443%. LULD bands for Tier 2 names are 20% for $0.75–$3.00 and 75% (or 15 cents, whichever is lower) below $0.75, with a five-minute pause after 15 seconds in a Limit State — your stop simply does not execute during the pause and the reopening print can be anywhere. A stop is a portfolio-management tool. A long call is risk control.

practices.practice: Run a drawdown governor with a de-grossing ladder tied to borrow-fee and price triggers, not to P&L alone
practices.detail: Concrete ladder: at −5% month-to-date, no new shorts; at −8%, cut gross by one third; at −12%, cut gross by two thirds and close every position lacking a capping leg; at −15%, flat and stop for the month. Add non-P&L triggers because P&L lags: (a) any name whose IBKR indicative borrow rate rises more than 3x in five sessions gets halved automatically; (b) any name that appears on a Reg SHO threshold securities list gets closed (buy-in risk is now real); (c) if the count of your names under a Rule 201 short-sale-restriction flag exceeds 30% in a week, that is a regime signal — de-gross. In Jan 2021 Goldman reported hedge-fund gross leverage fell 7.5% in a single day and 10% over the week of Jan 25, the fastest active de-grossing since February 2009: everyone de-grosses at once, so the ladder must fire on rules, not on a decision made during the event.

practices.practice: Treat broker liquidation-only risk as a modeled scenario and hold a second clearing relationship
practices.detail: On 28 Jan 2021 Interactive Brokers put AMC, BB, EXPR, GME and KOSS options into liquidation-only and set long stock to 100% margin and short stock to 300% margin. A 300% short requirement on a position you already hold is a forced-deleveraging event independent of your own risk model. Model it explicitly: assume your broker can, without notice, (i) triple the margin on your largest positions, (ii) refuse new opening orders, and (iii) recall your borrow. Mitigation is structural — maintain a second prime/clearing relationship and keep enough excess liquidity that a 3x requirement on your full short book does not trigger a house liquidation.

practices.practice: Use the mean-versus-median gap as the direct measure of how much insurance you are implicitly short
practices.detail: On a distribution calibrated to your stated quantiles (median −2.5%, P(down) 55%, p95 +22.2%, P(>+25%) 4.0%, Pareto tail alpha 1.8), the mean stock return is +4.40% against a median of −2.46% — a 6.86-point gap — and 72.7% of ALL upside movement in the universe comes from the top 4% of observations.
