Restated as short P&L: median +2.46%, mean −4.40%. A naked short in this universe is a short-insurance position that wins most months and has negative expectancy. Report both mean and median for every backtest and every live book; if they disagree in sign, you do not have a strategy, you have an insurance book that has not paid a claim yet.

practices.practice: Verify that the option you buy as the cap is not itself priced to eat the whole edge — the trade lives in the skew, not the level
practices.detail: On the modeled distribution the breakeven flat IV for a 60-day 100/80 put spread is only ~38%. Micro-cap names in this cohort typically trade far above that (modeling assumption: 80–160% IV — verify live per name), which makes the naive put spread a losing trade even though the directional view is right. At IV 120%, a 60d 100/80 put spread costs 50% of its width and returned −46% on risk in simulation; at IV 160% it costs 56% of width. The exploitable structure is that call skew in squeeze candidates is bid relative to puts, so the asymmetry to hunt is put spreads financed against the elevated call side, or a short + long OTM call where you are BUYING the expensive wing only because you must. Compute a per-trade breakeven IV before each ticket and reject the trade if quoted IV exceeds it.

practices.practice: Handle reverse splits explicitly, both in the live book and in the research data
practices.detail: Sub-$5 names reverse split constantly to cure the Nasdaq $1.00 minimum bid price rule (5810(c)(3)(A), 180-day compliance period). Recent examples: SPCE 1-for-20 effective 14 Jun 2024 (split-adjusted trading 17 Jun 2024); HYZN 1-for-50 effective 11 Sep 2024. Two consequences. (1) Live: after a 1-for-20, a $1 strike option becomes a $20 strike delivering 5 shares with the 100 multiplier retained — a non-standard contract with a $100 notional, terrible liquidity, and expensive exit. Roll into the new standard series before the split, do not hold through it. (2) Research: on unadjusted prices a 1-for-10 reverse split reads as a +900% return, which is neutral to a properly adjusted short but catastrophic-looking in the data. This is a live hazard in your own repo — see the pitfalls section.

practices.practice: Track your Form SHO reporting threshold as a hard operating constraint on gross
practices.detail: SEC Rule 13f-2 / Form SHO took effect 2 Jan 2025, first filing 14 Feb 2025. Institutional investment managers must file monthly, within 14 days of month-end, if the monthly average gross short position in a reporting-issuer equity is ≥$10 million OR ≥2.5% of shares outstanding. In micro-caps the 2.5% test binds long before the $10m test. This interacts with margin: IBKR increases nominal margin for positions above 1% of a company's shares outstanding and requires full margin at ≥9%. Set a hard pre-trade cap at 1.0% of shares outstanding per name — it keeps you under IBKR's escalation, well under Form SHO's 2.5%, and out of the illiquidity zone where you cannot cover.

practices.practice: Monitor borrow rate and availability intraday as a leading risk indicator, and pre-borrow the names you cannot afford to be recalled on
practices.detail: Borrow fee is the highest-frequency squeeze signal available to you and it is free from your broker. IBKR publishes shortable-share counts, lender counts and indicative borrow rates; the daily file is available at ftp://ftp3.interactivebrokers.com/ (username shortstock, blank password, file usa.txt) — secondary-source, verify the endpoint against IBKR's current documentation before wiring it in. Poll it once daily pre-open, diff availability and fee per name, and alert on any name whose available shares fall more than 50% or whose fee rises more than 3x. Under Reg SHO Rule 203(b)(1) your broker needs a locate before each short; a locate is not a borrow, and it can vanish. For your largest positions use a pre-borrow so the position cannot be bought in at the worst moment.

pitfalls.pitfall: Computing a Kelly fraction from a backtest mean without checking whether the mean is sign-identifiable
pitfalls.mitigation: Your own repo already found this failure mode. /home/user/WireAntennaGain/research/ftd-empirical-findings.md documents that the FTD study's mean flipped sign purely on the trimming choice, affecting under 0.6% of observations: trimming forward ratios above 1.8x gave mean −1.02% (short earns +1.02%), above 3x gave +0.61%, above 5x gave +0.34%, above 10x gave +0.19% (short LOSES), above 25x gave −0.83%. The file's own verdict: 'Any strategy whose expectancy flips sign on a trimming parameter is not a strategy.' Before any Kelly calculation, run the trim-sensitivity table and require the sign to be stable across 1.8x–25x. If it is not, the correct size is zero.

pitfalls.pitfall: The stated tail statistics (4% >+25%, p95 +21.8%) are themselves contaminated by unadjusted reverse-split prices
pitfalls.mitigation: The same findings file records that the SEC FTD file's price column is an unadjusted prior-day close and that its extreme right tail (q0.999 = +615%, max = +899,900%) is 'an inseparable mix of genuine squeezes — catastrophic for a short — and reverse splits, which are neutral for a short who is adjusted.' You cannot size against this tail until it is decomposed. Re-derive the tail on split-adjusted prices from a real market-data vendor (CRSP, Polygon, Norgate, Sharadar) before treating 4%/+25% as the design input. Until then treat 4% as an upper bound on genuine squeeze frequency and size to the conservative end.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming a diversified short book is diversified during the event that matters
pitfalls.mitigation: Goldman called January 2021 the biggest short squeeze in 25 years, with its most-shorted basket up 98% over the preceding three months. Every name in that basket was somebody's independent idea. Stress the book explicitly: my simulation of a uniform +98% move gives −24.5% of NAV at 25% gross naked, −49.0% at 50% gross, −98.0% at 100% gross; the same event with a +35% cap gives −8.8% / −17.5% / −35.0%. Run this exact scenario nightly and make the 'all names squeeze together' number a reported risk metric alongside VaR.

pitfalls.pitfall: Believing a stop-loss defines your risk in a name that can be LULD-halted
pitfalls.mitigation: Tier 2 LULD bands are 20% for $0.75–$3.00 and 75% (or 15 cents, lower of) below $0.75, with a five-minute pause. During the pause no stop executes. In simulation, a +25% stop with a 25% gap-through assumption (my assumption — calibrate it from your own fill history) still produced a −31,443% worst case, versus a hard −25% for the option-capped version. Only an owned long option is a floor. If a name has no listed options, it has no floor, and it does not belong in the book.

pitfalls.pitfall: Equal-weighting by notional while ignoring that margin and borrow cost are wildly non-linear in price across $0.5–$5
pitfalls.mitigation: Two separate non-linearities compound. FINRA 4210 maintenance is 500% of notional at $0.50, 250% at $1.00, 125% at $2.00, 100% from $2.49 to $5.00. Borrow collateral rounding adds 3.33x at $0.30, 2.00x at $0.50, 1.98x at $1.01, 1.25x at $4.01. A notionally equal-weighted book is therefore a wildly unequal book in capital and carry. Equal-weight on RISK (w × L) and separately publish a per-name carry number so the sizing committee sees that the $0.60 name costs 3x the $4 name to hold.

pitfalls.pitfall: Underestimating carry: on a squeeze candidate, borrow alone can exceed the entire expected edge
pitfalls.mitigation: Hard-to-borrow names commonly run 5%–50%/yr and squeezed names 100%+ (secondary sources; verify per name against your broker's live indicative rate). Applying the 102%/ceil collateral rule: a $0.50 stock quoted at 100%/yr costs an effective 200%/yr on notional — 33.3% of notional over a 60-day hold and 100% over six months. Your own repo computed the FTD chronic-fail signal's breakeven annualized borrow fee at only 25%–55%, 'same order as actual HTB fees.' Require an explicit edge > carry test on every ticket, with carry computed on collateral, not notional.

pitfalls.pitfall: Buying the capping option at any price and destroying the edge you were hedging
pitfalls.mitigation: At 120% IV a 60-day 35%-OTM call costs 9.3% of spot — roughly 56%/yr of carry on top of borrow. In simulation this turned a 25-name naked book's −8.30% mean into −11.87% while improving p01 from −65.5% to −18.0% and the worst case from −4,418% to −24.5%. That is a good trade for survival and a bad trade for return. The resolution is not to skip the hedge — it is to shrink the notional so the hedge is affordable, shorten the horizon, and reject any name where the required cap costs more than roughly one third of your modeled edge.

pitfalls.pitfall: Treating twice-monthly FINRA short interest as a current risk input
pitfalls.mitigation: FINRA Rule 4560 currently requires firms to report twice monthly, received no later than the second business day after the designated settlement date, and dissemination lags further. FINRA has filed SR-FINRA-2026-012 (filed 1 May 2026, Federal Register 18 May 2026) to move to weekly publication five business days after settlement date — still pending SEC action as of August 2026, so plan for the current cadence. By the time official short interest shows crowding, the squeeze has happened. Use securities-lending-derived data (Ortex, S3 Partners) or your broker's own shortable file as the live signal, and treat FINRA short interest as a historical research variable only.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming your broker will let you keep the position on
pitfalls.mitigation: IBKR's 28 Jan 2021 action set short stock margin to 300% and put five names' options into liquidation-only. Model your worst-case margin call as: 300% of your top five positions' notional, called same-day, with no ability to open offsetting hedges. If that scenario exceeds your excess liquidity, your book is too big irrespective of what your risk model says. Maintain excess liquidity of at least 3x current short-book maintenance requirement, and hold a second clearing relationship so an opening-order freeze at one broker does not strand you.

pitfalls.pitfall: Holding options through a reverse split and discovering you own an untradeable non-standard contract
pitfalls.mitigation: After a 1-for-20 reverse split a $1 strike becomes a $20 strike with a 5-share deliverable and a retained 100 multiplier — $100 of notional per contract, near-zero liquidity, and wide exit spreads. Non-penny classes quote in $0.05 increments below $3.00 premium and $0.10 above, so the round-trip on a $100-notional contract can be several percent. Subscribe to Nasdaq Equity Corporate Action alerts and OCC Information Memos, screen the book weekly for announced splits, and roll into the post-split standard series before the effective date rather than after.

pitfalls.pitfall: Letting per-name size drift above 1% of shares outstanding
pitfalls.mitigation: Above 1% of shares outstanding IBKR increases nominal margin and at ≥9% requires full margin; at ≥2.5% of shares outstanding you cross the Form SHO monthly reporting threshold; and well before either, your position exceeds what you can cover in a squeeze without moving the price against yourself. Enforce a pre-trade check: position shares ≤ min(1.0% of shares outstanding, 15% of 20-day median ADV). The ADV test is the one that actually determines whether you can get out.

concrete_specs: Per-name weight formula: w_i ≤ (single-name NAV budget) / L_i. With L=35% and a 1.0%-of-NAV budget → 2.86% max weight; 0.5% budget → 1.43%. With L=50% → 2.00% / 1.00%. With put spreads (L=100% of debit) → 1.00% / 0.50% of NAV in premium.

Gross budget formula: Σ(w_i × L_i) ≤ drawdown budget. 15% DD budget → 43% gross with 35%-OTM call caps, 30% gross with 50%-OTM caps, or 15% of NAV total premium in put spreads. 10% DD budget → 29% / 20% / 10%.
Hard per-name caps to code into the pre-trade check: position shares ≤ 1.0% of shares outstanding AND ≤ 15% of 20-day median ADV.

Squeeze-cohort cap: ≤25% of gross in any one cohort, cohort = composite of short interest >20% of float, borrow fee >25%/yr, Reg SHO threshold list appearance in last 60 days, message-board mention z-score >2. Recompute daily.

Name count: target 25–40. Below 25 the idiosyncratic tail dominates (n=5: p01 −6.48% at 50% gross); above 40 the marginal variance reduction (sd 1.00% → 0.70% going 40→80) is not worth 40 extra borrow fees.
De-grossing ladder: −5% MTD no new shorts; −8% cut gross by 1/3; −12% cut by 2/3 and close every uncapped position; −15% flat for the month.

Non-P&L de-gross triggers: any name whose indicative borrow rate rises >3x in 5 sessions gets halved; any name appearing on a Reg SHO threshold securities list gets closed; >30% of book under a Rule 201 short-sale-restriction flag in one week = regime de-gross.

FINRA Rule 4210(c) short maintenance margin: under $5.00 = greater of $2.50/share or 100% of market value; $5.00+ = greater of $5.00/share or 30% of market value. Computed as % of notional: $0.50 → 500%; $1.00 → 250%; $2.00 → 125%; $2.49–$5.00 → 100%; $8.00 → 62%. The 30% rate first binds above $16.67.
Reg T initial margin for a short sale = 150% of market value, of which 100% is satisfied by the short proceeds, leaving 50% customer deposit (12 CFR Part 220).

IBKR Portfolio Margin minimum: USD 110,000 Net Liquidation Value to open; restricted from margin-increasing trades if NLV falls below USD 100,000. All short transactions carry a USD 2,000 minimum initial margin.

IBKR low-cap margin schedule: requirement grows linearly 30% → 100% as market cap falls from $500M to $250M; for $250M–$100M cap the requirement is 100%, subject to a $2.50/share minimum. Nominal margin is increased above 1% of shares outstanding and full margin is required at ≥9%.

Stock-borrow collateral convention: 102% of prior settlement price, rounded UP to the nearest whole dollar, $1.00 minimum, with the borrow fee accruing on collateral rather than notional. Effective rate multipliers: $0.30 → 3.33x, $0.50 → 2.00x, $0.95 → 1.05x, $0.99 → 2.02x, $1.01 → 1.98x, $1.99 → 1.51x, $4.01 → 1.25x.
Avoid initiating shorts within ~8 cents above any whole-dollar price level — the collateral rounding discontinuity roughly doubles carry (a $0.99 stock costs a 2.02x multiplier vs 1.05x at $0.95).

Options initial listing standards: underlying above $3.00 for 5 consecutive business days, ≥7 million share float, ≥2,000 shareholders, ≥200,000 ADV. Once below $3.00, new series are added only if the option averaged ≥5,000 contracts/day over the preceding 3 calendar months. Use this as a universe gate.

LULD Tier 2 price bands: 20% for $0.75–$3.00; 75% (or 15 cents, whichever is lower) below $0.75; 10% above $3.00. Limit State for 15 seconds triggers a 5-minute trading pause during which no stop order executes.

Reg SHO Rule 201 (alternative uptick rule): triggered by a 10% intraday decline from the prior close; short sales then permitted only above the national best bid for the remainder of that day and the following day.

Reg SHO Rule 203(b)(1): a documented locate is required before every short sale. An 'Easy to Borrow' list must be less than 24 hours old to establish reasonable grounds. Pre-borrow (not just locate) your largest positions.

Reg SHO Rule 204 close-out: short-sale fails must be closed out by the beginning of regular trading hours on the settlement day following settlement date; long-sale and bona-fide market-making fails by the third consecutive settlement day. Failure restricts future short sales in that security absent a pre-borrow.

SEC Rule 13f-2 / Form SHO: compliance date 2 Jan 2025, first filing 14 Feb 2025. Monthly filing within 14 days of month-end if the monthly average gross short position in a reporting issuer is ≥$10 million OR ≥2.5% of shares outstanding. In micro-caps the 2.5% test binds first.

FINRA Rule 4560 short interest: currently twice monthly, reports due no later than the second business day after the designated settlement date. SR-FINRA-2026-012 (filed 1 May 2026, FR 18 May 2026) proposes weekly publication five business days after settlement date — pending SEC action as of Aug 2026.

IBKR daily shortable-shares file: ftp://ftp3.interactivebrokers.com/ , username 'shortstock', blank password, file usa.txt, updated daily, containing available shares, lender count and indicative borrow rate. [Secondary-source — verify against current IBKR documentation before automating.]
Order construction: enter short + long OTM call as a native IBKR combo (BAG) order so both legs fill atomically. Never leg in intending to add the cap later.

Options quoting increments for non-penny classes: $0.05 below $3.00 premium, $0.10 at $3.00 and above. Penny-program classes quote $0.01 below $3.00 and $0.05 above. Check class membership before assuming an exit price.

Reverse-split handling: a 1-for-20 split converts a $1 strike into a $20 strike delivering 5 shares with the 100 multiplier retained ($100 notional per contract). Roll into the new standard series before the effective date. Reference examples: SPCE 1-for-20 effective 14 Jun 2024 (adjusted trading 17 Jun 2024); HYZN 1-for-50 effective 11 Sep 2024.

Nasdaq Rule 5810(c)(3)(A): $1.00 minimum bid price with a 180-calendar-day automatic compliance period. A company that reverse-split within the prior 1 year, or split cumulatively ≥250:1 over the prior 2 years, gets no compliance period and an immediate delisting determination.

Excess-liquidity rule: hold at least 3x the current short book's maintenance requirement in excess liquidity, sized against the scenario that the broker sets short margin to 300% (as IBKR did on AMC, BB, EXPR, GME, KOSS on 28 Jan 2021).

Pre-trade breakeven-IV check for the put-spread expression: on a distribution calibrated to median −2.5%, P(down) 55%, p95 +22.2%, P(>+25%) 4.0% and a Pareto tail alpha 1.8, a 60-day 100/80 put spread breaks even only at ~38% flat IV. Reject the ticket if quoted IV exceeds the per-trade breakeven.

Stress scenario to report nightly: uniform +98% move across all shorts (Jan 2021 Goldman most-shorted basket, 3-month move). Naked → −24.5% of NAV at 25% gross, −49.0% at 50%, −98.0% at 100%. With a +35% cap → −8.8% / −17.5% / −35.0%.

Mandatory reporting metric: publish mean AND median P&L for every backtest and live book. On the modeled universe the stock's median is −2.46% and its mean is +4.40% (a 6.86-point gap), with 72.7% of all upside movement arising from the top 4% of observations.
costs: FINRA Trading Activity Fee (TAF), effective 1 Jan 2026: $0.000195 per share on each sale of a covered equity security, capped at $9.79 per trade; options $0.00329 per contract. Applies to the sale side, so every short entry pays it.

SEC Section 31 fee: $0.00 per million for covered sales through 3 April 2026, then $20.60 per million from 4 April 2026 (FY2026 rate; SEC Fee Rate Advisory / FINRA Information Notice 03/17/26). Security futures assessment unchanged at $0.0042 per round turn.

IBKR Pro Fixed US stock commission: $0.005/share, $1.00 minimum per order, capped at 1% of trade value. IBKR Pro Tiered: $0.0035/share at the base tier scaling to $0.0005/share, $0.35 minimum, with exchange, clearing and regulatory fees passed through separately. [Secondary sources — IBKR's own pricing pages returned HTTP 403; verify against interactivebrokers.com/en/pricing before use.]
IBKR US options: approximately $0.65/contract on the fixed plan; tiered with limit orders can be below that and occasionally negative after exchange rebates. [Secondary source — verify.]

Stock borrow fees: roughly 0.25%/yr for easy-to-borrow; 5%–50%/yr typical hard-to-borrow; 100%+/yr for names in an active squeeze; 1,000%+/yr in extremis. Fees accrue daily on collateral. [Secondary sources — always price against your broker's live indicative rate.]

Effective borrow cost after the 102%/round-up-to-$1 collateral rule, at a 100%/yr quoted rate: $0.50 stock → 200%/yr effective on notional = 33.3% of notional over a 60-day hold, 100% over six months; $2.01 stock → 149%/yr = 24.9% over 60 days; $4.01 stock → 125%/yr = 20.8% over 60 days.

Cost of the capping call (Black-Scholes, S=100, r=4%, no dividend; IVs are a modeling assumption — verify live per name): 60-day 35%-OTM call = 3.71% of spot at 80% IV, 9.30% at 120% IV, 15.58% at 160% IV. 60-day 50%-OTM call = 2.07% / 6.77% / 12.67%.

Cost of the put expression: 60-day ATM put = 12.52% of spot at 80% IV, 18.83% at 120% IV, 25.02% at 160% IV. A 60-day 100/80 put spread costs 42% of its width at 80% IV, 50% at 120% IV, 56% at 160% IV — i.e. at realistic micro-cap IVs you are paying about half the width for the whole payoff range.

Ortex short-interest and borrow data: Basic $39/month ($348/yr), Advanced $129/month ($948/yr) with real-time short interest and options data; API subscriptions from $499/month. S3 Partners does not publish retail pricing — enterprise only, also distributed via Bloomberg Data License. [Secondary sources — confirm current pricing directly.]

Simulated cost of the hedge in portfolio terms (25 names, 100% gross, 60-day hold, 25%/yr borrow, 35%-OTM call at 120% IV): mean P&L moves from −8.30% naked to −11.87% hedged, while p01 improves from −65.51% to −18.00% and the worst case from −4,418% to −24.5%. The hedge costs roughly 3.6 points of mean per period and buys a bounded loss.

execution.topic: The full cost stack for a small US equity/options trader, sized for short-biased and event-driven trades in $0.50–$5 US small/micro caps (PLUG, BYND, CGC, SPCE, HYZN-type names), plus ETF/event trades — commissions, regulatory/exchange fees, routing, spread and impact, borrow, options frictions, and the tax layer. Figures verified against primary sources as of 2026-08-13.

practices.practice: Price the trade off the borrow COLLATERAL, not the notional — IBKR marks short collateral at 102% of prior close rounded UP to the nearest whole dollar, $1.00 minimum
practices.detail: Verified verbatim on IBKR's own interest-rate page: 'Collateral Balance = (stock A prior day closing price x 102%, rounded up to the nearest 1.00) x (number of shares).' Daily fee = (Collateral x FeeRate)/360 (360-day count, per IBKR's Borrow Fee Details guide). For sub-$5 names this rounding is not a rounding error, it is a multiplier: $0.55 -> $1.00 collateral = 1.82x notional; $0.99 -> $2.00 = 2.02x; $1.05 -> $2.00 = 1.90x; $2.00 -> $3.00 = 1.50x; $3.50 -> $4.00 = 1.14x; $10 -> $11 = 1.10x. So a quoted 60% borrow on a $0.55 stock costs 109% annualized on notional; a quoted 40% on a $1.05 stock costs 76%. ALWAYS multiply the screen rate by ceil(1.02*px)/px before it enters a P&L model. The function is a sawtooth — worst just above each whole dollar ($0.99-$1.02 is the single worst zone in the whole range at ~2.0x).

practices.practice: Trade the $2.50–$5.00 band, not the $0.30–$1.00 band; the all-in cost differs by ~7x for the same dollar notional
practices.detail: Computed all-in (passive fills, IBKR Pro Tiered, 10-day hold, ex-spread, ex-impact) for a ~$22-25k short: $0.55 name @60% borrow = 4.42% of notional. $1.05 name @40% = 2.54%. $3.50 name @15% = 0.60%. Breakeven quoted borrow for a 10-day hold against a 3.0% gross edge: $0.55 -> 32%, $0.99 -> 40%, $1.05 -> 49%, $1.50 -> 73%, $2.50 -> 85%, $3.50 -> 91%. Max hold-days before cost eats a 3.0% edge: 5.3 days at $0.55/60%, 12.2 days at $1.05/40%, 60 days at $3.50/15%. The cheapest names carry the largest gross edge in the FTD panel (-3.03% under $1 vs -1.11% at $3-5) but the cost curve is steeper than the edge curve — net, the $3-5 band is the only part of the range that survives.

practices.practice: Post, do not take. Passive vs aggressive routing is the largest single controllable execution cost — larger than the commission itself
practices.detail: Cboe BZX (verified fee schedule): securities >= $1.00 pay $0.0030/share to remove, receive $0.0016/share rebate to add — a $0.0046/share swing, versus an IBKR Pro Tiered commission of only $0.0035/share. Sub-$1.00: BZX charges 0.30% of dollar value to remove and is FREE to add (no rebate, no fee); BYX charges only 0.10% to remove. Worked example, 20,000 sh of a $1.05 name: round-trip fees $272.56 (1.30%) taking liquidity vs $88.56 (0.42%) adding — a 88bp round-trip saving on a strategy whose median edge is ~1-3%. Rule: default to limit orders resting on BZX/EDGX (rebate) or IEX/BYX; use IBKR Tiered so the rebate is actually passed through — Fixed pricing does not credit exchange rebates.

practices.practice: Use IBKR Pro TIERED, never Fixed, for anything under $5, and never a $0-commission PFOF broker for this book
practices.detail: IBKR US stocks (verified on interactivebrokers.com/en/pricing/commissions-stocks.php): Tiered <=300k sh/mo = $0.0035/share, min $0.35/order, max 1% of trade value; Fixed = $0.005/share, min $1.00/order, max 1% of trade value. Tiered adds NSCC/DTC clearing $0.00020/share and passes exchange fees/rebates through; Fixed swallows the rebate. On a $0.55 stock the per-share rate alone is 0.64% (Tiered) vs 0.91% (Fixed) ONE WAY. IBKR's own worked example confirms the 1% cap binds: '1,000 Shares @ USD 0.25 Share Price = USD 5.00' becomes USD 2.50. Zero-commission brokers are worse here, not better: you cannot choose the venue, cannot capture the add rebate, cannot avoid the 0.30% sub-dollar take fee, and Schwab charges $6.95/trade for OTC equities anyway.

practices.practice: Budget market impact separately using the square-root law — it is invisible on every fee schedule and dominates at $25k+ in thin names
practices.detail: Impact ~ sigma * sqrt(Q/V) where sigma = daily vol, Q/V = participation rate. For a micro cap with $2M/day dollar volume and 8% daily vol: $5,000 order = 0.25% participation -> 40bp impact; $25,000 -> 1.25% -> 89bp; $50,000 -> 2.50% -> 126bp. For a $10M/day name at 6% vol: $5k -> 13bp, $25k -> 30bp, $50k -> 42bp. Practical rule: cap any single order at 1% of 20-day median dollar volume (keeps impact under ~70bp for these vol levels), and require ADV >= $3M before the name is tradeable at $25k clip size. Slice with TWAP/VWAP across 30-60 minutes rather than a single print.

practices.practice: Recognize that the minimum tick is a hard floor on spread cost in the $1.00–$3.00 band, and that sub-$1 names are NOT tick-constrained
practices.detail: Rule 612: minimum increment is $0.01 for quotes at or above $1.00, but $0.0001 for quotes below $1.00. So a $1.05 stock has a mathematically minimum spread of 0.95% (half-spread 48bp per side) and a $1.50 stock 0.67%; a $0.55 stock can legally quote in hundredths of a cent and often shows a much tighter percentage spread — but with trivial displayed size, so you pay in impact instead. The $1.00-$2.00 band is the worst of both worlds: tick-constrained AND high borrow multiplier AND $2.50/share margin. The half-penny tick amendment to Rule 612 (which would help exactly these tick-constrained names) and the Rule 610(c) access-fee cap cut from $0.0030 to $0.0010 were both delayed by SEC exemptive order (Oct 31, 2025) to the first business day of November 2026 — i.e. Nov 2, 2026 — and SIFMA has requested a further extension. Do not model the 10-mil cap as live today; BZX still charges $0.0030.

practices.practice: Run index/beta hedges through Section 1256 instruments (SPX, /ES, RUT, NDX, VIX, XSP), never SPY or IWM
practices.detail: Section 1256 contracts (US futures, options on futures, options on broad-based indices) get automatic 60/40 treatment regardless of holding period plus year-end mark-to-market. Blended top federal rate is 26.8% (60% x 20% + 40% x 37%) versus 37% ordinary + 3.8% NIIT = 40.8% for short-term equity gains — roughly a 14-point swing on the hedge leg. Options on SPY/IWM ETFs are securities options and get NO 1256 treatment even though they track the same index. 1256 also marks to market at 12/31, which sidesteps wash-sale bookkeeping entirely on that sleeve and permits a 3-year carryback of net 1256 losses against prior 1256 gains.

practices.practice: Assume every dollar of equity short profit is taxed at the top ordinary rate, and size the gross edge accordingly
practices.detail: Gain on a short sale is short-term capital gain essentially by construction (IRC 1233) — there is no holding-period path to long-term rates on a short. 2026 top federal ordinary rate is 37% (permanent post-TCJA, applying above ~$640,600 single / ~$768,700 MFJ) plus the 3.8% NIIT above $200k/$250k MAGI = 40.8% federal, before state. A 3.0% gross edge is a ~1.78% after-federal-tax edge at the top bracket. Combined with a 4.42% all-in cost on a $0.55 name, the sub-$1 sleeve is not marginally unprofitable — it is unprofitable by a wide margin.

practices.practice: Make the Section 475(f) mark-to-market election a live decision if the book turns over frequently, and know the deadline is absolute
practices.detail: For an existing individual taxpayer, the 475(f) election statement must be filed by the UNEXTENDED due date of the PRIOR year's return — i.e. an election effective for tax year 2026 had to be filed by April 15, 2026 with the 2025 return or extension request; for tax year 2027 the deadline is April 15, 2027. Multiple sources state there is no 9100 relief for individuals who miss it. Benefits for a high-turnover short book: wash-sale rules do not apply, the $3,000 net capital loss cap does not apply (losses become ordinary on Form 4797), and open positions mark at 12/31. Cost: you forfeit long-term capital gain rates — irrelevant for a book whose gains are all short-term anyway. Requires Trader Tax Status, which is a facts-and-circumstances determination, not an election. NOTE (UNVERIFIED): one secondary source claims the July 2025 OBBBA further changed 475 loss treatment starting TY2026; I could not confirm this against primary law — verify with a CPA before relying on it.

practices.practice: Keep short holding periods above 45 days OR avoid dividend payers entirely, because of IRC 263(h)
practices.detail: Payments in lieu of dividends on a short held 45 days or less are NOT deductible — they must be capitalized into the basis of the stock used to close the short. Held more than 45 days, the substitute payment becomes deductible as investment interest expense, which is itself limited by IRC 163(d) to net investment income and requires itemizing. The 45-day window extends to one year for extraordinary dividends. For a book of 5-15 day event trades, this means any dividend paid during the hold is a pure, non-deductible economic cost. Screen the ex-dividend calendar before initiating and simply avoid names going ex during the intended hold.

practices.practice: Reconcile the actual borrow charge on the daily activity statement, because the quoted rate is only indicative
practices.detail: IBKR states the fee rate shown in the TWS fee-rate column is 'indicative'; the 'actual borrow fee rate is determined after market close and will be available on your activity statement.' You cannot lock the cost of an open HTB short. The only way to fix the rate is a pre-borrow, which at IBKR carries a $10,000 minimum order value and uses the same 102%/round-up-to-$1.00 collateral convention. Build a daily reconciliation that pulls the Borrow Fee Details section of the Activity Statement (via Flex Query) and flags any position whose realized rate exceeded the rate assumed at entry by more than, say, 25% relative.

practices.practice: Treat any stock/option hedge on the same name as a straddle under IRC 1092, and never short a name you already hold long at a gain
practices.detail: The natural response to this book's negative skew — shorting the stock and buying calls as tail protection — creates a straddle under Section 1092: the loss on the losing leg is deferred to the extent of unrecognized gain on the offsetting leg, and holding periods are modified. Separately, IRC 1259 constructive-sale rules fire if you short a stock (or substantially identical property) while holding an appreciated long position in it, forcing immediate gain recognition on the long. If the ETF/event sleeve and the short sleeve can ever touch the same underlying, you need a position-level check before the order goes in, not at tax time.

practices.practice: Verify the current regulatory-fee rates each quarter — the Section 31 rate is not a constant and was literally zero for part of FY2026
practices.detail: SEC Section 31 fee: $0.00 per million for covered sales through April 3, 2026, then $20.60 per million (i.e. $0.0000206 x sales value) from April 4, 2026, per SEC Fee Rate Advisory (announced Feb 27, 2026) and FINRA Information Notice 03/17/26; it remains in effect until 60 days after FY2027 appropriations legislation. Security futures assessment stays $0.0042 per round turn. FINRA TAF rose Jan 1, 2026 to $0.000195/share on equity sales with a per-transaction cap of $9.79 (from $0.000166 / $8.30), and $0.00329/contract on option sales (from $0.00279). Both are sell-side only. Note the FINRA rulebook web page for Schedule A Section 1 still displayed the OLD $0.000166/$8.30/$0.00279 figures when fetched — the current rates are confirmed by tastytrade's fee schedule (updated July 30, 2026) and IBKR's live commission pages. Trust broker schedules and FINRA notices over the rulebook page.

pitfalls.pitfall: Modelling borrow cost as (quoted rate x notional), which understates the true cost by 1.1x to 3.3x on exactly the names this strategy targets
pitfalls.mitigation: Apply the collateral multiplier ceil(1.02 * prior_close)/prior_close to every quoted rate. Hard-code the table: <$0.98 -> collateral $1.00/sh; $0.99-$1.96 -> $2.00/sh; $1.97-$2.94 -> $3.00/sh; $2.95-$3.92 -> $4.00/sh; $3.93-$4.90 -> $5.00/sh. Reject any candidate where quoted_rate * multiplier * (days/360) exceeds 40% of the modelled gross edge. The multiplier also drifts daily with the mark, so recompute nightly.

pitfalls.pitfall: The $2.50/share maintenance margin floor on sub-$5 shorts destroys return on capital before any cost is even counted
pitfalls.mitigation: FINRA Rule 4210 maintenance for a short equity under $5.00 is the GREATER of $2.50/share or 100% of market value (and $5.00/share or 30% of market value at or above $5.00). Shorting 40,000 shares of a $0.55 stock ($22,000 notional) requires $100,000 of maintenance margin — 4.5x notional. A $1.05 name requires 2.4x. This means a $100k account holds ONE such position, and a 3% winner returns 0.66% on deployed capital gross, which is less than the 4.42% all-in cost. Size the book on MARGIN CONSUMED, not notional, and price the strategy's capacity off $2.50/share. Above $2.50/share stock price the constraint stops binding, which is another reason to live in the $2.50-$5 band. Verify whether your broker's portfolio-margin regime changes this before assuming it does.

pitfalls.pitfall: Rule 201 (SSR) blocks you from taking liquidity to get short on precisely the days the thesis is working
pitfalls.mitigation: A 10% intraday decline from the prior close triggers the short-sale price test for the remainder of that day AND the following day: short orders may not be executed or displayed at or below the current national best bid. Chronic-failer decay and event-driven shorts concentrate their moves on exactly these days. Consequence: on trigger days you can only post above the bid and hope to be lifted — expect materially lower fill rates and adverse selection, not the modelled fill. Backtests that assume a fill at the bid or at VWAP on down-10% days are structurally optimistic. Build an SSR flag into the backtest and either exclude SSR days from entry or model a passive-only fill with a realistic non-fill rate.

pitfalls.pitfall: Recall and forced buy-in on hard-to-borrow names is the fat positive tail against the short, and it is not something you can hedge with a stop
pitfalls.mitigation: Under Reg SHO Rule 204, a participant must close out a fail-to-deliver by the beginning of regular trading hours on the settlement day following the settlement date (under T+1, that is the T+2 open); a market-maker fail from bona fide market making gets until T+3, and certain long-sale/deemed-to-own fails get 35 calendar days. If the clearing broker misses the deadline, the firm enters the 'penalty box' — it and every broker it clears for may not accept further short orders in that security without a bona fide pre-borrow. Practical exposure: your position can be bought in at market with no notice, at the worst possible price, in exactly the squeeze scenario. Mitigations: pre-borrow (IBKR $10k minimum) for any position you must hold; prefer names NOT on the daily threshold securities list (fails >= 10,000 shares AND >= 0.5% of shares outstanding for 5 consecutive settlement days) unless the fail IS the thesis; cap single-name notional so a 100% adverse gap is survivable; and express the highest-conviction, highest-borrow ideas as long puts instead of short stock.

pitfalls.pitfall: Options on $0.50–$5 underlyings look like the fix for negative skew, but the round-trip spread is 10–35% of premium and swamps the edge
pitfalls.mitigation: Under the Penny Interval Program the minimum increment is $0.01 for series priced under $3.00 and $0.05 above, but only for the ~300 most active multiply-listed classes (reviewed annually over a Jun 1-Nov 30 window; exchanges publish adds via Nasdaq Options Trader Alerts and MIAX notices). Non-penny classes quote in $0.05 under $3.00 and $0.10 above. A $0.30 put in a NON-penny class quoted 0.25/0.35 costs ~33% of premium round trip; a penny-class put quoted 0.28/0.32 still costs ~13%. Add commissions: IBKR Pro Tiered is $0.65/contract for premium >= $0.10, $0.50 for >= $0.05, $0.25 below $0.05, with a $1.00 per-order minimum — so a 1-lot on a $0.20 option is $1.00 = 5% of premium each way. Before treating defined-risk puts as the answer to the FTD question, measure the actual NBBO width and the IV-vs-realized-drift gap on the specific chains; the structural presumption is that the market maker is charging more for the skew than the signal is worth.

pitfalls.pitfall: Direct-routing options at IBKR costs $1.00/contract instead of $0.65 — the opposite of the equities lesson
pitfalls.mitigation: IBKR's options schedule states plainly: 'Direct routed orders are charged USD 1.00/contract on all option premiums.' Use SMART routing for options. The equities logic (route direct to capture the add rebate) does NOT carry over. Also note IBKR charges no commission for US exercise and assignment, and no commission for US cabinet buy-to-close trades where the minimum tick exceeds $0.01.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assignment of a short option leg in a hard-to-borrow name silently converts a defined-risk position into an unhedged short at a punitive borrow
pitfalls.mitigation: An assigned short call leaves you short the stock — at that moment you inherit the full borrow cost with its collateral multiplier, the $2.50/share margin floor, and the Rule 204 buy-in exposure, none of which were in the defined-risk P&L. Check exercise/assignment fees too, they are not uniform: IBKR $0 (no commission on US exercise/assignment), Schwab $0 online, Fidelity $0, tastytrade $5 per exercise/assignment. Operationally: close short option legs before expiration in any HTB name rather than letting them go to assignment, and never carry a short call into an ex-dividend date or expiry in a name you cannot borrow.

pitfalls.pitfall: Wash sales apply to SHORT sales too, and a high-turnover short book in a small universe generates them constantly
pitfalls.mitigation: The wash-sale rule reaches a loss on a short sale if you enter another short sale of substantially identical stock within 30 days before or 30 days after the date the short sale is complete (IRS Pub 550; IRC 1091). A systematic strategy that re-shorts the same chronic-failer universe every few weeks will disallow losses and roll them into basis, producing a taxable gain far larger than the economic gain — the classic phantom-income blowup. Options on the same name can also trigger it. Two mitigations: (a) make the 475(f) MTM election, which removes wash-sale treatment entirely; or (b) enforce a hard 31-day cooldown per ticker after any losing exit, which materially reduces strategy capacity — model that capacity loss explicitly.

pitfalls.pitfall: Treating the sub-$1 exchange fee as a per-share fee when it is a percentage of dollar value
pitfalls.mitigation: For securities below $1.00 the fee schedules switch to a percentage basis: BZX charges 0.30% of total dollar value to remove liquidity (free to add); BYX charges 0.10% to remove; NYSE charges 0.30% for most executions and 0.08% for orders routed to NYSE American. On a $0.55 stock, 0.30% = $0.00165/share, roughly half the entire Tiered commission, and it does NOT scale down as the price falls. Route sub-dollar takes to BYX where possible, or post and pay nothing.

pitfalls.pitfall: Small account size silently forfeits the short rebate and pays the worst margin rate, adding a hidden spread to every position
pitfalls.mitigation: IBKR pays interest on USD cash balances only above $10,000, and clients with NAV under $100,000 'receive a lower annual rate' that scales up toward the full rate as NAV approaches $100k. Short-sale proceeds collateral is part of this calculation. So a sub-$100k account earns little or nothing on the short credit while still paying the full borrow fee — the rebate side of the trade is simply gone. Margin side: IBKR Pro margin begins at benchmark + 1.5% with lower spreads at higher balances, versus IBKR Lite at benchmark + 2.5%; cash interest is benchmark - 0.5% (Pro) vs benchmark - 1.5% (Lite). Never run this book on IBKR Lite. Assume zero short rebate in every model until NAV clears $100k.

pitfalls.pitfall: Backtesting against a 3% edge while ignoring that fees, spread, impact, borrow and tax are five separate deductions that compound
pitfalls.mitigation: Stack them explicitly for a representative $1.05 name, 20,000 shares, 10-day hold, passive fills: exchange/commission/regulatory round trip 0.42%, borrow 2.12%, minimum-tick half-spread cost if forced to cross 0.95% round trip, market impact at 1.25% participation 0.89%, = 4.38% pre-tax against a 3.0% gross edge — negative before the 40.8% tax on any gain that does survive. Publish this five-line stack next to every backtest Sharpe. The FTD panel's own finding that breakeven annualized borrow is 25-55% is corroborated and sharpened by this: computed breakeven QUOTED borrow for a 10-day hold at a 3% edge is 32% at $0.55 and 49% at $1.05 — right in the middle of the range actual HTB fees occupy, meaning the trade is a coin flip on borrow alone.

pitfalls.pitfall: Relying on the FINRA rulebook web page or stale broker help articles for current fee rates
pitfalls.mitigation: The FINRA rulebook page for Schedule A Section 1 returned the superseded TAF rates ($0.000166/share, $8.30 cap, $0.00279/contract) when fetched on 2026-08-13. Similarly, IBKR help content still describes short-sale settlement as 'generally 2 business days' despite T+1 having been in force since May 28, 2024. Use as authoritative sources, in order: the live broker commission pages (interactivebrokers.com/en/pricing/commissions-stocks.php and commissions-options.php), the tastytrade Commissions & Fees PDF (dated, currently 'Last updated July 30, 2026'), SEC Fee Rate Advisories at sec.gov/rules-regulations/fee-rate-advisories, FINRA Information Notices, and the exchange fee schedules at cboe.com/us/equities/membership/fee_schedule/{bzx,byx,edgx}/ and nyse.com/publicdocs/nyse/markets/nyse/NYSE_Price_List.pdf.

concrete_specs: IBKR short collateral formula (verified on IBKR interest-rates page): Collateral = (prior day close x 102%, rounded UP to nearest $1.00, $1.00 minimum) x shares. Daily borrow fee = (Collateral x FeeRate) / 360.
Effective borrow on notional = quoted rate x multiplier. Quoted 60% on a $0.55 name = 109% annualized. Quoted 40% on a $1.05 name = 76%. Quoted 15% on a $3.50 name = 17%.

IBKR US stocks, IBKR Pro Tiered: $0.0035/share for <=300,000 sh/month; $0.0020 for 300,001-3,000,000; $0.0015 for 3,000,001-20,000,000; $0.0010 to 100,000,000; $0.0005 above. Minimum $0.35/order, maximum 1% of trade value. Marginal within a calendar month.
IBKR US stocks, IBKR Pro Fixed: $0.005/share, minimum $1.00/order, maximum 1% of trade value. IBKR's own example: 1,000 shares @ $0.25 = $2.50 (the 1% cap binds, not the per-share rate).

IBKR Tiered pass-throughs on US stocks: NSCC/DTC clearing $0.00020/share; SEC fee $0.0000206 x sale value; FINRA TAF $0.000195 x shares sold (cap $9.79/trade); FINRA CAT $0.000003 x shares; NYSE pass-through = commission x 0.000175; FINRA pass-through = commission x 0.00056.

Cboe BZX equities, securities >= $1.00: remove liquidity $0.0030/share, add liquidity rebate $0.0016/share (net swing $0.0046/share). Securities < $1.00: remove 0.30% of dollar value, add FREE. Cboe BYX removes sub-$1 at only 0.10% of dollar value — route sub-dollar takes there.
NYSE sub-$1.00 pricing: 0.08% of dollar value for orders routed to NYSE American, $0.0010/share for Away Market Auction executions elsewhere, 0.30% of dollar value for all other executions.

SEC Section 31 fee: $0.00 per million through April 3, 2026; $20.60 per million ($0.0000206 x sale value) from April 4, 2026, per SEC Fee Rate Advisory 2026-2 (announced Feb 27, 2026) and FINRA Information Notice 03/17/26. Security futures assessment unchanged at $0.0042 per round turn. Sell-side only. Rate persists until 60 days after FY2027 appropriations.

FINRA TAF from Jan 1, 2026: equities $0.000195/share sold, cap $9.79 per transaction (was $0.000166 / $8.30); options $0.00329/contract sold (was $0.00279); debt $0.00124/bond, cap $1.24. Sell-side only.

OCC clearing fee: $0.025/contract, all contracts (per IBKR options page, 2026). OCC has periodically declared monthly fee holidays (e.g. Dec 1-31, 2025) — check infomemo.theocc.com before assuming it is being charged.

Cboe Options ORF: $0.0023 per contract side through June 30, 2026; $0.0017 per contract side from July 1, 2026. Cboe BZX Options and EDGX Options $0.0002/contract; C2 Options $0.0003/contract (effective Jan 2, 2026). From July 1, 2026 Cboe moved to an on-exchange assessment model (ORF charged on executions occurring on Cboe, cleared in the customer range at OCC).

IBKR US options, Pro Tiered, <=10,000 contracts/month: $0.65/contract for premium >= $0.10; $0.50/contract for premium >= $0.05; $0.25/contract for premium < $0.05. 10,001-50,000/mo: $0.50 (>= $0.05 premium), $0.25 below. 50,001-100,000: $0.25 all premiums. >=100,001: $0.15 all premiums. Minimum $1.00 per order, applied per leg of a combo. Volume breaks are marginal within the month.

IBKR options third-party fees: SEC $0.0000206 x sale value, FINRA TAF $0.00329/contract sold, FINRA CAT $0.0003/contract, OCC clearing $0.025/contract, plus per-exchange ORF. IBKR Lite is $0.65/contract flat on the first 1,000 US contracts/month, then Pro Tiered applies.

IBKR direct-routed options are charged $1.00/contract on all premiums — always use SMART routing for options at IBKR. IBKR charges no commission for US exercise and assignment, and none for US cabinet buy-to-close where the minimum tick exceeds $0.01.

tastytrade (schedule dated July 30, 2026): equity options $1.00/contract to open, $0.00 to close, capped $10 per leg, plus $0.10/contract clearing. Stock $0 commission plus $0.0008/share clearing (= 0.15% one-way on a $0.55 stock — significant). Option exercise/assignment $5. ORF $0.02/contract. Futures $1.00/contract each way + $0.30 clearing; micro futures $0.75 + $0.30. Margin base rate 10%, debit balances $0-$24,999 charged 11.00%.

Exercise/assignment fees: IBKR $0, Schwab $0 online, Fidelity $0, tastytrade $5. Schwab's $25 is a broker-ASSISTED service charge, not an assignment fee. Schwab options $0.65/contract; OTC equities $6.95/trade online; foreign stock on OTC market $50 transaction fee.

FINRA Rule 4210 maintenance margin on shorts: greater of $2.50/share or 100% of market value for stock under $5.00; greater of $5.00/share or 30% of market value at or above $5.00. Shorting 40,000 sh of a $0.55 stock ($22,000 notional) ties up $100,000 = 4.5x notional. Size the book on margin consumed.

Market impact model: impact ~ sigma x sqrt(Q/V). Calibrated outputs for $2M ADV / 8% daily vol: $5k order -> 40bp; $25k -> 89bp; $50k -> 126bp. For $10M ADV / 6% vol: $5k -> 13bp; $25k -> 30bp; $50k -> 42bp. Operating rules: cap each order at 1% of 20-day median dollar volume; require ADV >= $3M for a $25k clip; slice over 30-60 minutes.
Minimum tick (Rule 612): $0.01 at or above $1.00, $0.0001 below $1.00. Minimum possible spread: $1.05 stock = 0.95% (48bp half-spread); $1.50 = 0.67%; $2.50 = 0.40%; $3.50 = 0.29%; $5.00 = 0.20%.

Half-penny tick (Rule 612 amendment) and the Rule 610(c) access-fee cap cut from $0.0030 to $0.0010 were delayed by SEC exemptive order dated Oct 31, 2025 to the first business day of November 2026 (Nov 2, 2026); SIFMA has requested further extension pending the Rule 611 review. Odd-lot information dissemination compliance date was May 4, 2026. The D.C. Circuit denied challenges to the amendments on Oct 14, 2025.

Rule 201 (SSR): triggers on a 10% intraday decline from the prior day's official closing price; short sales may not be executed or displayed at or below the national best bid for the remainder of that day and the following day.

Reg SHO Rule 204: fails to deliver must be closed out by the beginning of regular trading hours on the settlement day following the settlement date (T+2 open under T+1 settlement); bona fide market-maker fails get until T+3; deemed-to-own/long-sale fails under 204(a)(2) get until the 35th consecutive calendar day after trade date. Missing the deadline puts the participant and all brokers it clears for into a mandatory pre-borrow requirement for that security.

IBKR pre-borrow: $10,000 minimum order value; collateral = 102% x mark rounded up to nearest $1.00 ($1.00 minimum); the TWS fee-rate column is INDICATIVE only — the actual rate is set after market close and appears on the Activity Statement.

IBKR interest: no interest paid on the first $10,000 of cash; accounts with NAV under $100,000 receive a reduced rate scaling up toward the full rate at $100k. IBKR Pro margin begins at benchmark + 1.5% (lower at higher balances); IBKR Lite is benchmark + 2.5%. Cash interest: Pro = benchmark - 0.5%, Lite = benchmark - 1.5%. Site-quoted headline rates on 2026-08-13: 4.13% margin, 3.13% on uninvested cash.

Tax rates 2026: short-term capital gains taxed as ordinary income, top federal rate 37% (above ~$640,600 single / ~$768,700 MFJ), plus 3.8% NIIT above $200k single / $250k MFJ MAGI = 40.8% federal. Section 1256 blended 60/40 top rate = 26.8%. Net capital loss offsets ordinary income only up to $3,000/year ($1,500 MFS).

Section 1256 qualifying instruments: US futures, options on futures, and options on BROAD-BASED indices — SPX, NDX, RUT, DJX, VIX, XSP. Options on SPY/IWM ETFs do NOT qualify. 1256 positions open at 12/31 are marked to market; net 1256 losses may be carried back 3 years against prior 1256 gains.

IRC 263(h): payments in lieu of dividends on a short held 45 days or less are non-deductible and must be capitalized into the basis of the closing stock; over 45 days they are deductible as investment interest expense, limited by IRC 163(d) to net investment income. Window extends to 1 year for extraordinary dividends.

IRC 1091 wash sales apply to short sales: a loss is disallowed if you enter another short sale of substantially identical stock within 30 days before or 30 days after the date the short sale is complete. Disallowed loss rolls into the basis of the replacement position (1091(d)).

Section 475(f) MTM election deadline: unextended due date of the PRIOR year's return — April 15, 2026 for tax year 2026, April 15, 2027 for tax year 2027. No 9100 relief for individuals. Requires Trader Tax Status (facts and circumstances, not elected). Removes wash-sale treatment and the $3,000 capital loss cap; gains/losses become ordinary on Form 4797.

IRC 1259 constructive sale fires when you short (or enter an offsetting NPC/forward on) the same or substantially identical property while holding an appreciated long position — forces immediate gain recognition. IRC 1092 straddle rules defer losses on one leg to the extent of unrecognized gain on the offsetting leg (short stock + long calls on the same name is a straddle).

PFOF reference rates: Schwab Q4 2025 Rule 606 report disclosed marketable equity orders at $0.001/share or less, non-marketable at $0.0033/share or less, extended-hours at $0.0006/share or less. Source for cross-checking routing economics: citadelsecurities.com/rule-605-606-statements/ and the FINRA 606 CDN at cdn.finra.org/606/.

Verification endpoints to re-check quarterly: interactivebrokers.com/en/pricing/commissions-stocks.php and /commissions-options.php; interactivebrokers.com/en/trading/short-securities-availability.php (live borrow rates and availability); ibkrguides.com/reportingreference/reportguide/borrowfeedetails.htm (borrow fee formula); cboe.com/us/equities/membership/fee_schedule/{bzx,byx,edgx}/; nyse.com/publicdocs/nyse/markets/nyse/NYSE_Price_List.pdf; sec.gov/rules-regulations/fee-rate-advisories; nasdaqtrader.com Options Trader Alerts (penny program adds); theocc.com/company-information/schedule-of-fees and infomemo.theocc.com.

NOTE — these figures were NOT verified and must be checked before use: live per-ticker borrow rates for PLUG/BYND/CGC/SPCE/HYZN (time-varying; IBKR's public FTP file at ftp3.interactivebrokers.com/usa.txt was unreachable through this environment's proxy — pull it from an unproxied host or use the IBKR shortable-instruments search); Cobra Trading (~$0.003/share falling to $0.002, ~$27,000 minimum) and CenterPoint Securities (Pro platform ~$138/month, ~$30,000 minimum, reported 3x overnight locate multiplier) pricing, which came from secondary review sites rather than the brokers' own schedules; and the claim that the July 2025 OBBBA changed Section 475 loss treatment for TY2026.
costs: Worked example A — short 20,000 sh @ $1.05 ($21,000 notional), 10-day hold, IBKR Pro Tiered, quoted borrow 40%: round-trip fees $272.56 (1.298%) taking liquidity, or $88.56 (0.422%) adding liquidity. Borrow: collateral $40,000 (1.90x notional), $44.44/day, $444.44 over 10 days = 2.116% of notional = 76.2% annualized on notional. ALL-IN with passive fills, before spread and impact: $533.00 = 2.54% of notional. Maintenance margin $50,000 (2.4x notional).

Worked example B — short 40,000 sh @ $0.55 ($22,000 notional), 10-day hold, quoted borrow 60%: round-trip fees $436.70 (1.985%) taking, $304.70 (1.385%) adding. Borrow: collateral $40,000 (1.82x notional), $66.67/day, $666.67 over 10 days = 3.030% of notional = 109.1% annualized on notional. ALL-IN passive: $971.37 = 4.42% of notional. Maintenance margin $100,000 (4.5x notional). This trade cannot clear a 3% edge.

Worked example C — short 7,000 sh @ $3.50 ($24,500 notional), 10-day hold, quoted borrow 15%: round-trip fees $95.75 (0.391%) taking, $31.35 (0.128%) adding. Borrow: collateral $28,000 (1.14x notional), $11.67/day, $116.67 over 10 days = 0.476% = 17.1% annualized on notional. ALL-IN passive: $148.01 = 0.60% of notional. Maintenance margin $24,500 (1.0x notional). Roughly 7x cheaper than example B for the same dollar notional.

Breakeven QUOTED borrow rate for a 10-day hold against a 3.0% gross edge, passive fills, IBKR Tiered: $0.55 -> 32.0%; $0.99 -> 39.7%; $1.05 -> 48.7%; $1.50 -> 73.0%; $2.50 -> 84.7%; $3.50 -> 90.5%; $5.00 -> 87.3%.

Maximum hold in calendar days before all-in cost consumes a 3.0% gross edge (passive fills): $0.55 @60% borrow = 5.3 days; $0.99 @60% = 6.6 days; $1.05 @40% = 12.2 days; $1.50 @40% = 18.3 days; $2.50 @25% = 33.9 days; $3.50 @15% = 60.3 days; $5.00 @10% = 87.3 days.

Full five-line stack for a representative $1.05 name, 20,000 sh, 10 days: fees/commissions/regulatory (passive) 0.42% + borrow 2.12% + minimum-tick spread if forced to cross 0.95% + market impact at 1.25% participation 0.89% = 4.38% pre-tax, against a 3.0% gross edge; any surviving gain is then taxed at up to 40.8% federal as short-term.

Passive-vs-aggressive routing value: $0.0046/share swing on securities >= $1.00 at Cboe BZX ($0.0030 take vs $0.0016 add rebate), which exceeds the entire $0.0035/share IBKR Tiered commission. Worth ~88bp round trip on a 20,000-share $1.05 position.

Regulatory fee run-rate on a $25,000 sale of a $1.00 stock (25,000 shares): SEC $0.52 + FINRA TAF $4.88 + CAT $0.08 = $5.48 total, or ~2.2bp — negligible relative to borrow, spread and impact. Regulatory fees are the smallest layer of this stack and are not where optimization effort belongs.

Options frictions on a $0.30-premium put: IBKR Pro Tiered $0.65/contract (premium >= $0.10) with a $1.00 order minimum, + OCC $0.025 + TAF $0.00329 on sells + CAT $0.0003 + ORF ~$0.0002-$0.0023. A 1-lot costs ~$1.03 to open = 3.4% of premium. The binding cost is the spread: ~13% of premium round trip in a penny-program class, ~33% in a non-penny class quoting $0.05 ticks.

Broker cost comparison for a $0.55 stock, one-way commission on 40,000 shares: IBKR Pro Tiered $140 (0.636%) + $8 clearing; IBKR Pro Fixed $200 (0.909%); tastytrade $0 commission but $32 clearing at $0.0008/share (0.145%); Schwab $6.95 flat if the name trades OTC. Per-share pricing is punitive sub-$1; flat-rate and per-value structures win there, but only IBKR Tiered gives venue control and rebate pass-through.

execution.topic: Building the data pipeline for FTD / Reg SHO / short-volume / filings-event signals on US small-and-micro-cap shorts (point-in-time storage, endpoints, rate limits, alerting)

practices.practice: Key every table bitemporally: (observation_date, knowledge_date) — never observation_date alone
practices.detail: knowledge_date = the moment YOU could first have known the row, taken from the HTTP Last-Modified header of the source file, not from the settlement/trade date inside it. Every backtest query becomes `WHERE observation_date <= :asof AND knowledge_date <= :asof`. Measured proof this matters: cnsfails202607a.zip contains settlement dates 2026-07-01 through 2026-07-14 but its Last-Modified is Thu, 30 Jul 2026 12:02:36 GMT. A naive join on settlement_date gives you 16-29 days of look-ahead on every single FTD row. cnsfails202606b.zip (settlements 06-16..06-30) Last-Modified Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:54:30 GMT confirms the pattern: 'a' file publishes ~end of same month, 'b' file publishes ~15th of next month.

practices.practice: Land raw bytes immutably before parsing; store sha256 + Last-Modified + fetch timestamp in a manifest
practices.detail: Schema: raw/{source}/{fetched_utc}/{filename}, plus a manifest row (source, url, http_status, etag, last_modified, sha256, bytes, fetched_utc). Re-parsing is then free and auditable, and you can detect silent restatements (FINRA revises short interest — the shrt20260715.csv file carries a revisionFlag='R' on 1 of 22,375 rows). Never overwrite a landed file; a new fetch with a different sha256 becomes a new knowledge_date row, which is exactly the restatement history you need.

practices.practice: Prefer the FINRA REST API over guessing cdn.finra.org filenames
practices.detail: cdn.finra.org returns HTTP 403 (not 404) for paths that don't exist, so filename guessing gives you false negatives that look like outages. Verified: https://cdn.finra.org/equity/otcmarket/biweekly/shrt20260731.csv returns 403 as of 2026-08-13, yet the identical 2026-07-31 settlement data IS available via POST https://api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/consolidatedShortInterest. Use the CDN only for the daily short-volume files (verified working) and the API for short interest and the OTC threshold list.

practices.practice: Poll EDGAR's getcurrent Atom feed for real-time events; use daily-index only for backfill and reconciliation
practices.detail: Measured latency on https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcurrent&type=8-K&count=40&output=atom: feed <updated> was 2026-08-13T12:45:15-04:00 with the newest entry at 12:44:14-04:00 — roughly 60 seconds behind acceptance. By contrast daily-index files land ~22:00-22:06 ET (index.json Last-Modified values: company.20260701.idx at '07/01/2026 10:01:47 PM', 20260812 sitemap at '08/12/2026 10:02:34 PM'). Poll getcurrent every 60s during 06:00-22:00 ET; reconcile against https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/daily-index/2026/QTR3/index.json the next morning and alert on any filing present in the index but missing from your event log.

practices.practice: Use the EDGAR full-text search JSON API for screening, and exploit the undocumented _source.items field for 8-K item codes
practices.detail: GET https://efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index?q=%22...%22&forms=8-K&startdt=YYYY-MM-DD&enddt=YYYY-MM-DD returns clean JSON. Each hit's _source carries ciks, display_names (with tickers), form, adsh (accession), file_date, sics, biz_states, AND items — the 8-K item list. Verified: q=%22Item%203.01%22&forms=8-K over 2026-08-01..2026-08-13 returned 33 hits with items arrays like ['3.01','7.01','9.01']. Item 3.01 (listing-rule non-compliance / delisting notice) is directly tradeable intel for a $0.5-$5 short book.

practices.practice: Take the union of all four SRO Reg SHO threshold lists daily — no single list covers your universe
practices.detail: Nasdaq covers Nasdaq-listed, NYSE covers NYSE/NYSE American/NYSE Arca, Cboe covers BZX/EDGX, FINRA covers OTC. A name like HYZN that migrates from Nasdaq to OTC disappears from the Nasdaq list entirely. Store as (trade_date, symbol, sro, threshold_flag) with a composite unique key so you can ask 'was X on ANY threshold list on date D' point-in-time.

practices.practice: Join FTD on CUSIP, not ticker — but persist both and build a CUSIP↔ticker history table
practices.detail: The FTD file's stable key is the 9-char CUSIP (column 2); SYMBOL (column 3) is a convenience field that changes on symbol changes and is blank/stale for some issues. Reverse splits change the CUSIP (verified via Nasdaq Equity Corporate Actions alerts, e.g. ECA2026-98 'Reverse Stock Split and CUSIP Number Change for Noodles & Company (NDLS)', ECA2026-94 for SMX). Maintain cusip_ticker_history(cusip, ticker, valid_from, valid_to) fed from daily snapshots of https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/dynamic/symdir/nasdaqtraded.txt and https://www.sec.gov/files/company_tickers_exchange.json. Without it, a reverse-split name silently splits into two unlinked FTD series and your chronic-fail day counts reset to zero.

practices.practice: Snapshot the tradable universe daily to kill survivorship bias in a short book
practices.detail: Persist nasdaqtraded.txt (verified 991,231 bytes, pipe-delimited, columns: Nasdaq Traded|Symbol|Security Name|Listing Exchange|Market Category|ETF|Round Lot Size|Test Issue|Financial Status|CQS Symbol|NASDAQ Symbol|NextShares) every trading day with a snapshot_date. The 'Financial Status' column flags deficient/delinquent issuers and the ETF column lets you exclude the leveraged single-stock ETF sludge (AMZD, BMNZ, AMKL, DAMD etc.) that now dominates threshold lists — verified, those made up a large share of the 2026-08-12 Nasdaq and Cboe threshold files. Shorting a 2x single-stock ETF is not the same trade as shorting a distressed micro-cap; filter them out at the universe layer, not in the strategy.

practices.practice: Treat the Nasdaq trade-halt RSS as a real-time risk kill-switch, not a data source
practices.detail: https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/rss.aspx?feed=tradehalts, ttl=1 (one minute). Verified schema fields: IssueSymbol, IssueName, Market, ReasonCode, HaltDate, HaltTime (ms precision), ResumptionDate, ResumptionQuoteTime, ResumptionTradeTime. Live sample 2026-08-13 had 49 items with reason codes LUDP:19, T12:13, T3:8, M:6, H11:2, T1:1. For a negative-skew short book LUDP (limit-up/limit-down volatility pause) is the fat tail arriving in real time — an LUDP halt on a name you are short is the single highest-value 30-second alert in the whole pipeline.

practices.practice: Snapshot borrow availability and fee daily and store it point-in-time — backtesting with today's borrow is look-ahead
practices.detail: IBKR publishes a public shortable-securities file (documented as ftp://shortstock:@ftp3.interactivebrokers.com/usa.txt, pipe-delimited, header #SYM|CUR|NAME|CON|ISIN|REBATERATE|FEERATE|AVAILABLE). UNVERIFIED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT — the FTP host was unreachable through the sandbox proxy (connection reset); confirm from your own network before relying on it. This matters more than any signal file: the prior FTD study in this repo computed a breakeven annualized borrow fee of only 25-55% for the chronic-fail signal, which is the same order as actual HTB fees on $0.5-$5 names. If you don't have a point-in-time FEERATE series, you cannot honestly backtest the strategy at all.

practices.practice: Rate-limit with a per-host token bucket and retry on 5xx, which occur even under the limit
practices.detail: SEC declares 10 requests/second across sec.gov and efts.sec.gov, with User-Agent, Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, and Host headers required. Verified empirically: 15 rapid sequential efts.sec.gov requests returned 200 fourteen times and 500 once — transient 500s are normal, not rate-limit signals. Implement a 150ms inter-request delay (≈6.7 rps, comfortably under 10), exponential backoff with jitter on 5xx, and 3 retries. There is no X-RateLimit response header to observe; the only failure signal is a sudden 403.

practices.practice: Set a real, identifying User-Agent on every SEC request or you get 403
practices.detail: SEC's declared format is 'Sample Company Name AdminContact@<domain>.com'. Use e.g. 'MB Research maxwellbilodeau@gmail.com'. The existing fetch_ftd.sh in this repo already does this via $SEC_UA. Nasdaq, FINRA CDN, Cboe and MSHA did not require a UA in testing, but send one anyway so you're identifiable if you need to ask for access back.

practices.practice: Pull MSHA weekly on Saturday and diff against the prior snapshot rather than reprocessing 150MB
practices.detail: Verified: files at https://arlweb.msha.gov/OpenGovernmentData/DataSets/ are refreshed Friday afternoons — Violations.zip (151,035,097 bytes), Inspections.zip (73,234,290), Accidents.zip (55,049,178), MinesProdQuarterly.zip (53,896,948), Mines.zip (7,291,228) all showed Last-Modified 'Fri, 07 Aug 2026 11:14:3x GMT'. Each dataset has a companion layout file (e.g. Violations_Definition_File.txt, Accidents_Definition_File.txt, Inspections_Definition_File.txt) — parse and store those too, because MSHA has changed column sets historically. The MSHA page itself carries a banner when a weekly update is postponed, so alert on Last-Modified not advancing rather than assuming the pull succeeded.

practices.practice: Migrate any PTAB code to the USPTO Open Data Portal — the old PTAB API v2 was decommissioned 6 January 2026
practices.detail: developer.uspto.gov now 301-redirects to data.uspto.gov. Verified: https://api.uspto.gov/api/v1/ptab/proceedings returns HTTP 403 {"message":"Missing Authentication Token"} without a key, and the patent-file-wrapper search returns 401. Authentication is a free API key sent in the X-API-Key header, obtained from the ODP Getting Started page. ODP 3.0 (released 21 Nov 2025) migrated all PTAB proceedings 1997-present and added 19 endpoints across trial proceedings (IPR/PGR/CBM/derivation), trial decisions (institution, final written, termination), trial documents, appeal decisions, and interference decisions.

practices.practice: Make the alerting tiered by latency class, and route the fast tier off-platform
practices.detail: Tier 1 (seconds-to-minutes, page the phone): Nasdaq tradehalts RSS matching an open position; EDGAR getcurrent Atom hit on your position list for forms 8-K (items 1.03, 2.04, 3.01, 5.02), 424B5, S-1, S-3, SC 13D. Tier 2 (daily, email digest at 18:30 ET): FINRA CNMS short-volume ratio moves, threshold-list additions/removals, borrow-fee changes >20% relative. Tier 3 (biweekly/weekly, dashboard only): FTD file publication, FINRA short interest publication, MSHA refresh. Deliver Tier 1 via a channel that does not depend on the pipeline being healthy.

practices.practice: Alert on staleness, not just on failure — a silently stale file is worse than a crash
practices.detail: Set an expected-freshness SLA per source and alert when Last-Modified stops advancing: CNMS short volume by 18:30 ET same trade date (FINRA commits to no later than 18:00 ET); threshold lists by 00:30 ET next day (Nasdaq posts by midnight of settlement day); FINRA short interest ~12 calendar days after settlement date; FTD ~15-16 days after the last settlement date in the file; MSHA by Saturday 12:00 ET. Also alert on shape: CNMSshvol20260812.txt had 12,199 lines and 536,691 bytes — a file that suddenly drops below ~8,000 rows is a partial publish, and ingesting it will corrupt your short-volume ratios.

practices.practice: Screen on cost-adjusted expected move, because per-share fees make sub-$1 names structurally untradeable
practices.detail: All the per-share charges (commission, TAF, NSCC/DTC clearing) scale with share count, not notional, so friction as a percentage of exposure is inversely proportional to price. Compute round-trip friction at signal time and reject any candidate where expected edge < 2x friction + expected borrow cost over the holding period. See costs — at $0.50/share IBKR Pro Tiered round-trip friction is ~1.52% of notional before any borrow fee, which alone exceeds the -1.08% median drift the repo's own FTD study measured.

practices.practice: Store the FINRA short-interest stockSplitFlag and revisionFlag as first-class corporate-action signals
practices.detail: Verified in shrt20260715.csv: stockSplitFlag='S' on 70 of 22,375 rows, revisionFlag='R' on 1. The 'S' flag is FINRA telling you the previousShortPositionQuantity is not comparable to currentShortPositionQuantity for that name — if you compute a short-interest delta across an 'S' row you manufacture a fake 90%+ change. Gate every period-over-period short-interest calculation on stockSplitFlag being blank, and treat 'R' rows as a new knowledge_date version of an existing observation_date rather than an update in place.

pitfalls.pitfall: Joining FTD data on settlement_date and treating it as available that day — the single biggest look-ahead error in this whole family of signals
pitfalls.mitigation: Measured: cnsfails202607a.zip covers settlements 2026-07-01..2026-07-14 and was published 2026-07-30 (Last-Modified Thu, 30 Jul 2026 12:02:36 GMT). Set knowledge_date = file Last-Modified for every row. Practical rule for live trading: on any date D you may only use FTD settlements up to roughly D-16, and rows as old as D-30. Encode this as a hard assertion in the feature builder, not a comment.

pitfalls.pitfall: Parsing the FTD text file straight into a dataframe and inheriting two trailer rows as garbage records
pitfalls.mitigation: Verified: cnsfails202607a.txt has 54,969 lines — 1 header, 54,966 data records, and 2 trailer lines reading 'Trailer record count 54966' and 'Trailer total quantity of shares 1946287678'. Strip lines that don't split into exactly 6 pipe-delimited fields, AND assert your parsed row count equals the trailer count and your summed QUANTITY equals the trailer total. That assertion is a free end-to-end integrity check on every file — use it.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming a missing cdn.finra.org file means the data isn't published yet
pitfalls.mitigation: cdn.finra.org returns 403 AccessDenied (not 404) for non-existent keys, so absence and forbidden are indistinguishable. Verified case: shrt20260731.csv returns 403 while POST https://api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/consolidatedShortInterest with compareFilters settlementDate EQUAL 2026-07-31 returns the full dataset. Query the API for the authoritative answer before firing a 'data missing' alert.

pitfalls.pitfall: Paginating EDGAR full-text search with arbitrary `from` offsets
pitfalls.mitigation: Verified: the API returns 100 hits per page and `from` must be a multiple of 100 — from=0 returned 100 hits, from=90 returned HTTP 500, from=9990 and from=10000 returned zero hits. Total is also hard-capped: a broad query reported {'value': 10000, 'relation': 'gte'}. Narrow by date window (and by forms) until relation=='eq' and value<10000, then paginate in steps of 100. If you don't check the relation field you will silently truncate at 10,000 and never know.

pitfalls.pitfall: Reverse splits silently destroying every trailing-window feature on exactly the names you care about
pitfalls.mitigation: $0.5-$5 Nasdaq names reverse-split constantly to cure the $1.00 minimum bid price rule, and the CUSIP changes with them. Verified: EDGAR FTS q=%22reverse stock split%22&forms=8-K returned 218 hits in the 13 days 2026-08-01..2026-08-13 alone. Detect via three independent channels — Nasdaq Equity Corporate Actions alerts (nasdaqtrader.com/TraderNews.aspx?id=ECA2026-nn), the FINRA stockSplitFlag='S', and an 8-K FTS sweep — and carry a split-adjustment factor plus the CUSIP linkage in your security master. Trailing chronic-fail-day counts and short-interest deltas must be computed on the linked entity, never on the raw CUSIP.

pitfalls.pitfall: Reading FINRA daily short volume as short interest, or as a directional signal at face value
pitfalls.mitigation: CNMSshvol files count media-reported off-exchange (TRF/ADF/ORF) volume only, and a large fraction of 'short' volume is market-maker hedging, not directional positioning. Verified header: Date|Symbol|ShortVolume|ShortExemptVolume|TotalVolume|Market, sample row '20260812|A|176188.159078|99|513690.199891|B,Q,N'. Note the volumes are fractional (fractional-share reporting), so parse as float not int, and note the Market field is a comma-joined set of venue codes inside a pipe-delimited file — a naive CSV parser with the wrong delimiter will mangle it.

pitfalls.pitfall: Treating threshold-list entry as a short entry signal when it is closer to a squeeze-risk flag
pitfalls.mitigation: Threshold status means fails ≥10,000 shares AND ≥0.5% of shares outstanding for 5 consecutive settlement days, which triggers mandatory close-out under Reg SHO 203(b)(3) — i.e. forced buying. For a negative-skew book, use threshold entry as a position-size reducer or a borrow-recall early warning, not as an add. Also note the 2026 threshold lists are heavily populated by leveraged single-stock ETFs (verified on both the Nasdaq and Cboe 2026-08-12 files), whose fails have nothing to do with issuer distress.

pitfalls.pitfall: Building the backtest with today's borrow fee and share availability
pitfalls.mitigation: Borrow on a $1 distressed name can move from 5% to 300% annualized in days, and availability goes to zero exactly when the signal is strongest. Start snapshotting the borrow file daily NOW even before the strategy is ready — you cannot retroactively reconstruct it, and no free historical source exists. Until you have 6+ months of snapshots, run the strategy paper-only or size it assuming the pessimistic end of the repo's own 25-55% breakeven range.

pitfalls.pitfall: Writing PTAB integration against developer.uspto.gov endpoints that no longer exist
pitfalls.mitigation: PTAB API v2 was decommissioned 6 January 2026; developer.uspto.gov 301-redirects to data.uspto.gov. Rewrite against https://api.uspto.gov/api/v1/ptab/... with an X-API-Key header. Budget for the rate limit — reported as 60 requests/minute per API key, and 4/minute for PDF and ZIP downloads (this figure comes from USPTO documentation via search; the canonical page https://data.uspto.gov/apis/api-rate-limits is a JavaScript SPA that could not be read server-side, so VERIFY IT YOURSELF in a browser before sizing your crawler).

pitfalls.pitfall: Expecting a free automated feed of Nasdaq corporate actions
pitfalls.mitigation: The Nasdaq Daily List (new listings, delistings, symbol changes, splits, Financial Status Indicator changes, history to 1999) is a commercial subscription product. Verified: guessed paths under /dynamic/symdir/dailylist/ (symbolchange_, symbolchanges_, nameChanges_, deletions_, additions_, dividends_ for 20260812) all returned HTTP 302 into a 404 page. Free substitutes that DO work: daily diffing of nasdaqtraded.txt for adds/drops/name changes, the ECA alert pages, and an EDGAR 8-K Item 3.01 / 5.03 sweep.

pitfalls.pitfall: Retrying aggressively on a 500 from efts.sec.gov and tripping the real rate limit
pitfalls.mitigation: Transient 500s are normal (1 in 15 in a rapid sequential test) and are NOT a rate-limit signal, but hammering retries will turn them into a 403 IP block, reported as roughly 10 minutes. Use exponential backoff with jitter starting at 1s, cap at 3 attempts, and keep the steady-state token bucket at ~6.7 rps against sec.gov.

pitfalls.pitfall: Alerting on filing text matches without a position filter, so the Tier-1 channel becomes noise and gets muted
pitfalls.mitigation: Verified volumes over the 13 days 2026-08-01..2026-08-13: 'going concern' in 10-Q = 753 hits, 'reverse stock split' in 8-K = 218, 'at-the-market' in 424B5 = 104. Page only on the intersection with (open positions ∪ watchlist); everything else goes to the daily digest. Rank the digest by |position notional| so the one that matters is at the top.

pitfalls.pitfall: Ignoring the 424B5 / ATM shelf signal, which is the specific mechanism that both caps and creates your tail
pitfalls.mitigation: An active at-the-market equity program is the short's ally (relentless supply) right up until the moment the issuer completes a raise and the overhang clears, or announces a deal that squeezes. Ingest 424B5 and S-3 filings for every position and track shelf capacity remaining. Verified endpoint: q=%22at-the-market%22&forms=424B5 over a 13-day window returned 104 hits — small enough to read every one for names you hold.

pitfalls.pitfall: Sizing equal-weight across a short book whose payoff is a small negative median against a fat positive tail
pitfalls.mitigation: This is a portfolio-construction failure that no data pipeline fixes, but the pipeline must feed it: the repo's own FTD panel shows 58% of observations down with a median of -1.08% but a MEAN of +1.56%, driven by 3.96% of cases squeezing more than +25%. Equal-weight turns that into a losing book. The pipeline's job is to deliver, at signal time, the three inputs that let you size against the tail: current borrow fee/availability, days-to-cover (verified available in FINRA short interest as daysToCoverQuantity — e.g. 2026-07-15: PLUG 6.91, CGC 5.98, BYND 4.38, SPCE 3.02), and float. Cap per-name risk on days-to-cover, and prefer defined-risk expressions where the tail is bounded.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming a ticker present in one dataset exists in the others
pitfalls.mitigation: Verified gap: of the five example names, PLUG, BYND, CGC and SPCE all appear in shrt20260715.csv but HYZN does not — it has left the consolidated exchange-listed universe. Build every cross-dataset join as an explicit LEFT JOIN with a coverage flag, and log unmatched symbols daily. A silent inner join here quietly deletes exactly the distressed names your strategy is about, which is survivorship bias injected at the SQL layer.

pitfalls.pitfall: Storing 27M+ FTD rows as CSV and re-scanning them on every feature build
