This settles whether the basis was ever capturable at the moment it was observable, and what the true executable spread and depth were in the small funds (the estimate I could not verify: 50-150bp round trip).
3. TRACE prints on the underlying bonds during 3/9-3/24/2020 versus the pricing-service marks used to strike NAV. This directly measures how much of the 'discount' was stale marking versus genuine liquidity premium — i.e. it partitions the 81-88% of five-day gap closure that came from NAV falling.
4. A survivorship-complete product universe: every US-listed fixed-income ETF and ETN alive on 2/28/2020, including those delisted, accelerated or liquidated afterwards, with premium/discount and terminal outcomes. Specifically verify the UBS ETRACS and Credit Suisse VelocityShares accelerations of March 2020 (flagged above as recall, unverified in this session — the web-search budget was exhausted). This quantifies the left tail the survivor-only sample cannot see.
5. Borrow/financing and repo cost on the short leg during the stress window, for any hedged implementation.

Reproduction artifacts for everything above: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WireAntennaGain/82dc742b-08fa-562e-9653-7f5ab2131e39/scratchpad/ (fetch.py, fetch2.py build px.pkl from Yahoo; basis.py and diag.py validate the same-share-class NAV reconstruction and date alignment; main.py through main5.py run the persistence, convergence-decomposition, pre-Fed counterfactual, 2008 out-of-sample, chronic-discount, buy-the-dip, retail-hedge, execution-gap and time-in-market tests).

redteam.target: Daily Short-Volume Reversal on FINRA CNMS daily short-sale volume (long low-relss / short high-relss), gated by SEC fails-to-deliver, motivated by Diether–Lee–Werner (2009, RFS 22:2). Evaluated against the analyst's own 27.5M-row SEC FTD panel (2004–2026) at /home/user/WireAntennaGain/research/data/ftd/, the prior referee swarm at /home/user/WireAntennaGain/research/data/referee/ftd-edge-referee-results.json, and the already-published retraction at /home/user/WireAntennaGain/research/ftd-empirical-findings.md.

kill_shots.attack: CITATION INVERSION — the load-bearing 'still alive in the public-data era' authority explicitly nulls the exact signal proposed. Wang, Yan & Zheng (JFE 2020, 135(1):191-212, 'Shorting flows, public disclosure, and market efficiency') is quoted selectively. Retrieved abstract: predictability pre-disclosure (2005-2007) was short-term; post-disclosure (2010-2015) 'LONG-TERM shorting flows are more informative than short-term shorting flows,' and — decisively — 'abnormal SHORT-TERM shorting flows do not predict future returns or anticipate bad news.' Short sellers 'shifted from trading on short-term private information to trading on long-term public information that is gradually incorporated into prices.' The proposed strategy is a daily (short-term) abnormal shorting-flow signal. The quoted sentence about predictability that 'decays slowly and lasts for a year' refers to the long-horizon accumulated flow measure, not the daily signal. The proponent's own flagship citation is a refutation, not a defense.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Only by abandoning the strategy. You could rebuild on long-horizon cumulative shorting flow, which is what WYZ says survives — but that is a different, slow-moving signal that converges on short interest, is already in every commercial risk model, and has none of the daily-file novelty that motivated this project. No rebuttal preserves the daily-rebalance design.

kill_shots.attack: THE DLW EFFECT IS SHORT-TERM REVERSAL IN DISGUISE, AND FF3 CANNOT SEE IT. From DLW's own abstract (verified primary text): 'Short sellers increase their trading following positive returns' and 'The results are consistent with short sellers trading on short-term OVERREACTION of stock prices.' So high-relss names are recent winners and low-relss names are recent losers by construction; Low-minus-High is mechanically long past losers and short past winners — that is the short-term reversal factor (Lehmann 1990; Jegadeesh 1990). The cited alphas are THREE-FACTOR alphas. FF3 contains no reversal factor and no momentum, so the one factor most likely to explain the entire result is the one absent from the control. Short-term reversal is not free money: Nagel (2012) shows it is the return to liquidity provision — compensation for bearing inventory risk, which is precisely the risk the strategy would be taking. Compounding the problem, the sample is a SINGLE YEAR (2005 SEC-mandated data), and t-statistics of 2.59-2.98 sit below the Harvey-Liu-Zhu (2016) t>3.0 hurdle for anomaly discovery in a multiple-testing world.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Partially. You can test it directly: re-run the sort with a short-term-reversal factor and momentum in the model, and double-sort on past 1-day and 1-week returns. If a relss alpha survives orthogonalization to STR, the attack fails. My prior is strongly that it does not, because DLW themselves name short-term overreaction as the mechanism. Even if some alpha survives, it is a liquidity-provision premium — a risk you are paid for, not an inefficiency — and it is the single most cost-sensitive anomaly known because it lives entirely inside the bid-ask spread.

kill_shots.attack: THE MODERN DATA IS A DIFFERENT ECONOMIC OBJECT AND THE SIGN MAY BE INVERTED. DLW measured exchange-executed short flow on NYSE/Nasdaq in 2005. FINRA confirms the CNMS file is the 'Consolidated TRF/ADF' file — it combines trades in exchange-listed securities reported to the Trade Reporting Facilities and the ADF, i.e. OFF-EXCHANGE volume only. Exchange short volume is published separately by each exchange and is NOT in this file. In today's internalized market a customer BUY filled by a wholesaler prints as a market-maker SHORT sale, so off-exchange short-volume ratio is substantially a measure of retail/institutional buying pressure, not bearish conviction. The analyst's own corpus documents this inversion (research/unorthodox-data-points-vol2.md:60): 'In dealer-intermediated dark venues a customer buy is printed as a market-maker short sale, so a high dark-pool short-volume ratio counterintuitively reveals passive institutional accumulation,' and SqueezeMetrics' DIX — built on this exact file — reports roughly +9.7% annualized forward S&P returns after HIGH short-volume-ratio readings. The strategy shorts high-relss names. If the DIX sign holds cross-sectionally, the strategy is systematically backwards. Market structure has also changed beyond recognition: DLW's shorts were 24% of NYSE and 31% of Nasdaq share volume in a pre-Reg NMS, pre-HFT, pre-mass-internalization market.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Yes, and this is the one genuinely worthwhile test in the whole project. Split short volume into its exchange leg (Nasdaq/NYSE/Cboe own files) and its off-exchange TRF leg and measure each separately. The exchange leg is the true analogue of DLW's variable. But note this abandons the 'one free file, no key' convenience that motivated the idea, and the two legs may well carry opposite signs — in which case the consolidated CNMS ratio the strategy actually uses is a blend of two offsetting effects and is close to uninformative by construction.

kill_shots.attack: FRICTIONS EXCEED THE GROSS EDGE ON THE ONLY UNIVERSE WITH CAPACITY — CONCEDED BY THE PROPONENT. Their own arithmetic: liquid universe gross expected edge is approximately 0.0%/month on WYZ's authority; even granting a generous post-decay 0.3-0.6%/month, cost is 0.9%/month at 5-day holds and ~2.8%/month at the daily rebalance the measured 30-35% decile persistence actually implies. Net: -0.5% to -2.5% per month. The measured 30-35% persistence is itself damning — it means ~65-70% one-way daily turnover, which is the turnover profile of a microstructure signal, not an information signal, and it is exactly what you would expect if the signal is short-term reversal. A strategy whose author computes a negative net expectancy and proposes trading it anyway has already lost the argument.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No. This is arithmetic on the proponent's own inputs, and every unverified input is biased in the strategy's favor: the 3-10bp half-spread is a guess the analyst explicitly could not source ('I could NOT verify a current authoritative per-market-cap figure'), it excludes market impact entirely, and it assumes fills at the midpoint of a quote you are crossing. Real all-in one-way cost for a 1,244-name book rebalanced daily would need to be under ~2bp for this to break even. That is below what the fastest professional execution achieves in non-S&P names.

kill_shots.attack: THE FTD GATE IS A STALE, LOW-RESOLUTION PROXY FOR BORROW FEE — WHICH IS OBSERVABLE LIVE AND ALREADY PRICED. Measured on the panel (2023-2026): MEDIAN FAIL NOTIONAL IS $12,170 per row (p75 $74,559). The gate fires on an economically trivial event and is a marker, not a flow. Verified Interactive Brokers borrow rates from the prior work (2026-08-12) rank-correlate with the alleged edge in the direction that destroys it: BYND 35.87%, CGC 12.30%, FBIO 8.27%, VUZI 2.98%, SPCE 2.76%, PLUG 0.52%. The cheap names that supposedly decline cost 12-36%/yr to borrow; the one cheap-to-borrow name sits where the edge is weakest and is not short-constrained at all, so the Miller (1977) / Boehme-Danielsen-Sorescu overvaluation mechanism that is supposed to generate the return does not even apply to it. Worse, the FTD state is disseminated FREE AND DAILY via the Reg SHO threshold list, and option-implied borrow fee from put-call parity (Muravyev, Pearson & Pollet, JF 2022) is real-time, continuous, and strictly dominates a binary gate that is stale by construction.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: No — this is the same conclusion the prior 26-agent referee swarm reached independently ('you did not discover an FTD anomaly, you rediscovered the securities-lending fee'). The only honest response is to drop the FTD gate and use borrow fee directly; but then you are trading a known, priced, and commercially available factor with no informational advantage, and the JF 2025 result applies: 162 anomalies go from +0.14%/mo gross to -0.01%/mo net of borrow, and are unprofitable even gross once the high-fee 12% of names is removed. This cohort IS that 12%.

kill_shots.attack: NEGATIVE SKEW IS FATAL AND THE EXPECTANCY IS NOT SIGN-IDENTIFIED. I measured the FTD-gated sub-$5 cohort's 1-month forward returns on the analyst's own panel (N=145,514): median -2.32%, 56.5% down — but MEAN +6.58%. A fixed-dollar short book earns the negative of the MEAN, so it loses ~79%/yr arithmetic before a single dollar of cost. The sign of expectancy flips on an arbitrary trimming choice affecting 0.32% of observations: trimming gross forward ratios above 4x gives the short +19.1%/yr, trimming above 10x gives -1.6%/yr, untrimmed gives -79.0%/yr. Geometric growth at 20% per-name sizing runs from +9.1%/yr (trim 1.5x) to -45.9%/yr (untrimmed). 1.07% of observations exceed +100% and 0.41% exceed +300%. The tail is also irreparably contaminated: the FTD file's price column is an UNADJUSTED prior-day close, and I measured that 0.41% of sub-$5 next-print observations jump more than 1.8x, 0.12% more than 4x, and 0.061% more than 9x — a 1-for-10 reverse split reads as +900%. Genuine squeezes (real, catastrophic losses) and reverse splits (neutral for an adjusted short) are inseparable in this data.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Only with data the project does not have. Split-adjusted prices with delisting returns from CRSP or a real market-data vendor would separate splits from squeezes and settle the sign of the mean. Until then, any strategy whose expectancy flips sign on a trimming parameter is not a strategy. Note that defined-risk puts genuinely do cap the tail — but that trade is unresolved because it needs options/IV data, and IV on these names is extraordinarily rich precisely because everyone knows about the skew, so you would be buying the insurance at the price the insurer charges.

kill_shots.attack: SELECTION AND SURVIVORSHIP — THE MEASUREMENT CONDITIONS ON A FUTURE EVENT, AND THIS EXACT BUG ALREADY MANUFACTURED A RETRACTED FINDING IN THIS PROJECT. Forward returns are computable only for names that REMAIN on the FTD file, and remaining is driven by renewed short pressure — a future event. The precedent is documented in research/ftd-empirical-findings.md: a gap filter that interacted with the treatment variable kept 2.3% of chronic-cohort rows versus 15.3% of control rows, and that differential selection produced the entire apparent effect (median -1.804% collapsed to +0.000% once corrected across 1,018,754 rows). I measured attrition directly on the chronic sub-$10 cohort at seven anchor dates: 16-28% absent from the file at the two-year mark, and permanent exit (never prints again) of 12-22% by 2 years and 26-46% by 4 years. I could NOT replicate the brief's '51% within ~2 years' — my permanent-exit figure is roughly half that — but the direction and the mechanism are confirmed. Exits are a mix of cash mergers (catastrophic for a short), reverse splits (fake +900% returns), and delistings to OTC (where a short can be bought in at ruinous prices or left stranded).
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Yes, mechanically: use a delisting-inclusive security master, assign proper CRSP delisting returns to the short leg, and retain halted and bankrupt names through their terminal return — which the project's own design notes already prescribe (ftd-deep-dive.md:224). This is fixable engineering. But fixing it can only make the measured edge smaller, never larger, because the current construction drops exactly the observations where the short leg blows up.

kill_shots.attack: CAPACITY AND CROWDING — A FREE 6PM FILE IS NOT AN INFORMATIONAL ADVANTAGE. The dataset is public, keyless, ~12,200 rows/day, posted by 6:00pm ET, and already consumed at scale: SqueezeMetrics publishes DIX free every evening from these exact files, open-source GitHub replications exist, and Fintel, Quiver and ChartExchange all ship derived short-volume dashboards to retail. Any signal computable from a free file within minutes of publication is arbitraged into the T+1 opening auction. On the liquid universe, 1,244 names carrying a reversal-type signal means capacity is bounded by the spread you pay as the marginal liquidity DEMANDER — the strategy is on the wrong side of the liquidity trade it is trying to harvest. On the FTD-gated microcap universe, capacity is a rounding error: median fail notional $12,170.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Weakly. A very small book (low six figures) genuinely does not compete for capacity, and crowding arguments are often overstated for retail size. But small size does not fix a negative gross expectancy, and it makes the fixed cost of the split-adjusted data needed to even measure the effect uneconomic relative to the dollars at stake.

kill_shots.attack: THE 'EDGE' IS A BUNDLE OF KNOWN, COMPENSATED RISK PREMIA. The FTD-gated universe is definitionally a portfolio of low price, high idiosyncratic volatility, financial distress, and expensive borrow — median price ~$1.93, dominated by busted-growth names. Shorting that basket is short the lottery-demand premium (Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw MAX), short the distress-risk premium (Campbell, Hilscher & Szilagyi), and short the securities-lending fee, while carrying a large negative-skew liability. Each of those is documented, each is a payment for bearing a risk somebody else does not want, and none of them is an inefficiency. The prior referee swarm independently reached the same conclusion and graded all twelve FTD-derived candidate strategies NO-EDGE or LIKELY-ILLUSORY.
kill_shots.rebuttal_possible: Partially — you can neutralize the exposures. Sector-, size-, and beta-neutralize; screen out the top borrow-fee decile; cap idiosyncratic vol. But every one of those neutralizations removes precisely the names carrying the alleged return, and the referee's verified borrow data shows the edge and the fee are rank-correlated, so hedging out the fee exposure should hedge out the edge with it. That is the test: if the signal survives a borrow-fee-neutral construction, it is real; the strong prior is that it does not survive.

redteam.survives:
No. The strategy does not survive in either of its two proposed forms, and it fails independently on several axes, any one of which is sufficient.

The liquid-universe version is dead on the proponent's own arithmetic: they compute gross edge ≈ 0.0%/month and net expectancy of -0.5% to -2.5%/month. There is nothing left to attack — the author has already killed it and is proposing to trade it anyway. The FTD-gated microcap version is dead because its expectancy is not sign-identified: on the project's own panel the median says short it (-2.32%) and the mean says do not (+6.58%, i.e. -79%/yr for a fixed-dollar short), and the sign flips on a trimming choice touching 0.32% of observations.

Underneath both sits a citation problem that should end the discussion on its own. Wang-Yan-Zheng (2020) — the single source invoked to establish the effect is alive in the public-data era — states that abnormal SHORT-TERM shorting flows do not predict future returns or anticipate bad news, and that only long-horizon flows remain informative. The strategy is a short-term shorting-flow signal. The quoted defense is a refutation.

For the strategy to work at all, ALL of the following must be true simultaneously:

1. The off-exchange TRF short-volume ratio must carry the DLW sign (high short volume → negative forward returns) rather than the DIX sign (high short volume → positive forward returns, reflecting internalized customer buying). These are opposite predictions from the same file. This is currently untested and is the single largest unknown.
2. The relss signal must produce alpha against a factor model that INCLUDES short-term reversal, momentum, size, illiquidity, idiosyncratic volatility, and a borrow-fee factor. Three-factor alphas are not evidence here, because DLW themselves identify short-term overreaction as the mechanism.
3. Whatever alpha survives (2) must exceed all-in one-way execution cost of roughly 2bp at daily rebalance or 10bp at a 5-day hold, inclusive of market impact, in non-S&P names. Nothing in the proponent's cost work suggests this is achievable.
4. For any microcap leg: prices must be split-adjusted with delisting returns applied, and the MEAN — not the median — must be negative after honest treatment of squeezes. On unadjusted FTD prices this is unknowable.
5. The signal must not be spanned by borrow fee. Given verified IB rates rank-correlate with the alleged edge (0.52% → 35.87% across the cohort), this is the least likely condition to hold.

My honest assessment of the joint probability: very low. Conditions 1 and 5 are each more likely false than true, and condition 3 is close to arithmetically impossible at the measured 30-35% signal persistence.

One caveat in the proponent's favor, stated plainly: I could not replicate the brief's claim that 51% of chronic names stop printing within ~2 years. My direct measurement gives 12-22% permanent exit at 2 years and 26-46% at 4 years. The survivorship attack is real and the mechanism is confirmed by the project's own retracted finding, but the specific magnitude in the brief is overstated by roughly a factor of two, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

The genuinely valuable residue — consistent with the project's own retraction — is a free NEGATIVE SCREEN: do not go long cheap, chronically-failing, expensive-to-borrow names. That is worth keeping and costs nothing. It is not a trade.
redteam.required_evidence:
One pre-specified test settles the whole question, and it requires data the project does not currently have.

DECISIVE TEST — the sign test on decomposed short volume:
Rebuild the panel on a point-in-time, SPLIT-ADJUSTED, DELISTING-INCLUSIVE security master (CRSP, or Polygon/Nasdaq Data Link with corporate actions). Then decompose daily short volume into (a) the exchange leg, from the Nasdaq/NYSE/Cboe individual short-volume files, and (b) the off-exchange leg, from FINRA CNMS. Sort separately on each. If the off-exchange leg carries the DIX sign (high relss → POSITIVE forward returns), the strategy as specified is backwards and must be abandoned or inverted. This single test costs a few days of work and is the highest-value experiment available, because it is the one thing nobody in the prior research actually measured.

CONFIRMATORY TESTS, in priority order:
1. FACTOR SPANNING. Regress the Low-minus-High portfolio return on FF5 + momentum + SHORT-TERM REVERSAL + a borrow-fee factor. Pre-register t>3.0 (Harvey-Liu-Zhu) as the survival threshold. If the alpha dies once STR is included, the effect was reversal all along and everything downstream is moot.
2. DOUBLE-SORT ON PAST RETURNS. Sort on relss within past-1-day and past-1-week return quintiles. If the relss spread vanishes within past-return buckets, the signal is a noisy proxy for reversal and adds nothing.
3. BORROW-FEE NEUTRALITY. Re-run within borrow-fee deciles. If the edge exists only in the top fee decile, you have rediscovered the lending fee and the JF 2025 result applies directly.
4. HONEST COST MODEL. Replace the unsourced 3-10bp half-spread guess with realized per-name effective half-spreads from TAQ or a broker TCA file, plus a square-root impact term at the actual intended notional. The proponent explicitly could not verify this figure; it is load-bearing for the entire net-edge claim.
5. MEAN, NOT MEDIAN, WITH A PRE-COMMITTED TRIM. On split-adjusted data, report the mean with the trimming rule fixed BEFORE looking at results, and report the geometric growth rate at the intended sizing — not the arithmetic mean, which no short book actually earns.

STOPPING RULE: if test (1) or the decisive sign test fails, stop. Do not proceed to execution research, options overlays, or sizing work — the prior 26-agent swarm already spent that effort on a signal that turned out to be the borrow fee.

playbooks.name: Do-Not-Own Screen: Reg SHO Threshold + Chronic-FTD Block (the only thing that survived)
playbooks.verdict: FUND NOW — ZERO RISK CAPITAL. This is the single item in the entire program that survived every referee and every red team, and it survived precisely because it is not a trade. No borrow, no squeeze exposure, no Rule 4210 charge, no buy-in risk, no fee to a lender, no unbounded left tail. Sell it internally as a risk control, never as alpha: its measured benefit (avoiding a roughly -1% two-week / -20% 21-day median in the flagged cohort) is real but sits inside the noise of most long books. Three independent referees converged on it and the red team did not attack it, because there is nothing to attack — declining to own something is free.
playbooks.universe: Every US-listed common stock, ADR or unit that is (a) currently held long, or (b) a candidate for a long, with a last sale under $20.00. HARD BLOCK below $5.00. REVIEW-AND-DOCUMENT flag $5.00–$20.00. No action above $20.00 (the price-band work measured the effect at 0.00% above $5 and the tradeable tail there is thin — do not spend attention on it). EXCLUDED from the screen entirely: ETPs, leveraged/inverse ETNs, warrants, rights, units. 34 of the 74 current Nasdaq threshold names are leveraged-ETP creation/redemption artifacts; flagging those is a false positive by construction and will destroy the screen's credibility with whoever has to obey it.
playbooks.signal: THREE FLAGS, all free, computed nightly. FLAG A (primary, zero lag): symbol appears on any SRO Reg SHO threshold securities list on any of the last 5 trading days. Nasdaq: https://www.nasdaqtrader.com/dynamic/symdir/regsho/nasdaqth{YYYYMMDD}.txt (pipe-delimited: Symbol|Security Name|Market Category|Reg SHO Threshold Flag|Rule 3210|Filler; 80 names on 2026-08-12, range 55–80 over the trailing month). NYSE and Cboe publish equivalents; FINRA OTC via POST https://api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/ThresholdList. Published daily by every venue, free, no lag. FLAG B (secondary, lagged): symbol appears in the SEC CNS fails file on >=63% of settlement dates over the trailing 6 PUBLISHED months. Source: https://www.sec.gov/files/data/fails-deliver-data/cnsfails{YYYYMM}{a|b}.zip, pipe-delimited SETTLEMENT DATE|CUSIP|SYMBOL|QUANTITY|DESCRIPTION|PRICE. MANDATORY: knowledge_date = the HTTP Last-Modified header, never the settlement date (cnsfails202607a covers settlements 07-01..07-14 and was published 07-30); strip the two trailer lines and assert your parsed record count and summed share quantity against them as a free end-to-end integrity check; join on CUSIP through a corporate-action-linked security master, never on raw ticker. FLAG C (context, not a block): your broker's live indicative borrow fee and shares-available. This is strictly better information than A or B and is free to any account holder — log it so that when A or B fires you can see whether the fee already said the same thing a month earlier.
playbooks.entry: There is no entry. The rule is a NON-entry, and it must live in the order path, not in a morning email. Pre-trade gateway check runs at 07:30 ET off the prior session's files. FLAG A true -> hard block on any new long AND scheduled exit of any existing long. FLAG B true alone -> hard block on new longs; an existing position requires a written PM override or is trimmed 50%. Every override is logged with a reason string. Order type is irrelevant because no order is placed — that is the entire point of the design.
playbooks.expression: No new instrument. Exits of already-held flagged names are done in SHARES with marketable limit orders worked over 2–5 sessions. Never market orders and never stops: Tier 2 LULD bands are 20% for $0.75–$3.00 names, a 5-minute pause means no stop executes at all, and the live halt feed on 2026-08-13 showed ~19 LULD pauses across ~9 symbols with one name (FGI) halting ~7 times in a single session. NEVER express this screen as a short. Everything that killed the short side — borrow at 756–1,074%/yr on the top threshold names, FINRA 4210's $2.50/share floor, Rule 204 buy-ins, the +596% BYND tail — is entirely absent when you simply decline to own.
playbooks.sizing: Target exposure to flagged names is 0% of the long book; hard cap 0% below $5.00, no exceptions. In the $5–$20 review band: aggregate flagged exposure capped at 2% of NAV, single name at 0.5% of NAV, each requiring a written override. Expect the screen to bind rarely — roughly 215 chronic sub-$5 names exist per settlement date and 55–80 sit on the Nasdaq threshold list on a given day — so if the long book is not in microcaps this will almost never fire. That low bind rate IS the honest measure of its value; do not inflate it.
playbooks.exit: A flagged name becomes re-eligible only after it has been absent from EVERY SRO threshold list for 20 consecutive trading days AND its trailing-6-published-month chronic-fail rate is under 25% AND its price is above $5.00. Re-eligibility is evaluated nightly by the system, never on request from whoever wants to buy it.
playbooks.stops: Not applicable — there is no position, therefore no stop. State this explicitly to anyone who asks for one, because the request is the first step back toward turning a screen into a trade. On this universe a stop is not a risk control: 20% LULD bands below $3.00, 5-minute pauses during which nothing executes, repeated intraday halts, and a buy-stop that becomes a market order into a reopening auction. Position sizing and the block itself are the only real controls available here.
playbooks.costs: Data: $0 (SEC, FINRA, Nasdaq, NYSE, Cboe are all free and keyless). Build: ~2–3 engineer-days for the pollers, on top of the security master that is needed anyway. Ongoing operation: ~10 minutes/day. ONE-TIME CLEANUP of legacy flagged longs is the only real cost: measured median quoted spread across the 36 current threshold common names is 4.28% (p75 6.41%, p90 16.98%) with median top-of-book depth of $820, so budget 1–3% of the flagged position value and work it over several days rather than crossing in one clip. Recurring cost thereafter: zero. Opportunity cost is genuine and should be stated up front — you will decline names that then run (HTZ printed +14.3% on the day it was sampled, on $195M of volume). That is a lottery premium you are choosing not to sell, and declining it is the correct decision for a long book.
playbooks.monitoring: (1) MONTHLY EFFICACY: forward 21-day and 63-day median return of the blocked cohort versus a price-, size- and sector-matched control, on split-adjusted prices with delisting returns applied. The screen's entire claim is that blocked names underperform; if that gap narrows to under 5pp on a rolling 24-month window, the screen has decayed into pure friction and should be retired rather than defended. (2) OVERRIDE RATE: if overrides exceed 10% of blocks, the screen is not being enforced and every number above is fiction. (3) COMPOSITION AUDIT: if the flagged list becomes majority leveraged-ETP artifact rather than distressed common, the signal has changed meaning post-Rule 204 and the exclusion set must be re-specified. (4) REGIME WATCH: the Nasdaq listing-rule tightening effective 2025-01-17 (suspension after 360 days rather than 540; immediate delisting determination with no grace period if a company falls below $1 within a year of a reverse split) is what makes the prior solid. If it loosens, re-measure before continuing to rely on the screen.
playbooks.first_test: HISTORICAL REPLAY, $0 capital, ~1 engineer-week. Take your own holdings history 2019–2026 (or, absent one, a Russell Microcap / Nasdaq sub-$5 constituent panel), apply Flags A and B with strict knowledge-date discipline, and compare forward 21-day and 63-day returns of flagged versus matched-unflagged holdings on SPLIT-ADJUSTED prices with delisting returns applied. PRE-REGISTERED SUCCESS CRITERION: flagged-name median forward 21-day return at least 5pp below the matched control, sign stable in at least 5 of 7 calendar years, and robust to dropping 2020–2021. The threshold-list referee measured -20.3% median 21-day with a 76% down rate on 879 daily lists; if a clean, split-adjusted, survivorship-honest replay does not reproduce at least half of that, do not wire the screen — write that down and move on. COMPLIANCE: none triggered. Public data, no position, no short sale, no MNPI. The only discipline required is the knowledge-date rule, which is research integrity rather than regulation.

playbooks.name: Borrow-Fee Horse Race — the one gated experiment, funded at $0 of risk capital
playbooks.verdict: FUND THE EXPERIMENT ONLY, WITH A SIGNED STOPPING RULE. NO CAPITAL IS AUTHORIZED BY THIS PLAYBOOK. My prior is that this fails and thereby closes the entire FTD / threshold-list / short-volume line of inquiry for the price of an afternoon — and that outcome is worth paying for, because the alternative is this program re-proposing the same signal every six months under a new name. Three referees independently reached the same diagnosis: the signal ranks names by how expensive they are to borrow, and the lender charges the entire spread. This experiment is designed to prove or disprove exactly that in one regression. Capital becomes discussable only if BOTH a statistical and an economic gate clear; I expect the first to fail.
playbooks.universe: THE TEST runs on the full split-adjusted US common-stock panel 2015–2026 — not a filtered cohort, because filtering is what manufactured every false positive in this program. THE CONDITIONAL TRADE, if the gates ever clear, would be confined to: US common stocks priced $2.50–$5.00 at signal (below $2.50 the FINRA 4210 $2.50/share floor makes return-on-capital hopeless — 250% of notional at $1.00, 500% at $0.50; above $5.00 the measured band edge is 0.00%), 20-day median dollar volume > $2M, listed options in a Penny Interval Program class (check the MIAX CSV — 356 classes on 2026-08-13), and a broker indicative borrow fee under 5%/yr with genuine availability. Note the tension that must be resolved before any capital moves: cheap borrow means no short constraint, which means the Miller (1977) overvaluation mechanism the thesis relies on does not apply in the only cell that is tradeable.
playbooks.signal: THE PRE-REGISTERED REGRESSION. Pooled cross-sectional regression of split-adjusted forward 10–24 calendar-day returns on chronic-FTD status (and, separately, threshold-list status) run ALONGSIDE, in the same specification: live borrow fee, shares-available, short interest as % of float, log price, log market cap, trailing 6-month share-count growth, 1-month reversal, 12-month momentum, idiosyncratic volatility, and a lottery/MAX term. Standard errors double-clustered by date and by name. The inference unit for any portfolio claim is the ~187 period returns, NOT the 264,834–1,008,493 overlapping rows (a chronic name prints nearly daily; ~168 overlapping rows per symbol inflates t-statistics by roughly sqrt(168)). DATA: SEC FTD knowledge-date stamped; SRO threshold lists; borrow fee from the broker SLB feed or IBKR's public file ftp://ftp3.interactivebrokers.com/usa.txt (user shortstock, blank password; SYM|CUR|NAME|CON|ISIN|REBATERATE|FEERATE|AVAILABLE) captured FORWARD daily if history is unpurchasable; prices from a split-adjusted vendor with delisting returns (CRSP / Polygon / Norgate / Sharadar) — never the FTD file's unadjusted price column, which is what made the expectancy sign unidentifiable (max observed 2-week 'return' +899,900%; sign flips on a trim touching <0.6% of rows).
playbooks.entry: STAGE-GATED; both gates written and signed BEFORE the first regression is run. GATE 1 (STATISTICAL): chronic-FTD/threshold status must retain |t| > 3.0 (Harvey–Liu–Zhu, not 2.0) on double-clustered errors after the full control set, AND the per-period equal-weight portfolio MEAN — not the pooled median — must carry the right sign with t > 2 on the 187-period series, AND the sign must be stable across trims from 1.8x to 25x. The red team measured that per-period mean at -0.170% gross, i.e. wrong-signed, so Gate 1 is a genuine hurdle and not a formality. GATE 2 (ECONOMIC): measured median edge in CENTS PER SHARE from a 20-session live NBBO capture on the specific candidate names must exceed 2x the measured effective spread in CENTS, per name. Percentage framing is banned at this gate — it is what produced the false price-band monotonicity (a near-constant 1–3 cent drift divided by a shrinking price). Only after both gates clear does a capital request get written. If a pilot ever trades: entry on a limit order posted ABOVE the NBB, worked over 2 sessions, never marketable and never IOC/ISO.
playbooks.expression: IF AND ONLY IF both gates clear: long-dated defined-risk PUTS, not short shares — penny-class listed puts, 45–75 DTE, strike placed AT the thesis drift target, sent as a single combo/BAG order at a net price via smart routing, never legged. Why not shares: FINRA 4210 demands the greater of $2.50/share or 100% of market value below $5; the left tail is unbounded (0.13% of two-week observations exceed +5x, which is -400% on a short); borrow is recallable without notice; and Rule 204 buy-ins land precisely inside the squeeze. Why the strike sits AT the target: a debit vertical sells away the crash, which is where a short-bias edge earns its money — verticals are correct only for a bounded-grind thesis, outrights for a genuine solvency thesis. THE CAVEAT THAT MUST APPEAR IN THE CAPITAL REQUEST: at 80–150% IV the option already prices a decline of roughly the size being forecast (at 130% IV the 90-day risk-neutral median is -18.8%), and measured crossing costs are 21% of premium on PLUG and 59% on CGC. Gate 2 must therefore be run on the OPTION chain, not just the share, before a dollar moves.
playbooks.sizing: ZERO until both gates clear. If they clear: maximum 1.0% of NAV of total premium at risk in the pilot, 0.15% of NAV per name, minimum 20–30 names (below 25 the idiosyncratic tail dominates; above 40 the marginal variance reduction is not worth the operational load). Hard caps: <=1.0% of shares outstanding, <=15% of 20-day median ADV, and <=25% of gross in any one squeeze cohort — cohort defined as the composite of short interest >20% of float, borrow fee >25%/yr, threshold-list appearance in the last 60 days, and message-board mention z-score >2, recomputed daily. Stress the book nightly against a uniform +98% adverse move (the Goldman most-shorted basket's actual three-month move into January 2021) and report that number alongside VaR.
playbooks.exit: The EXPERIMENT exits at the gate decision: publish the result either way and close the file. For a conditional pilot if one ever exists: close at the thesis horizon (10–24 calendar days, or at 21 DTE for options to stay off the gamma/theta cliff), or IMMEDIATELY on any of — name appears on any SRO threshold list (borrow supply is failing and buy-in risk is live), broker indicative borrow fee rises >3x in 5 sessions, or a reverse split or other corporate action is announced.
playbooks.stops: For the experiment, the stop IS the stopping rule: if Gate 1 fails, stop. Do not proceed to execution research, options overlays, sizing work, or a 'smaller version'; do not reopen without genuinely new data. This is the discipline that was missing when a prior 26-agent swarm spent its effort on a signal that turned out to be the securities-lending fee. For a pilot: defined risk is the premium paid, full stop. Do not use price stops on the underlying — on this universe a stop is not a stop (Tier 2 LULD bands of 20% below $3.00, 5-minute pauses in which nothing executes, repeated intraday halts). In simulation a +25% stop with a 25% gap-through assumption still produced a -31,443% worst case versus a hard -25% for the option-capped version. Only an owned long option is a floor; a name with no listed options has no floor and does not belong in the book.
playbooks.costs: THE EXPERIMENT: ~2 person-weeks of analyst/engineer time and $0 of data spend if borrow-fee history is captured forward rather than purchased. A split-adjusted price panel is the only defensible purchase and Playbook 1 needs it anyway. EXPLICITLY NOT AUTHORIZED: Ortex ($39–129/mo), S3/Markit, sec-api.io ($99–2,000/mo), ChartExchange or Fintel premium — each would be bought to accelerate a signal we have not yet shown is non-redundant with a free broker quote. THE HURDLE GATE 2 MUST BEAT for a pilot, per two-week round trip: 0.44–0.98% quoted spread at these prices (Rule 612 tick floor; realistically 1.5–3x wider in the illiquid tail) + 0.31–0.77% borrow at 8–20%/yr, computed on collateral marked up 102% and ROUNDED UP TO THE NEXT WHOLE DOLLAR (a $1.05 name carries a 1.90x multiplier, turning a quoted 40% into a true ~76% on notional; watch the cliffs at $0.9804, $1.9608, $2.9412, $3.9216, $4.9020) + 0.10–0.70% commission (per-share fees are catastrophic at low prices; IBKR's 1%-of-trade-value cap binds below ~$1) + 30–100bp per side of impact at 5% of ADV + 100% short-term ordinary-income tax on anything that survives. Total 1.2–2.5% per two weeks, i.e. 31–65% annualized at 26 turns.
playbooks.monitoring: For the experiment: version control and a signed pre-registration document; nothing else is needed. For a pilot if one ever runs — (1) rolling-50-trade MEDIAN trade return with a +0.40% tripwire, NEVER the mean (on a negatively skewed short book the rolling-50 mean's 5th percentile is -3.05% with the edge fully intact, so a mean-based rule false-alarms 5% of the time and needs thousands of trades to detect a true kill); (2) SPRT on trade signs, H0 p=0.64 vs H1 p=0.50, alarm at +2.77, clear at -1.56, ~35 trades to detection at 92.7% power; (3) adverse-tail CUSUM on excursions >20% of entry notional, alarm at 6 events in 20 trades; (4) EWMA on slippage-versus-arrival with 3-sigma limits (+21bp at 30bp per-trade sd); (5) daily read of the Nasdaq shorthalts SSR file and the threshold lists. DECAY-SPECIFIC KILL: regress realized P&L on contemporaneous borrow fee monthly and kill on a significant negative loading — that is the direct test of whether Muravyev–Pearson–Pollet (JF 2025: 162 anomalies, +0.14%/mo gross to -0.01%/mo net of borrow, unprofitable even gross once the high-fee 12% is removed) has swallowed the pilot. Set the drawdown kill near the bootstrapped intact p95–p99 of your own trade returns, not at a round 20% — at 10%-of-NAV positions over 250 trades a fully healthy version of this has a median max drawdown of 18.0% and a p90 of 32.6%, so a 20% kill fires on 40%+ of healthy runs.
playbooks.first_test: THE REGRESSION ABOVE IS THE FIRST TEST, and it is deliberately the cheapest experiment available: one afternoon of desk work against data already in the repository plus a split-adjusted price join. SUCCESS CRITERION: chronic-FTD/threshold status retains |t| > 3.0 after controlling for live borrow fee and the factor set, with the per-period portfolio mean correctly signed at t > 2 and sign-stable across 1.8x–25x trims. EXPECTED FAILURE: the coefficient collapses once borrow fee enters — in which case the finding is 'we rediscovered the securities-lending fee', the whole FTD/threshold/short-volume line closes permanently, and the twelve rejected candidates go into the research log as answered. COMPLIANCE, if a pilot ever runs: locate before every short sale (Rule 203(b)); Rule 201 makes short entry limit-only above the NBB for the trigger day AND the following day, and IOC/ISO shorts are silently CANCELLED rather than repriced while routing strategies silently stop routing — so reconcile intended versus actual fills intraday, not at EOD; blanket ban on participating in any follow-on offering in a name shorted within the prior 5 business days (Rule 105 of Reg M — no intent required, enforced mechanically, and this universe is full of serial ATM/shelf issuers); never structure a trade that requires holding a specific short across a specific date, because stock loans are callable without notice; and obtain the broker's current day-trading margin policy in writing, since the PDT repeal (SR-FINRA-2025-017, effective 2026-06-04) phases in through 2027-10-20 and firms implement on their own schedules — SEC investor.gov still publishes the old regime.

playbook.allocation:
HEADLINE, STATED PLAINLY: TWELVE CANDIDATES WENT IN AND ZERO EARNED CAPITAL. Eleven were graded NO-EDGE or LIKELY-ILLUSORY by independent referees; the red team confirmed with fatal, unrebutted attacks. I am writing two playbooks and neither of them is a trade: one is a free negative screen, one is a $0 experiment designed to close the file. If that reads as a disappointing return on the research spend, the alternative — funding one of these to keep morale up — would have cost real money. The program's actual output is a correctly answered question and a much better data pipeline.

WHAT TO FUND
- Playbook 1 (Do-Not-Own Screen): $0 risk capital, ~2–3 engineer-days plus ~1 engineer-week for the replay. Ship it as a pre-trade block in the order path.
- Playbook 2 (Borrow-Fee Horse Race): $0 risk capital, capped at 2 person-weeks, with a signed stopping rule. Its value is closing the inquiry, not opening a book.
- Everything else stays where it is: the existing long mandate and/or 3-month T-bills at 3.81%. That T-bill line is not a placeholder — it is the benchmark three of these candidates (XRT create-to-lend, the miner fade, the $5–20 threshold short) actively fail to beat.

WHAT NOT TO FUND — EXPLICITLY, WITH REASONS
1. CHRONIC-FAIL DECAY SHORT — KILL. The tradeable object's per-period equal-weight portfolio mean is -0.170% GROSS across 187 periods (already trimmed at 3x), before borrow, spread or commission. The edge is 1–3 CENTS per share against a $0.01 regulatory tick floor and realistic 2–5 cent spreads; the celebrated price-band monotonicity is a near-constant cents drift divided by a shrinking price, not economics. A fixed-dollar short earns the negative of the MEAN (+1.56%), which is arithmetic. Expectancy sign flips on a trim parameter touching <0.6% of rows because FTD prices are unadjusted for reverse splits.
2. REG SHO THRESHOLD-LIST SHORT — KILL. 8 of the market's top-20 borrow fees sit on a 74-name list at 756–1,074%/yr — a 31x concentration versus random. A 30-day hold costs 63–88% of notional in borrow alone against a 19–21% gross median. HTZ's 22-day ATM put costs 20.2% of spot against a 20.3% median 21-day decline: the options market has priced it to the basis point. ~0.92 tradeable names/day, t = 0.46 over 3.5 years.
3. FTD-CONFIRMED SHORT-CONSTRAINT L/S — KILL. The headline was reproduced exactly and then traced to the `BETWEEN 7 AND 35` gap filter in `research/data/ftd/analyze_patterns.py` (the `r_np` line), which retains 2.27% of chronic rows and conditions on a future event. Corrected, the mean flips from -0.47% to +1.08%/+7.29%. Borrow alone is ~2x the most favorable measured gross.
4. XRT CREATE-TO-LEND BORROW HARVEST — KILL, algebraically, no backtest required. A hedged lender earns rf − borrow×(1 − split×util), which is strictly less than rf for any positive borrow and any split below 100%. The factual premise is also inverted: XRT's actual fee is 1.07% with 500,000 shares freely available, and parity-implied borrow of 0.79–1.57% brackets it. The profitable version requires AP status.
5. BOND-ETF NAV-DISCOUNT CONVERGENCE — KILL. From the earliest ex-ante actionable entry (3/13/2020) to the last close before the SMCCF announcement, the PERFECTLY HEDGED basis was -1.72% and the unhedged trade -5.83% with a -7.68% mean worst mark. 100% of the profit lands after 3/23. Signal fires on 0.4% of fund-days, clustered into two calendar weeks in eighteen years, and has printed zero times below -1% at eight of nine funds since July 2020 — through 2022, March 2023 and April 2025. Retail cannot short NAV and cannot see the discount until it is gone (mean overnight gap 2.15–2.50% in the stress window exceeds the entire edge). 81–88% of the gap closed by NAV falling to price, not price rising to NAV. This is a bet on a central-bank reaction function wearing an arbitrage costume.
6. DAILY SHORT-VOLUME REVERSAL (+FTD GATE) — KILL, and possibly sign-inverted. Wang–Yan–Zheng (JFE 2020) state directly that abnormal SHORT-TERM shorting flows do not predict returns or anticipate bad news — the paper cited as the survival evidence is the refutation. CNMS is off-exchange only (~46.5% of consolidated volume), and an internalized retail BUY prints as a market-maker SHORT, so the ratio may proxy buying (the DIX reading). DLW's own arithmetic: 1.39%/mo gross versus 2.7%/mo cost, in 2005, on price>=$5 names.
7. MSHA 103(k) COAL TRIPWIRE — KILL. 3.09M-row census parsed, 324 events mapped: issue-day relative volume 0.87–1.12x, no abnormal volatility, 5-day drift +2.40% full sample (wrong sign for a short) and +0.07% post-2021. MSHA publishes weekly on Friday with a further 2–3 day entry lag; local press, the UMWA and IR all lead the file by days.
8. WAREHOUSE AMENDMENT WIRE — KILL. 0 of 62 warehouse Item-1.01 8-Ks were filed during market hours; 97% post-close. Event-day absolute move equals the unconditional baseline (PFSI 1.26% vs 1.23%; CACC 1.52% vs 1.34%). The sign is probably inverted — capacity cuts are borrower-initiated cost reductions on uncommitted lines. UWMC options quote 100–120% of mid with $0.50 strikes on a $1.50 stock; COOP is delisted.
9. IPR TRUCE TAPE — KILL. §317(b) requires the settlement agreement be filed before termination and Form 8-K Item 1.01 requires disclosure within four business days: the docket structurally cannot lead the press release. In the rare cases it does, the issuer has already determined the event immaterial — you are trading against their disclosure committee. IDCC's front-month ATM put is 45% of mid on 20 contracts of OI; ParkerVision trades ~$13,000/day.
10. PROXY-SOLICITOR FEE SIREN — KILL. Median fee $30k, p90 $60k, 64% dual-solicitor base rate, 37% TBD/success-fee language, and the PREM14A frequently leaves the number blank. The tradeable version of 'the vote is in trouble' is the DEFC14A form-type flag — free, earlier, unambiguous. You would also be shorting a documented ~4%/yr risk premium while short a free bump option (Alcon raised $28.00 to $30.75).
11. MINER CURTAILMENT LEDGER — KILL. The event no longer occurs: Riot's December 2025 print was its last monthly update, and there are no monthly production 8-Ks at MARA, CIFR or WULF in 2026. MARA's block count was exactly pre-observable on mempool.space (212+235+253 = 700, matching the disclosed 700). A 10% production miss is ~0.05% of market cap against 5.48% daily volatility, and the curtailment credits disclosed in the same release push the read the other way.
12. OVERNIGHT RETAIL FADE — KILL. It conditions on the news subsample where the literature predicts continuation, not reversal; the signal is defined on the opening print and must be executed at that print, and degrades sharply within one minute. Best published breakeven is 35–40bp round trip (S&P 500, 1998–2015) against realistic retail all-in of 40–90bp mid-cap and 100–250bp small-cap. NightShares closed in 14 months; the NY Fed documents the overnight drift at ~zero since January 2021.

ALSO NOT FUNDED
- $0 of data spend. No Ortex, S3/Markit, sec-api.io, ChartExchange/Fintel premium, iBorrowDesk paid tiers, Docket Alarm, or an ODP/P-TACTS pipeline. Every one would be purchased to accelerate a signal not yet shown to be non-redundant with a free broker borrow quote. Everything these playbooks need is free: SEC FTD, FINRA CDN and API, the SRO threshold and SSR files, Cboe delayed chains, MIAX penny-class CSVs, EDGAR FTS, mempool.space, MSHA.
- $0 to options overlays as a rescue for any short thesis. Measured: 36-day put crossing costs 21% of premium on PLUG and 59% on CGC; a PLUG 2.50/2.00 vertical's sum-of-touch is 17.9% of the debit; nickel-class names run 3–5x the penny-class width. The option is not the escape hatch — it is where the borrow fee is resold to you with a variance margin on top.
- $0 to a retail fully-paid securities-lending program run AS A STRATEGY. Buying shares in order to lend them and hedging is algebraically worse than T-bills. Enrolling non-dividend-paying shares you already hold for independent reasons is permitted as an opportunistic 13–32bp, but it is not a line item, and the two forgotten costs must be on the record: loaned shares are NOT SIPC-covered, and dividends arrive as non-qualified payments in lieu.
- $0 to the 'long-horizon accumulated shorting flow' thread, the one variant Wang–Yan–Zheng left alive. It is a proxy for short interest, it is sold by at least four vendors, and it is a low-turnover liquid-name factor business — a different firm than this one.

THE ONE THING WORTH REAL ENGINEERING IS NOT A SIGNAL. Every decisive error in this program was data plumbing, not modelling: the line-46 lookahead, the unadjusted reverse-split tail that made the expectancy sign unidentifiable, the differential survivorship in a 'matched' control (98.9% of chronic rows had a forward price versus 71.7% of control rows), and the settlement-date-versus-publication-date join. Fund the point-in-time security master. Note also that the existing retraction in the repo (commit c966038) is itself defective — it 'corrected' the forward return to the next FTD print, but chronic names print nearly daily, so it measured one-day returns and unsurprisingly got 0.000%. A wrong retraction in the log is as dangerous as a wrong finding; fix the record.
build_order: FREEZE ALL SHORT-SIDE CAPITAL DEPLOYMENT TODAY. Write the twelve kills into the research log with their one-line reasons and the specific measurement that decided each, so none of them can be re-proposed under a new name in six months. This costs nothing and is the single highest-value action in the list.

CORRECT THE EXISTING RECORD BEFORE BUILDING ANYTHING NEW. The repo's retraction (commit c966038) measured one-day returns because chronic names print in the FTD file nearly daily (median gap = 1 day), so it retracted a real statistical pattern for the wrong reason. Restate it accurately: the pattern reproduces on a calendar-matched 10-24 day horizon, and what kills it is the cents-versus-tick arithmetic, the negative per-period portfolio mean, and the unidentifiable sign — not a zero result. A wrong retraction is as dangerous as a wrong finding.

BUILD THE POINT-IN-TIME SECURITY MASTER FIRST — nothing downstream is decidable without it. Requirements: CUSIP-to-ticker linkage that survives corporate actions, split and dividend adjustment factors, delisting returns, and a knowledge_date stamped on every row. Detect reverse splits through three independent channels (Nasdaq Equity Corporate Actions alerts, the FINRA stockSplitFlag='S', and an EDGAR full-text 8-K sweep — 218 hits in the 13 days to 2026-08-13 alone). Compute every trailing feature on the linked entity, never on the raw CUSIP.

WIRE THE FREE DAILY POLLERS with integrity assertions baked in, not bolted on. SRO threshold lists (Nasdaq/NYSE/Cboe) plus the FINRA OTC ThresholdList API; the Nasdaq shorthalts SSR file; the SEC FTD semi-monthly zips with knowledge_date = HTTP Last-Modified and hard assertions that the parsed record count and summed share quantity match the two trailer lines. Remember cdn.finra.org returns 403 rather than 404 for missing keys, so query the FINRA API before firing any 'data missing' alert, and paginate EDGAR full-text search only in multiples of 100 while checking the total-hits relation field for the 10,000 cap.

SHIP PLAYBOOK 1 AS A PRE-TRADE BLOCK IN THE ORDER PATH — not a morning report, not a dashboard. If it can be skipped manually it will be, and then its measured benefit is fiction. Log every override with a reason string and review the override rate monthly.

RUN PLAYBOOK 1'S HISTORICAL REPLAY against the pre-registered criterion (flagged-cohort median forward 21-day return at least 5pp below a matched control, sign stable in 5 of 7 years, robust to dropping 2020-2021). Keep or retire the screen on that number alone. Do not adjust the criterion after seeing the result.

RUN PLAYBOOK 2'S HORSE RACE with the two gates signed in advance and a written stopping rule. Publish the outcome either way. My expectation is that the chronic-FTD coefficient collapses the moment live borrow fee enters the specification, which closes the entire line of inquiry for two person-weeks — the cheapest decisive experiment available anywhere in this program.

ONLY IF GATE 1 CLEARS: run Gate 2 — a 20-session live NBBO and option-chain capture measuring edge in CENTS against effective spread in CENTS, per name, on both the share and the put. Ban percentage framing at this gate; it is what produced the false price-band monotonicity. Stop again if edge is under 2x spread.

INSTALL THE MONITORING AND KILL-SWITCH INFRASTRUCTURE BEFORE ANY CAPITAL EVER GOES ON, NOT AFTER: rolling-50-trade median tripwire at +0.40% (never the mean), SPRT on trade signs with alarm at +2.77, adverse-tail CUSUM on >20% excursions, EWMA cost-drift control limits, and a drawdown kill set at the bootstrapped intact p95-p99 of your own trade returns rather than a round number. A strategy without a pre-built kill switch is a strategy that will be argued about while it loses money.

REDIRECT THE RESEARCH TEAM AWAY FROM ANY IDEA WHOSE PAYOFF IS A RENT SOMEONE ELSE IS ALREADY COLLECTING. The unifying lesson across all twelve: in every case the money went to the securities lender, the options market maker, or the wholesaler, and the 'anomaly' was the price of a service being sold in a competitive market. Before the next brief is written, require it to answer one question on the first page — who is paying, and why are they wrong? If the answer is 'a lender who bears no directional risk and marks daily', there is no trade.

verdictSummary.strategy: Chronic-Fail Decay: systematically short (or avoid) cheap single names that appear on >=11 of the last ~13 semi-monthly SEC FTD prints, sized by price band, held ~2 weeks. Universe ~650-730 names/print, median price ~$1.93, dominated by optionable busted-growth names (PLUG, BYND, CGC, SPCE, HYZN, GETY, VUZI, LAES, VFS, FBIO).
verdictSummary.verdict: NO-EDGE (as a short strategy). The statistical pattern is real and was published a decade ago; the exploitable net-of-cost expectancy is negative with high confidence. The only surviving use is as a free long-side negative screen.
verdictSummary.confidence:
HIGH that no exploitable short edge exists; MEDIUM-HIGH on the precise magnitude of the loss.

Reasons for high confidence: (1) The two decisive numbers come from the commissioning analyst's own data, not from my research — a +1.56% mean and a -0.21% lag-honest median. A fixed-dollar short earns the negative of the mean; that is arithmetic, not opinion, and it means the strategy has negative expectancy BEFORE any cost I researched. (2) The spread floor is a regulatory constant (SEC Rule 612: $0.01 above $1.00, $0.005 only for demonstrably tight names) and at a $1.93 median price it is 0.52% per round trip, more than double the honest signal. (3) Borrow rates are verified primary-source observations from Interactive Brokers for six of the ten named chronic stocks, and they are inversely aligned with the edge in exactly the way Muravyev-Pearson-Pollet predict. (4) The result is already published (Stratmann & Welborn 2016, same dataset), already factor-spanned (Drechsler CME factor, Bali MAX, Asness QMJ), already commercialized by multiple vendors, and the underlying state is disseminated free and daily via the Reg SHO threshold list. (5) The JF 2025 paper is a direct, out-of-sample, general refutation: 162 anomalies go from +0.14%/mo gross to -0.01%/mo net of borrow, and are unprofitable even gross once the high-fee 12% is removed. This strategy is entirely inside that high-fee 12%. (6) Three independent kill mechanisms — negative gross mean, cost floor exceeding the signal, and the edge being the borrow fee itself — each sufficient alone; all three would have to be wrong simultaneously.

Reasons the magnitude estimate is only medium-high: I could not obtain live NBBO spreads (used tick-size floors, which understate cost), could not obtain historical or cohort-wide borrow distributions (six point observations plus literature deciles), could not verify BYND's current short-interest percentage of float (source returned 403), and the 234% IV figure is single-sourced. Every one of these gaps, if resolved, makes the trade WORSE, not better — my estimate is biased in the strategy's favor and it still fails.

The single most important thing I would tell the analyst: you did not discover an FTD anomaly, you rediscovered the securities-lending fee. The signal ranks names by how expensive they are to borrow, and the lender charges you the entire spread. If you want to test whether anything is left, do not run a short book — measure the MEAN (not the median) of the market-neutral chronic-minus-fresh spread, and regress the chronic-minus-fresh return on the contemporaneous borrow fee. If the alpha vanishes when you control for the fee, which I expect, the question is closed.

verdictSummary.strategy: Reg SHO Threshold-List Overvaluation Reversal — short (or buy puts on) names newly added to / persisting on SRO Reg SHO threshold lists, per Autore, Boulton & Braga-Alves (2015), Financial Review 50(2), 143-172.
verdictSummary.confidence:
HIGH that there is no exploitable net edge for a small trader or small fund. Medium-high on the precise magnitude of the gross pattern.

WHY HIGH: the conclusion does not rest on the return estimate at all. It rests on two independently verified facts that cannot be argued around. First, 8 of the 20 highest-borrow-fee stocks in the entire US market sit on today's 74-name threshold list at 756-1,074%/yr — a 31x concentration versus random — which means a 30-day hold costs 63-88% of notional against a 19-21% gross median. Second, the most liquid optionable name on the list, HTZ, prices a 22-day ATM put at 20.2% of spot against a 20.3% median 21-day decline, i.e. the options market has already fully priced the effect. Both are direct measurements from live market data taken today, not estimates. Additionally the paper's own authors state the mispricing "is likely to be difficult to arbitrage because of extreme shorting costs" — they never claimed it was tradeable.

WHY NOT HIGHER ON THE GROSS MAGNITUDE — things I could NOT verify, stated plainly:
- The IBKR borrow fees came from chartexchange's screener with NO visible timestamp. I could not reach IBKR's own securities-lending file from this environment (both the FTP and https endpoints returned nothing). The 8/20 overlap is so extreme it is robust to staleness, but treat the individual percentages as indicative rather than executable quotes.
- Cboe quotes were captured after the close (last trade 2026-08-12 16:00), so spreads may be wider than mid-session. I have flagged them as an upper bound; intraday spreads on the common names are likely somewhat tighter than the 4.28% median.
- Put-call-parity implied borrow assumes European-style parity on American options with no dividends. Early exercise on hard-to-borrow names biases this; treat 25-88%/yr as an order-of-magnitude estimate.
- I used ONLY the Nasdaq threshold list. NYSE, Cboe and the FINRA OTC lists are not included; the OTC list in particular is larger and would be strictly worse on every friction.
- I have no shares-outstanding data, so I could not reconstruct threshold membership before 2023-01-03. The 3.5-year window covers 879 trading days and ~47 independent monthly observations — adequate but not long.
- Prices are the FTD file's embedded prior-day closes, unadjusted for splits. I applied a +/-70% one-day guard at entry, but reverse splits inside the forward window remain and bias short returns DOWNWARD (making my gross figures conservative).
- Returns condition on the name reappearing in the FTD file later. Delistings-to-zero drop out, which biases short returns DOWNWARD too. So the true gross is if anything better than I report — and the net conclusion is unaffected, because the borrow fee is 3x the gross either way.

RECOMMENDATION: reject as a trade. Adopt the on-threshold-list flag as a free do-not-own screen alongside the existing chronic-FTD filter, and route the research effort elsewhere. If anyone wants exposure to this phenomenon, the economically correct expression is to be the LENDER, not the short — but that requires a prime brokerage balance sheet, not a trading account.

verdictSummary.strategy: FTD-Confirmed Short-Constraint Long-Short — use SEC fails-to-deliver (chronic-persistence + low-price pattern) as a confirming filter on a high-borrow-fee / high-utilization / high-days-to-cover short-constraint anomaly, traded by a small trader or small fund.
verdictSummary.confidence:
HIGH — unusually so, because this rests on a reproduced computational finding rather than only on judgment.

What makes it high:
(1) I reproduced the analyst's headline number EXACTLY from their own code and data (N=23,203, median -1.8036%, mean -0.4719%, 58.26% down vs the reported N=23,203, -1.80%, -0.47%, 58.3%), then isolated the mechanism: the 7-35 day gap filter on line 46 of analyze_patterns.py retains 2.27% of chronic rows and conditions on a future event. This is a verifiable, deterministic fact about the pipeline, not an opinion.
(2) The corrected result reverses the tradeable statistic: the mean flips from -0.47% to +1.08% (unbiased next-observation) and +7.29% (horizon-matched), meaning an equal-weight short loses gross.
(3) The cost arithmetic is dominant and robust to every input: borrow fee alone at a mid-range HTB rate is ~2x the most favorably measured gross edge. Nothing about the signal's refinement changes that ordering.
(4) A December 2025 Journal of Finance paper measures the entire anomaly class at -0.01%/month net of borrow fees, with the alpha concentrated in exactly the high-fee subset this strategy targets — independent top-down confirmation of my bottom-up stack.

Where I am LESS certain, stated plainly:
- I could not verify the exact borrow fee on any specific chronic-fail name on any specific date. I have no historical borrow-fee panel. The 30-100% range is inferred from documented public examples (BYND 152.1%, LMNL 80.4%, HEAR 45.1%) and IBKR's own statement that the least liquid shares exceed 100% annualized. I did not fabricate a name-level fee.
- My spread estimates are anchored on the mechanical $0.01 tick floor plus published small-cap spread ranges, not on quote-level microcap TAQ data, which I do not have.
- I could not retrieve the Muravyev/Pearson/Pollet or Drechsler PDFs directly (403 / corrupted binary); I relied on the RePEc abstract page, the publisher listing, and search summaries. The headline figures (0.14% -> -0.01%/month, 162 anomalies, 12% of stock-dates; Drechsler 1.31% gross / 0.78% net) appeared consistently across independent sources, but I did not read the full texts.
- The true gross expectancy remains genuinely unknowable from this dataset because of unadjusted prices in the tail. I have flagged this rather than resolved it.

None of these gaps can rescue the trade: they affect the size of a negative number, not its sign.

ONE THING WORTH SALVAGING: the free negative screen. "Do not go long a sub-$5 stock that fails on most trading days" survives my correction (median -2.02%/-1.35% in the cheapest bands, monotonic dose-response, n>1M) and costs nothing to apply, so no friction can eat it. That is a real, if modest, risk-management rule — and it is the honest residue of this research.
